basis: Source review plus runtime probe at the frozen SHA (f5c89e5c): CVE-2026-12151's carrier is many small or empty CONTINUATION frames accumulating in the receiver's fragment list. At v5.19.0 lib/websocket/receiver.js sets `#info.fragmented = !fin && opcode !== CONTINUATION` (line 67), so for every continuation frame that flag is false and the delivery branch (lines 230-236) runs: the frame is delivered via websocketMessageReceived and the list is cleared with `#fragments.length = 0`. Cross-frame accumulation is therefore impossible; only consecutive FIN=0 TEXT/BINARY frames grow the list. Runtime confirms it: 200k and 400k continuation frames produced 200000 and 400000 client messages with a flat +0.9 MB heap on both counts, while v6.26.0 with the same input produced 0 messages and +22.6 / +45.0 MB (~118 B per frame). The accumulating parser is commit 38c8b55c (#3247), first released in v6.17.0; the measured boundary is v6.16.1 (200000 messages, +0.9 MB) versus v6.17.0 (0 messages, +22.7 MB), and none of the three fixes (32dbf0b3/8cb10f98/b7f252e7) is contained in any v5.* tag. The ranges that do cover 5.19.0 (cvelistV5 `0 < 6.26.0`, OSV-GHSA `introduced 0`) are coarse back-fills contradicted by the advisory's own prose ("All releases starting at undici 6.17.0 are affected") and by GHSA/NVD (`6.17.0 < 6.27.0`). The same advisory is also internally wrong about the 6.x fix (cvelistV5 marks 6.26.0 unaffected and its prose says `>= 6.26.0`, but maxFragments first appears in 6.27.0 and 6.26.0 still accumulates).
notes: Round78 exclusion (runs/verification/undici_v5.19.0_CVE-2026-12151/NOT_APPLICABLE.md; 15 local probe runs in probe_run.txt, env in env.json). Recorded caveat: repeated FIN=0 TEXT frames DO accumulate unboundedly at v5.19.0 (+45.0 MB at 400k) and are rejected from v6.17.0 (expected continuation frame); that is a different, unassigned shape and is NOT counted as this CVE. notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, reviewer round79-undici-independent-reviewer, packet runs/independent/undici_v5.19.0_CVE-2026-6733_round79/). The reviewer built its own non-shallow clone and its own same-tick harness (not the collector's repro) and made request 2 receive an injected 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' head on a reused idle keep-alive socket in 30/30 runs at v5.19.0; a no-injection control and an idle-then-dispatch control on a second connection both returned request 2's own response 10/10, so reuse is not being forced by the harness. The same harness is clean at v6.27.0 (0/10) and v7.28.0 (0/25) and racy at v8.5.0 (2/25); v6.26.0, v7.27.0 and v8.4.0 poison 10/10, so the first fixed 6.x release is 6.27.0 even though the cvelistV5/NVD prose says 6.26.0, and GHSA/OSV's machine range agrees with 6.27.0. Source inspection confirms lib/client.js:680-706 binds a parsed head to client[kQueue][client[kRunningIdx]] after only a socket.destroyed and a slot-existence test, and onMessageComplete:828-896 advances kRunningIdx (871) and defers the pipelining-1 write with setImmediate (892). The reviewer records three further disagreements that do not change this snapshot: the advertised keepAliveTimeout: 0 workaround throws InvalidArgumentError on every version tested; the 'add the client[kRunning] === 0 guard' description is necessary but not sufficient (a v5.19.0 build with only the guards still poisons 20/20 — the resumeH1 reordering that drains buffered bytes before writing is load-bearing); and upstream's test/response-queue-poisoning.js passes on unfixed tags too, so it is non-discriminating. Later releases regress (reviewer-measured 15/15 poisoned at v6.29.1, v7.30.0 and v8.12.3; the perf backports 3866a3bc / f57411b8 / 8c9182eb are contained in those tags). The v5 line has no fix at all; 5.29.0 still poisons 10/10.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2026-27205; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round43 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed on the 3.1 line in 3.1.3 (089cb86d / c17f3793) by moving session-access tracking into RequestContext.session; that commit is absent from 2.3.1, 2.3.3 and 3.1.2.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). Flask writes ``Vary: Cookie`` from SessionInterface.save_session so that a shared cache keys session-dependent responses on the session cookie. At 2.3.1 that header is gated on SecureCookieSession.accessed, and the flag is set in exactly four places in src/flask/sessions.py: __getitem__ (71-73), get (77), setdefault and on_update (82-87). The plain dict operations that CallbackDict inherits are not overridden, so ``'k' in session``, ``len(session)`` and iteration (and .keys()/.values()/.items(), which route through CallbackDict.__iter__) read the session without ever setting accessed. Because flask.session and the Jinja ``session`` both resolve to the same SecureCookieSession object at this tag, a template that only tests ``{% if 'user' in session %}`` has the same blind spot. save_session (322-350) then skips the Vary gate at 347-349 whenever accessed is false, so the response carries no Vary and a caching proxy that does not ignore Set-Cookie responses can serve one user's rendered page to another. A second, snapshot-specific manifestation exists at this tag only: save_session returns early at 334 (``if not session: return True``) before reaching the gate, so even a value read on an empty session produces no Vary; 2.3.3 and 3.1.2 already evaluate the gate before that return and do emit Vary. The fix moves the tracking to RequestContext.session (3.1.3 ctx.py: the backing _session at 327 and the property at 368-375, which sets accessed on resolution), drops the four per-method assignments and the Vary guard's dependence on them (sessions.py 348-354), stops replacing the session proxy in the Jinja context (templating.py 35-36) so template lookups go through the tracked property, and saves from ctx._session (app.py 1321-1322) so the save itself does not count as an access. Fixed on the 3.1 line by 089cb86d (first release 3.1.3, PyPI 2026-02-19T05:00:56Z). 089cb86d is a merge commit; its second parent c17f3793 ('request context tracks session access') carries the actual diff, the merge tree equals c17f3793's tree, and commit/<sha>.patch returns the c17f3793 patch. It is an ancestor of tag 3.1.3 only, absent from 2.3.1, 2.3.3 and 3.1.2; sessions.py is byte-identical at 2.3.1 (912d178b...) and 2.3.3 (ac51f640...), so no 2.3 release can repair this by upgrading within the line. Repro evidence: the round43 reviewer installed genuine flask 2.3.1, 2.3.3, 3.1.2 and 3.1.3 from PyPI into four preserved venvs (sessions.py at 2.3.1 sha256 912d178b..., at 3.1.3 7b2c11aa..., equal to the tag files) and drove 64 red/green rows over 8 access routes (/in, /len, /iter, /get, /getitem, /setdefault, /nothing, /tmpl_in) x 4 versions x 2 modes (empty session, after login), with 0 mismatches against the expected Vary/result matrix. On 2.3.1, 2.3.3 and 3.1.2 the key-only routes emit no Vary while .get/.getitem/.setdefault do; only 3.1.3 emits Vary on every route. The reviewer also ran nginx 1.24.0 with proxy_cache (honouring but not ignoring Set-Cookie): on 2.3.1, logging in and then requesting as an anonymous client gave MISS then HIT, and the anonymous user received the logged-in response (result=yes, session_len=1) with no Vary in either response; the reverse order served the logged-in user result=null instead of alice. On 3.1.3 the same sequence was MISS then MISS with Vary: Cookie both times. Caveats: the empty-session early return at 334 is a snapshot-specific manifestation of the same missing-Vary outcome, judged NOT part of this CVE and not repaired by the fix diff, so the verdict does not depend on it; exposure requires Flask served behind a cache that stores responses carrying Set-Cookie (the docs' own guidance is to ignore it), so deployments whose cache ignores Set-Cookie are not affected. Public records agree: one PyPI range 0 -> 3.1.3, CWE-524, NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 4.3 MEDIUM / Secondary CVSS 4.0 2.3 LOW, and publication order PyPI 3.1.3 (2026-02-19T05:00:56Z) -> GHSA (20:45:41Z) -> OSV CVE (2026-02-21T05:21:17Z) -> NVD/PYSEC (06:17Z). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2024-49767; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round44 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. The snapshot 3.0.2 is inside >= 2.0.0rc1, < 3.0.6; the fix lands in 3.0.6 (50cfeebc / 8760275a) and is absent from 3.0.2 and 3.0.5.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). Werkzeug's multipart parser reads the request body in ``buffer_size`` chunks (64 KiB by default) through ``_chunk_iter`` and forwards each chunk to ``MultipartDecoder.receive_data``. The only enforcement of ``max_form_memory_size`` lives there, and it compares ``len(self.buffer) + len(data)`` against the limit -- one chunk, not one field. ``MultiPartParser.parse`` (src/werkzeug/formparser.py:353-392) drains the decoder after every chunk, so the buffer is empty each round, and for a non-file part it appends every ``Data`` event to a plain list at 381-382 with no accumulated accounting, then joins and decodes the whole list at 384-386. A field larger than the limit delivered in chunks smaller than the limit therefore passes every per-chunk check and is buffered in full. The fix merge 50cfeebc ('Merge commit from fork'; second parent 8760275a, 'apply max_form_memory_size another level up in the parser'; merge tree equals the second parent's, commit/<sha>.patch returns the 8760275a patch) declares field_size at 355, resets it to 0 for a Field at 374 and to None for a File at 379, accumulates each Data event at 386 and raises RequestEntityTooLarge at 388-389 once the accumulated field passes the limit; sansio/multipart.py keeps its per-chunk check and only gains explanatory comments. The fix is an ancestor of 3.0.6 (tag object a82e04ed -> 5eaefc39) and absent from 3.0.2 and 3.0.5. 3.0.5 is the last 3.0 release without it: its Data branch still appends bare at 380 and sansio/multipart.py is byte-identical to 3.0.2. The shape arrived with the sans-io refactor cbb446fd ('Refactor the Multipart parsing into a Sans-IO layer', 2021-01-20), which the GHSA references; that commit is an ancestor of 22bfb446 ('Release 2.0.0rc1'), matching the 2.0.0rc1 lower bound of the published ranges. Repro evidence: the round44 reviewer installed genuine werkzeug 3.0.2 and 3.0.6 from PyPI into two preserved venvs, with installed formparser.py / sansio/multipart.py sha256 matching the tag files (5411abb1... / bbf5cbb3... at 3.0.2; 9a4acff2... / 7cc1a063... at 3.0.6). With MultiPartParser(max_form_memory_size=1 MiB, buffer_size=64 KiB) and a 3 MiB non-file field, 3.0.2 returned the full 3145728-byte value in 0.0077 s with peak RSS 41416 KiB against 34760 KiB before parsing, while 3.0.6 raised RequestEntityTooLarge at formparser.py:389 with RSS 34900 vs 34772 KiB. Instrumentation on 3.0.2 saw 49 non-empty receive_data calls, zero of them with a non-empty decoder buffer, and a maximum of 65536 bytes of buffer + chunk, so the 1 MiB limit never engaged. Negative controls: buffer_size 2 MiB > limit, and a stream that ignores read(n) and returns 3 MiB at once, both raise in sansio/multipart.py receive_data on both versions; max_form_memory_size=None succeeds on both, so the bypass requires the limit to be set and the chunks to stay below it. Caveats recorded by the reviewer: the upstream regression test (max_form_memory_size=10, buffer_size=5) also raises on 3.0.2 (receive_data) and on 3.0.6 never reaches the new formparser.py:389 check, so it does not discriminate the fix and the 3 MiB case is the discriminating evidence; 3.0.5 was checked statically only; the reproduction drives MultiPartParser.parse directly (no WSGI server, socket, Request.from_values or Flask app); RSS is process-level ru_maxrss and the advisory's 3-8x / 1 Gbit/s / 32 GB figures were not measured; the quart package (0 -> 0.20.0) is a separate record and is not claimed as this repository's code. Public records agree: one PyPI range 2.0.0rc1 -> 3.0.6, CWE-400 (GHSA) plus CWE-770 (CVE/NVD), NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH / Secondary CVSS 4.0 6.9 MEDIUM, and publication order PyPI 3.0.6 (2024-10-25T18:52:30Z) -> OSV CVE (19:41:35Z) -> GHSA (19:44:43Z) -> NVD (20:15:04Z). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2026-15307; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. Fixed in 5.2.17 (main f1949c1f, backport 115ffd04) and 6.0.8 (backport 208f80cb); the 6.1 final tag already contains 39b3e2d0. notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict with a red/green reproduction. 4.2.13 BaseSpatialField.get_raster_prep_value() (db/models/fields.py:172-189) passes every str/bytes/__geo_interface__ value to gdal.GDALRaster(value) at line 180 and every dict at line 185; the call site is get_prep_value at 205. A dict (or a str holding JSON) forces _write = 1 (raster/source.py:129) and reaches capi.create_ds (163), letting a file-backed driver create an attacker-named file; a str beginning with /vsi skips the os.path.exists() check (source.py:87-97) and makes GDAL open a URL. The reviewer built GDAL 3.13.3 / GEOS 3.14.1 / Python 3.12.15 without root and drove 4.2.13 through dict, JSON-string and admin-changelist inputs: each wrote a 694-byte GTiff (sha256 c9c452e0...) and the /vsicurl value produced 15 outbound connections before failing on write mode. 5.2.17 and 4.2.13 plus the 5.2 fix hunk both raised DisallowedRasterLookup with zero writes and zero connections. Caveats kept from the verdict: GDAL 3.13.3 is not necessarily the target deployment, RCE was not demonstrated (only attacker-named GDAL-generated files plus SSRF), and the admin step ran on a non-spatial sqlite backend after the write had already happened. vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2026-15830; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round36 verdict is grade B and is static: no executable Django/GEOS environment was available, so the crash was not observed. Fixed in 5.2.17 (ba80833f) and 6.0.8 (6af5da31) by the phase-1 limiter, and completely in 5.2.18 (1eafa1a8), 6.0.9 (4353dfb5) and 6.1.2 (75d401a1) by the structural WKB rewrite; the 6.1 fix 9e4a3f18 is already an ancestor of the 6.1 final tag. 4.2 is unsupported and has no backport: 4.2.30, the branch's last release, still has the unguarded readers.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade B, static). 4.2.13 django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py hands WKT/WKB to GEOS with no collection limit: _WKTReader.read (156) and _WKBReader.read (167) call wkt_reader_read/wkb_reader_read(_hex) directly. GEOS recursed once per nested GEOMETRYCOLLECTION without a depth cap before 3.15.0 (upstream 8b8b3da7 adds MAX_PARSE_DEPTH = 100), so deeply nested input overflows the stack and kills the process. Reachable from GEOSGeometry.__init__ (geometry.py:714), i.e. from spatial lookups (BaseSpatialField.get_prep_value, db/models/fields.py:191/211) and GeometryField.to_python (forms/fields.py:37/50); GeoJSON goes through GDAL and is not affected. Phase 1 (5.2.17/6.0.8, main d2e59b77) added MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS = 198 before the GEOS call; phase 2 (5.2.18/6.0.9/6.1.2, main 62ef9d40) replaced the byte-pattern WKB scan with a structural _WKBFrame walk after bypasses. The 6.1 fix 9e4a3f18 is already an ancestor of the 6.1 final tag, so the advisory's 6.1.1 bound is late. 4.2.13 and 4.2.30 geos/prototypes/io.py are byte-identical and no fix commit is an ancestor of either tag (4.2's extended support ended 2026-04-07; 4.2.30, released that day, is its last release). Caveats: the exposure also depends on the linked GEOS version (>= 3.15.0 already caps parse depth at 100) and on application code passing attacker-controlled text into GEOSGeometry; the public records disagree on the fixed versions (5.2.17/6.0.8 in GHSA/PYSEC/Bitnami/CPE versus 5.2.18/6.0.9 in the CVE description and NVD text). Severity: Django 'moderate', GHSA MODERATE, Bitnami Medium, NVD 5.3 MEDIUM (CVSS 3.1) / 6.9 (CVSS 4.0), both Secondary. vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2026-25673; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The 4.2 line is fixed in 4.2.29 (2026-03-03); 4.2.28 is the last affected 4.2 release. Other patched lines: 5.2.12 and 6.0.3. notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict with a red/green reproduction. 4.2.13 URLField.to_python() (forms/fields.py:759-787) passes the whole submitted value to split_url(), which calls list(urlsplit(url)) at line 766; urllib.parse.urlsplit() runs unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', netloc) on a non-ASCII netloc, which the advisory says is disproportionately slow on Windows. The reviewer's probe showed 4.2.13/4.2.28 accepting a 20,017-character target with urlsplit x1 and NFKC x1 on the 20,008-character netloc, 2 urlsplit calls for a scheme-less value, and no normalization for long ASCII values; 4.2.29 imports no urlsplit, reports 0/0 on all 12 cases and returns inner control characters unchanged (inner_newline). Applying the 4.2 fix hunk to the 4.2.13 source produced a URLField block byte-identical to 4.2.29 and 0/0 probe calls. Impact is Windows-only and no DoS timing was measured on Linux (about 0.02 ms per 20,008-character normalize), so the record is a call-boundary positive, not an executed DoS. vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict; the evidence is static rather than executed. 4.2.13 GDALRaster.__init__'s bytes branch (gdal/raster/source.py:102-119) passes `size = sys.getsizeof(ds_input)` (line 106) to capi.create_vsi_file_from_mem_buffer. sys.getsizeof includes the PyBytesObject header, so GDAL records a buffer about 32 bytes longer than the payload (`sys.getsizeof(b'') == 33`); reading the vsi_buffer property (244-258, string_at(dat, out_length.value)) then walks past the buffer. 4.2.13 and 5.2.15 source.py are byte-identical files (sha256 366b028d...), and 5.2.15 is the last affected 5.2 release, so the 4.2 file sits on the same pre-fix code; 5.2.16 and 6.0.7 use `len(ds_input)` and drop `import sys`, and 5.2.16 adds the regression test test_vsi_buffer_length. Caveats: no GDAL execution was possible, so the over-read was not observed; the bytes branch is reachable from spatial lookups, but vsi_buffer has no in-library caller at 4.2.13, so impact needs application code that serializes through that property. basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2025-49007; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round37 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed in 3.1.16 (aed514df, 3.1 line) and 3.2.0 (4795831a, 3.2 line) by anchoring the Content-Disposition / Content-Type / Content-ID regexes at ^; the 3.1 fix is absent from v3.1.13, v3.1.14 and v3.1.15.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). At lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb:310 handle_mime_head matches the whole MIME header block against the unanchored /Content-Disposition:(.*)(?=#{EOL}(\S|\z))/ni defined at line 36: the engine retries the greedy (.*) plus look-ahead at every offset in the header block where the literal can start, and the CONTENT_DISPOSITION_MAX_BYTES = 1536 cap is checked only at line 311, after the match, so the whole header block is scanned before the cap applies. Quadratic cost needs many literal restarts in one header line plus a failing end-of-line look-ahead (e.g. a folded continuation line that starts with a space): a single occurrence followed by a long value pays one scan and stays linear. The header block is bounded only by the blank-line terminator (@head_regex, line 214) and read_data (258-262) appends up to BUFSIZE = 1_048_576 bytes per read; it is a MIME part header inside the request body, not an HTTP request header, so request-header size limits usually do not apply and the relevant bounds are body-size limits and concurrency. Reachable from Rack::Request#POST (lib/rack/request.rb:503, parse_multipart at 527) through Rack::Multipart.parse_multipart (lib/rack/multipart.rb:48/62) and Parser.parse into handle_mime_head. Fixed in 3.1.16 by aed514df and in 3.2.0 by 4795831a: ^-anchored regexes with FWS/HEADER_VALUE; neither fix is an ancestor of v3.1.13/14/15. CHANGELOG.md at tag v3.1.16 still has no [3.1.16] section. The reviewer's own probe on the real library, same bodies on both releases: median parse time 1.336 ms at 2.5 KB (k=125) rising to 1439 ms at 80 KB (k=4000) on v3.1.13, log-log slope ~2.01, versus 1.305 ms at 80 KB on v3.1.16 (slope ~0.99), with a benign multipart control parsing in both. Caveats: the exposure needs an attacker-controlled multipart part header carrying many literal restarts plus a failing end-of-line look-ahead (a plain long header value stays linear), and the bound on how much can be sent is a body-size limit rather than a request-header limit; the public records agree on the range (>= 3.1.0, < 3.1.16) but disagree on the metric version (NVD CVSS 3.1 5.3 MEDIUM Primary versus GHSA/rubysec CVSS 4.0 6.6) and on the CWE (NVD Primary CWE-1333 versus GitHub/CVE record CWE-770). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2025-61770; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round39 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed on the 3.1 line in 3.1.17 (e08f78c6) by capping the preamble before the first boundary at 16 KiB; that commit is absent from v3.1.13, v3.1.14, v3.1.15 and v3.1.16.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). At lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb:271 handle_fast_forward looks for the opening multipart boundary through consume_boundary (434-441), which scans @body_regex (435; defined at 210 as /(?:#{EOL}|\A)--#{boundary}(?:#{EOL}|--)/m) and, when it is not found, only calls @sbuf.terminate (438) - moving the scan pointer without releasing the string. The else branch at 287-289 just returns :want_read with no byte cap, and read_data (258-262) keeps appending io.read(@bufsize) (BUFSIZE = 1_048_576, line 40) into @sbuf, so every byte sent before the first boundary stays resident in memory. There is no amplification in retained bytes: the resident string grows with the bytes actually sent, so the bound is the server body limit and concurrency, not a small-input blow-up (peak RSS can still reach about 1.6-2x the payload because Ruby String growth copies the buffer; the round39 reviewer measured VmHWM 141,404 kB against a 25,856 kB baseline for a 64 MiB preamble). Reachable from Rack::Request#POST (lib/rack/request.rb:503, form_data? def 470 / test 474 with multipart/form-data at 153-155, parse_multipart at 527) through Rack::Multipart.parse_multipart (lib/rack/multipart.rb:48/62) and Parser#parse into handle_fast_forward. Fixed on the 3.1 line by e08f78c6 (first release 3.1.17): adds BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT = 16 KiB and raises "multipart boundary not found within limit" above the limit, comparing @sbuf.string.bytesize against the whole buffer after each read, so the first threshold hit is the first BUFSIZE multiple above 16 KiB (1,048,576 B with the default BUFSIZE; 24,576 B with BUFSIZE 8192, as the round39 reviewer measured). That commit is absent from v3.1.13/14/15/16. The same commit also fixes CVE-2025-61772 (per-part header limit); the retained-size limit (BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT) comes from the separate follow-up f224f93b for CVE-2025-61771 and must not be attributed to this CVE. Caveats: this is a missing ceiling, not an amplification bug - the memory used scales with the body the client actually sends, so exposure depends on the deployment body limit (proxy client_max_body_size and friends) and on concurrency; the buffered bytes are the multipart preamble inside the body, not an HTTP request header, and the advisory applies to every 2.x/3.x line with fixes in 2.2.19, 3.1.17 and 3.2.2. The records agree on the range (>= 3.1.0, < 3.1.17) and on a single CWE-400; severity is CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH, published as a Secondary NVD metric only (no CVSS 4.0). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2025-61771; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round40 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed on the 3.1 line in 3.1.17 (f224f93b) by capping the bytes retained for multipart parameters that are buffered in memory; that commit is absent from v3.1.13 and v3.1.16.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). At lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb:131 a part without a filename is a BufferPart ('file?; false'), so its body is never written to a Tempfile. Collector#on_mime_head (153) starts a String body (160) and Collector#on_mime_body (169-171) appends every chunk with @mime_parts[mime_index].body << content (170); the parser feeds it complete bodies at ordinary sizes and @sbuf.peek(delta) for the streaming tail (called from handle_mime_body at 414/422). check_part_limits (178-195) bounds the number of open files (182-187) and the number of parts (189-194) but never the byte count, so arbitrarily many non-file fields stay resident in RAM. Reachable from Rack::Request#POST (lib/rack/request.rb:503) through Rack::Multipart.parse_multipart (lib/rack/multipart.rb:48/62) and Parser#parse into handle_mime_head / handle_mime_body. Fixed on the 3.1 line by f224f93b (first release 3.1.17): adds BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (16 * 1024 * 1024, overridable with RACK_MULTIPART_BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT), @retained_size / @body_retained accounting and update_retained_size (475-480), which raises Error 'multipart data over retained size limit' once the retained bytes exceed the limit (the Error constant is an alias of BoundaryTooLongError, so the raised class reports as Rack::Multipart::BoundaryTooLongError). The retained-size commit is the child of e08f78c6: the sibling commits the public advisory, OSV GIT range and rubysec cite (e08f78c6 / 589127f4 / d869fed6) only add BOUNDARY_START_LIMIT and MIME_HEADER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT for CVE-2025-61770 and the per-part header limit for CVE-2025-61772, so the public record conflates the two changes; the 3.2 (3beacfcd, 3.2.2) and 2.2 (c370dcd9, 2.2.19) retained-size commits are the children of the matching sibling commits. Caveats: this is a missing ceiling, not an amplification bug - the resident memory scales with the bytes the client actually sends (the independent reviewer measured 1.03-1.12x of the payload after GC, with peak RSS around 1.6x from allocator overhead), so exposure depends on the deployment body limit and on concurrency. Only non-file fields are buffered; parts carrying a filename go to a Tempfile and are not counted against the limit. The advisory quotes 'e.g., 2 MiB' while the shipped default is 16 MiB, and the commit message names RACK_MULTIPART_MAX_BUFFERED_UPLOAD_SIZE while the code and README use RACK_MULTIPART_BUFFERED_UPLOAD_BYTESIZE_LIMIT; both discrepancies are recorded. The records agree on the range (>= 3.1.0, < 3.1.17) and on a single CWE-400; severity is CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH, published as a Secondary NVD metric only (no CVSS 4.0). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2025-61780; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round42 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed on the 3.1 line in 3.1.18 (7e69f65e) by removing the HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE fallback and gating HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING; that commit is absent from v3.1.0, v3.1.13 and v3.1.17.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). In lib/rack/sendfile.rb the middleware treats request headers as its configuration in two independently triggerable places. First, Rack::Sendfile#variation (148-152) returns @variation || env['sendfile.type'] || env['HTTP_X_SENDFILE_TYPE'], so a middleware constructed without a variation (the default Rack::Sendfile.new(app)) lets the client turn sendfile on and pick which response header name is written (headers[type.downcase] at 123 and 134). Second, Rack::Sendfile#map_accel_path (154-165) falls back to env['HTTP_X_ACCEL_MAPPING'] (157) whenever no application-level mapping matched, so the client also chooses the internal-to-external path substitution that ends up in the x-accel-redirect header at 123. Because the mapping half is separate, it also affects deployments that did configure x-accel-redirect explicitly. Rack::Files satisfies the precondition: its body has alias :to_path :path (files.rb:185), which is what makes body.respond_to?(:to_path) at 116 true. Fixed on the 3.1 line by 7e69f65e (first release 3.1.18): variation is now @variation || env['sendfile.type'], the new x_accel_mapping returns the header only when @variation matches x-accel-redirect and @mappings is empty, and both mapping regexes use \A instead of ^ so a newline-containing path cannot satisfy the anchor. The 3.2 (57277b77, 3.2.3) and 2.2 (fba2c8bc, 2.2.20) commits carry the same change. sendfile.rb is byte-identical at v3.1.13 / v3.1.17 / v3.2.2 (395efb8b...) and at v3.1.18 / v3.2.3 (b0b8a22e...); v3.1.0 already has both fallbacks. Repro evidence: the round42 reviewer installed genuine rack 3.1.13 and 3.1.18 gems (sendfile.rb sha256 395efb8b... / b0b8a22e..., equal to the tag files and git blobs) and drove Rack::Sendfile wrapping Rack::Files with Rack::MockRequest; 23/23 assertions passed. On 3.1.13 a bare middleware plus x-sendfile-type: x-accel-redirect and x-accel-mapping: <dir>/=/attacker/path/ produced x-accel-redirect: /attacker/path/secret.txt with content-length 0 and an emptied body, and x-sendfile-type: x-sendfile reflected the absolute tempfile path; 3.1.18 emitted neither header. Caveats: exposure requires a front proxy that forwards these client headers to the backend and then acts on the returned x-accel-redirect/x-sendfile header (proxies that pin or strip them are not affected), and the advisory states this is not arbitrary file read. The fix intentionally keeps the client mapping header when x-accel-redirect was configured explicitly and no app mappings exist, so that residual surface is by design, not a failure of the fix. The public records agree here: three real per-branch fix commits, no attribution conflation; the publication order is CVE (16:53:57Z) and NVD (17:15:39Z) before GHSA (17:31:31Z). Affected range >= 3.0, < 3.1.18; CWE-200 / CWE-441 / CWE-913; NVD carries two CVSS 3.1 metrics (5.8 Secondary S:C, 5.3 Primary S:U), no CVSS 4.0. vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2025-61919; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round41 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. Fixed on the 3.1 line in 3.1.18 (cbd541e8) by bounding the url-encoded body read to query_parser.bytesize_limit + 2; that commit is absent from v3.1.13 and v3.1.17.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). In lib/rack/request.rb the url-encoded branch of Rack::Request#POST reaches form_vars = get_header(RACK_INPUT).read at 531: IO#read with no argument, i.e. read to EOF into one resident String before any size check runs. At v3.1.13 the QueryParser has no byte or count limit at all (query_parser.rb initialize takes only params_class and param_depth_limit; no BYTESIZE_LIMIT, PARAMS_LIMIT or QueryLimitError), so the read is unbounded and the parse that follows it (parse_query at 538) is unbounded too. Fixed on the 3.1 line by cbd541e8 (first release 3.1.18): the read becomes get_header(RACK_INPUT).read(query_parser.bytesize_limit + 2) || '' (534) with attr_reader :bytesize_limit added to QueryParser, capping a body at bytesize_limit + 2 (4 MiB default via RACK_QUERY_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT). The +2 is the minimum that keeps a limit+1-byte body from being silently accepted after a trailing NUL is sliced, and the || '' covers IO#read returning nil at EOF for an empty body. The 3.2 (e179614c, 3.2.3) and 2.2 (4e2c9039, 2.2.20) commits carry the same bounded read. 3.1.17 is an intermediate state: the parser already limits the parse to 4 MiB, but the read still happens first, so the whole body is resident before the limit fires. The separate QueryParser limits that 3.1.14 introduced belong to CVE-2025-46727; this CVE's 3.1 commit only adds the accessor and rebinds the read. Caveats: no amplification - a client must send N bytes to make the process hold about N bytes for that request (the independent reviewer measured 1.0x with linear 1/8/32/64 MiB steps, VmRSS +1024/8192/32896/65536 KiB), so exposure depends on front-proxy body caps, the deployment's own limits and concurrency. 3.1.18 bounds the read at bytesize_limit + 2 = 4,194,306 bytes and rejects larger bodies with Rack::QueryParser::QueryLimitError; 3.1.17 reads the whole 8 MiB before its parser limit fires. The records agree on the range (>= 3.0, < 3.1.18) and on a single CWE-400; severity is CVSS 3.1 7.5 HIGH, published as a Secondary NVD metric only (no CVSS 4.0; SSVC automatable no). vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

The defect is a struct-size mismatch inside the per-element default-attribute name hash table: dtdCopy inserts entries with sizeof(NAMED) while storeAtts casts them to NAME_AND_DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTE (PR for 2.8.4), so attIndex is read past the allocation. That table (m_defaultAttForName / defaultAttsNames) was introduced by the CVE-2026-45186 fix in 2.8.1; at R_2_6_2 dtdCopy copies the DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTE array directly (xmlparse.c:7020, :7029-7035) and storeAtts resolves isCdata by walking elementType->defaultAtts (xmlparse.c:3456-3457, :3512). No such table entry is ever created, so the out-of-bounds read cannot occur at this tag.
notes: Fix-site structure absent at R_2_6_2 (mechanism introduced after the frozen tag); no promotion.

basis: Promoted after independent review of CVE-2021-3603; see data/vulnerabilities.jsonl, data/locations.jsonl and data/reviews.jsonl. The independent round45 verdict is grade A with an executed red/green reproduction. The snapshot v6.1.5 is inside >= 5.2.15, < 6.5.0; the fix lands in 6.5.0 (45f3c18d) and is absent from v6.4.1 and from every 5.2 tag.
notes: Known positive for this SHA from an isolated independent verdict (grade A, executed reproduction). PHPMailer::validateAddress($address, $patternselect = null) (src/PHPMailer.php:1304) resolves a null selector to static::$validator (1306-1307), which defaults to 'php' at 576, and then runs `if (is_callable($patternselect)) { return $patternselect($address); }` (1309-1311): any string naming a defined global function is called and its return value becomes the validation verdict. The built-in `case 'php': default: filter_var(...)` switch (1358-1360) is only reached when the callable test fails. The branch is reachable through validateAddress itself and through addAddress (999 -> addOrEnqueueAnAddress 1063 -> addAnAddress 1118 -> 1134), setFrom (1235 -> 1243), parseAddresses (1178 -> 1185/1202/1211), preSend (1453 -> 1500) and mailSend (1762 -> 1781/1784). It was introduced by 77c0bc8d (2016-05-09) and first ships in v5.2.15 (class.phpmailer.php:1056-1061) and v6.0.0rc2 (1033-1038); static::$validator is still 'auto' there and only becomes 'php' at v6.0.0rc3 (492), so the default-configuration hijack described by the CVE is code-level 6.0.0rc3 .. 6.4.1 and the earlier releases need the application to assign 'php' to $validator or pass 'php' explicitly. The fix 45f3c18dc6a2de1cb1bf49b9b249a9ee36a5f7f3 ('Deny string-based callables altogether', 2021-06-15; its parent 6334bab2 carried an unreleased partial guard that denied only php/pcre/pcre8/html5) adds `&& !is_string($patternselect)` at 1341 and switches to call_user_func at 1342 as released in 6.5.0; it is absent from v6.4.1 and from every 5.2 tag, and v5.2.28 (2020-03-19) still lacks it, so the 5.2 branch has no fixed release. The fix commit's own file still says VERSION 6.4.1 and predates the sibling CVE-2021-34551 setLanguage() rewrite from the same release, so it is not byte-identical to the v6.5.0 tag file; validateAddress() itself (1335-1342) is identical in both. Repro evidence: the round45 reviewer wrote its own harness.php (not the collector's probe), loaded its own refetch of src/PHPMailer.php at v6.1.5 (sha256 9e8ad5d8...6de0) and v6.5.0 (ce454285...1085), and ran injected and plain modes on PHP 8.4.23 CLI (NTS, WSL2) with empty stderr; compare_runs.py passed 18/18 assertions. Injected mode defines global php() (returns true, records the call) and phpx() (returns false) before the require. Results at 6.1.5 vs 6.5.0: validateAddress('not-an-address') with the default selector => true calling php(...) vs false with no call; validateAddress('victim@example.com') => true calling php(...) vs true with no call; validateAddress('not-an-address','php') => true calling php(...) vs false; validateAddress('victim@example.com','phpx') => false calling phpx(...) vs true; addAddress('bad@domain') => true storing 'bad@domain' vs false with no recipient; setFrom('bad@domain') => true with From='bad@domain' vs false keeping root@localhost. The marker file recorded six injected calls on 6.1.5 and none on 6.5.0. Closures still work on both versions, matching the fix's string-only prohibition and the 6.5.0 changelog BC note. Negative control: with no global php()/phpx() defined, 6.1.5 and 6.5.0 agree on all nine probes with zero injected calls and no marker. Caveats recorded by the reviewer: the harness supplies the injection premise directly, so this shows the trigger path rather than a standalone remote exploit; the reproduction loads the single pinned file instead of a composer install (sufficient here because validateAddress and its callers live in that file); public-API probes use 'bad@domain', because addresses without '@' are rejected by addOrEnqueueAnAddress/setFrom before validateAddress is consulted; no audit was made of applications that pass request data into $patternselect or assign $validator from user input; the 5.2 line was read statically only, and its default 'auto' changes the practical trigger; the 6.5.0 upstream test (test/validators.php) only discriminates the fix when that file is loaded, and it exists only from the fix onward, so the harness is the discriminating evidence; CVE-2021-34551 (setLanguage(), also fixed in 6.5.0) is out of scope. Public records agree on the code facts but their ranges are over-broad: GHSA/Packagist introduced 0, fixed 6.5.0 with 52 versions v5.2.2 .. v6.4.1; OSV CVE GIT introduced 0, last_affected 9256f12d, fixed 45f3c18d with a 24-version list down to v2.2.1; NVD CPE cpe:2.3:a:phpmailer_project:phpmailer:* with versionEndIncluding 6.4.1 and no lower bound. v5.2.2 has no $patternselect at all, so the code-level lower bound kept here is 5.2.15 / 6.0.0rc2. CWE is CWE-829 (NVD Primary and Secondary; GHSA also lists the broader CWE-74). Severity is published as is: CVSS 3.1 8.1 HIGH (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) and CVSS 2.0 6.8, despite GHSA's 'Low impact' narrative. OSV, NVD and the rendered GHSA page are live records whose bytes drifted between the packet pins and the reviewer's refetch; every cited field value was re-checked and none changed. vulnerability_id links to the selected-snapshot oracle row.

basis: CVE-2026-88056 / GHSA-f6mr-pjwc-34m4 states that @angular/platform-server URL resolution "previously executed String.prototype.trim()" and that trim() removing Unicode whitespace (U+00A0, U+FEFF) is what turns an input like "\u00A0//attacker" into a protocol-relative URL. At 19.2.15 the only resolution path is parseUrl in location.ts:23-44, which calls new URL(urlStr, "resolve://") directly; the tree contains no String.prototype.trim() call anywhere in packages/platform-server/src or packages/ssr (the only trim() hits under those packages are in platform-server test files). Node confirms the described discrepancy cannot occur here: new URL("/\u00A0//attacker.test", "resolve://") keeps the NBSP inside the path (pathname "/%C2%A0//attacker.test", hostname ""). CVE-2026-14164 describes a stale filtered_buf in the RAR5 reader: archive_read_support_format_rar5.c init_unpack() frees window_buf and filtered_buf and, if the window_buf calloc fails, returns before filtered_buf is reassigned, so the next entry frees it again. At the frozen SHA init_unpack() (archive_read_support_format_rar5.c:2483-2496) frees both buffers and then always reassigns them — the calloc results when window_size > 0 (lines 2490-2492), NULL otherwise (2493-2495) — and has no early return between the free and the reassignment, so no freed pointer can survive; freeing NULL is a no-op. The dangling-pointer shape requires the calloc-failure early returns added by 620bdafa ("Fix unchecked calloc results in init_unpack (rar5)", 2026-05-16), which are absent from v3.7.7 and every release tag through 3.8.7; the release-3.8.8 tree already carries the corrected form (NULL assigned immediately after the frees) that 1c914cdf (PR #3071) applies to master. NVD's only upstream references for this CVE are issue #3069 and PR #3071, both about the post-3.8.7 master code. Static review finds no reachable double free at this snapshot.
notes: The double-free shape needs the post-3.8.7 calloc-failure early returns (620bdafa); frozen init_unpack reassigns both pointers unconditionally.

CVE-2024-20696 is the Windows libarchive remote code execution that MSRC published in January 2024. The rar4 unpack path in the frozen tree therefore already carries the fix, and the only advisory attached to the candidate (USN-8147-1) points at this already-merged change. The CGI servlet resolves a requested pathInfo by walking the filesystem and derives the CGI script name from the on-disk name (cginameBuilder), so on a case-insensitive file system a request whose pathInfo case differs from the stored file still executes that script while Tomcat matched security constraints against the request URI; constraints that apply to the pathInfo component are therefore bypassed. The cited fix resolves the script through the WebResource API and sets scriptName from the requested urlPath instead of the on-disk cginame, keeping the executed script name consistent with the URI used for constraint matching.

Angular's template preparser classified an element as a script only when nodeName == SCRIPT_ELEMENT. The cited fix replaces the equality tests with a SCRIPT_ELEMENTS set containing both ':svg:script' and 'script'; both removed lines are present verbatim at the frozen anchor.

Host bindings derived their SecurityContext from input.componentSelector (the declaring component/directive selector) rather than from the concrete host element. Under hostDirectives composition, inherited HostBinding declarations, createComponent with a custom hostElement, SVG/MathML hosts or tag-neutral selectors such as :not(...), the sanitizer chosen at compile time could be wrong or absent, so attacker-controlled href/src/action/xlink:href values reached DOM attributes unsanitized. The cited fix removes both selector-based calcPossibleSecurityContexts calls in ingestHostBinding; the property-branch call is present verbatim at the frozen anchor.

In 19.2.15 xsrfInterceptorFn skips attaching the X-XSRF-TOKEN header only when req.url starts with 'http://' or 'https://' after lowercasing. Protocol-relative URLs ('//evil.example/x') and WHATWG-normalized forms (backslashes, leading C0/space, embedded tabs/newlines) do not match, so the cookie-derived token is attached to a cross-origin request. The cited fix commits replace the absolute-URL check with an origin comparison computed through the URL parser; the 20/21/22 incarnations use ABSOLUTE_URL_REGEX, whose pre-image is absent from this 19.2.15 branch, so the anchor is the equivalent vulnerable check here.

AssetGroup.newRequestWithMetadata rebuilt service-worker requests with only {headers: options.headers}, preserving every header across redirects. A cross-origin redirect therefore carried Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie to the new origin. The cited fix keeps the request init but, when the parsed URL origin differs from the adapter origin, deletes those three headers. The frozen 19.2.15 function body is shorter than the fix pre-image, so the anchor is the function that preserves headers unconditionally.

renderApplication (like renderModule) passes options.url straight into the platform INITIAL_CONFIG without validating its hostname, so ServerPlatformLocation adopts an attacker-supplied absolute URL (http://evil.com) as the current origin and relative HttpClient/PlatformLocation use is redirected there (SSRF). The cited fix adds validateAllowedHosts(url, allowedHosts) at both entry points; the destructuring line the fix rewrites is present verbatim at the frozen anchor.

SECURITY_SCHEMA registers URL security contexts per element|attribute but listed only HTML elements and omitted 'a|xlink:href', the MathML href/xlink:href entries and the SVG animation attributeName registrations. Templates using those attributes were compiled without a URL or ATTRIBUTE_NO_BINDING context, producing the stored XSS described in the advisory. The cited fix adds those entries (and the ATTRIBUTE_NO_BINDING block) to SECURITY_SCHEMA; the anchor is the URL registration list it extends.

When an easy handle with cookies enabled is duplicated, curl_easy_duphandle called Curl_cookie_init() with the source handle's cookie filename. The cited fix passes NULL so the clone starts without a cookie source; the two removed argument lines are present verbatim at the frozen anchor.

The wolfSSH backend builds its client context and session, sets the username, installs the auth callback and attaches the socket without ever installing a host-key check or comparing the server key against known hosts, so SFTP/SCP transfers cannot detect a MITM server. ConnectionExists compares the requesting handle's credentials with the cached connection only for NTLM (and proxy NTLM). For Negotiate/SPNEGO there is no such comparison: a connection that performed ambient-credential Negotiate authentication for one user is a reuse candidate for a later request from a different handle, sending that request over the authenticated connection. The cited fix (7103a93b05bc) rewrites this credential check around url_allow_sspi_empty_creds in newer code; the frozen 8.3.0 equivalent is the NTLM-only block at the anchor.

Connection reuse compares ssl_primary_config through Curl_ssl_config_matches, which covers version, verify flags, CA/client cert files, blobs, ciphers, curves, CRL and pinned key but not the client private key, key type or key passphrase. Changing only those options therefore leaves the config matching and a connection established with a different client key is reused, defeating mTLS separation. The cited fix adds the key fields to the matcher in newer code (match_ssl_primary_config); the frozen 8.3.0 equivalent is the function at the anchor.

A document of a few tens of kilobytes of '[' exhausts the memory limit (or the stack) before any guard runs, which is the DoS described in the advisory. The cited fix wraps the lexer body in enterNestingLevel()/leaveNestingLevel(); the frozen function at the anchor is the unguarded self-recursive form.

A carefully crafted attribute value could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name, possibly leading to ... This can cause excessive memory allocation and CPU consumption when the expanded number is form... Prior to versions 8.1.2.1, 8.0.4.1, and 7.2.3.1, the interaction between the repeated lookahead group and gsub! can produce quadratic time complexity on long digit strings. Versions 8.1.2.1, 8.0.... Advisory CVE-2026-33169 covers v8.0.4 (fixed in ec1a0e215efd27a3b3911aae6df978a80f456a49); fix commit 29154f1097da removes lines that are present in activesupport/lib/active_support/number_helper/number_to_delimited_converter.rb:19-20 at frozen SHA 624fe3cdb9ab (fix-diff comparison).

SafeBuffer#% built its result with self.class.new(super(escaped_args)) and never copied the receiver's @html_safe state. When a buffer has been mutated in place (e.g. by gsub!, which sets @html_unsafe) and is then formatted with % and untrusted arguments, the new buffer reports html_safe? == true even though the interpolated values were not escaped for the unsafe fragment, so ERB auto-escaping is bypassed (XSS). The cited fix copies @html_safe to the new buffer; frozen line 131 is the removed constructor call.

Direct uploads reach Blob.create_before_direct_upload!, which passes the client-supplied metadata hash straight to create!. Active Storage stores its internal flags (analyzed, identified, composed) in that same metadata hash, so a direct-upload client can pre-set them and make later MIME detection and analysis skip the uploaded file (content-type bypass). The cited fix inserts metadata = filter_metadata(metadata), which drops the protected keys, before the create! call at the anchor.

send_blob_byte_range_data accepts whatever list Rack::Utils.get_byte_ranges returns for the Range header and starts a multipart response for every entry, so a request with thousands of tiny ranges forces disproportionate CPU work for one response (DoS). The cited fix adds a check against ActiveStorage.streaming_max_ranges right after the ranges are parsed; the frozen 8.0.4 function has no such bound.

Active Storage loaded untrusted blobs with ruby-vips without disabling libvips operations that are unsafe for untrusted content. Beyond the analyzer path, image_processing variants could be made to invoke an unfuzzed loader/saver on a crafted upload, which is the arbitrary file read (e.g. of environment/secret files) and possible RCE described in the advisory. The cited fix adds active_storage/vips.rb, which requires image_processing/vips and then calls Vips.block_untrusted(true); frozen 8.0.4 has no such guard, and read_image calls Vips::Image.new_from_file on the uploaded file at the anchor.

This issue has been patched in versions 12.... A vulnerability in Laravel's local filesystem driver allows temporary signed URLs to be parsed ambiguously, potentially misrouting requests and bypassing expiration enforcement. Advisory GHSA-crmm-hgp2-wgrp covers v11.30.0 (fixed in 12.61.1); fix commit 7b2b2fe508d4 removes lines that are present in src/Illuminate/Filesystem/LocalFilesystemAdapter.php:71-71 at frozen SHA dff716442d9c (fix-diff comparison).
same advisory GHSA-crmm-hgp2-wgrp as adv3_840d026ac9932116; duplicate candidate row, not a second vulnerability

router/web/user/setting/security/openid.go settingsOpenIDVerify verifies a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion and immediately binds the asserted identity to ctx.Doer without checking that this signed-in user began the association. OpenID 2.0 permits unsolicited assertions, so an attacker-controlled provider can attach the attacker's identity to the account of a signed-in victim who opens a crafted link; the attacker can then sign in as the victim through OpenID login, which does not enforce the local TOTP or WebAuthn checks (CWE-287/CWE-352). The cited fix passes a time-limited state code in the redirect from OpenIDPost and requires base.VerifyTimeLimitCode at the top of settingsOpenIDVerify; frozen 82-88 has no such binding.

The Secure middleware decides whether to emit HSTS by trusting the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto header whenever c.IsTLS() is false, so a request over plain HTTP that carries X-Forwarded-Proto: https is treated as secure (CWE-346). The same unconditional header trust in Context.Scheme also lets a direct client bypass middleware.HTTPSRedirect. The cited fix requires the request to come from a trusted proxy before any forwarded scheme header is used and rewrites the HSTS condition to config.HSTSMaxAge != 0 && c.Scheme() == "https"; frozen line 121 is the removed header-trusting condition.

jsonPBlob (and JSONPBlob) concatenate the caller-supplied callback string directly into the JavaScript response body without validating or escaping it, so any route that passes attacker-controlled data as the JSONP callback yields reflected XSS (CWE-79). The cited fix validates the callback as an empty string, a JavaScript identifier or a dot-separated identifier path, returns a 400 wrapping ErrInvalidJSONPCallback for anything else, and sets X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; frozen lines 501-502 are the removed unvalidated header write.

ApplyDiffPatch applies an attacker-controlled patch with git apply --index --cached inside a temporary clone created by t.Clone(ctx, opts.OldBranch, true), i.e. a bare repository. With a bare clone the --index operation writes into the working tree of the shared temporary repository, so repository-controlled patch content can install files such as a Git hook that Gitea later executes, giving an ordinary repository writer (or any registered user under open registration) command execution as the Gitea OS user (CWE-94). The cited fix clones a non-bare repository (t.Clone(ctx, opts.OldBranch, false)) and notes that the following git commands may operate the working tree directly; frozen line 130 is the removed true.

Summary Advisory GHSA-mr3q-g2mv-mr4q covers v4.0.1 (fixed in 4.2.0); fix commit 3fe8c38dc405 removes lines that are present in lib/sinatra/base.rb:713-713 at frozen SHA 7dc5940e44cf (fix-diff comparison).

In Jenkins 2.567 and earlier, LTS 2.555.2 and earlier, it is possible for attackers to have Jenkins deserialize arbitrary types defined in Jenkins core or plugins from an attacker-controlled config.xml submission in a way that allows them to handle HTTP requests afterwards. Advisory GHSA-g2xq-2v27-4rh3 covers jenkins-2.441 (fixed in 2.555.3); fix commit 345a3190a49d removes lines that are present in core/src/main/java/hudson/util/CopyOnWriteList.java:204-204 at frozen SHA 3b0de10df3be (fix-diff comparison).

From 3.0.0 until 4.1.1, decoding a strip TIFF using CCITT Group 3 or Modified Huffman compression can pass attacker-expanded runs to BitWriterUtils.WriteBits without first checking the current row width. T4TiffCompression.WritePixelRun can accumulate oversized makeup-code runs, and ModifiedHuffmanTiffCompression.Decompress validates the width only after writing. The unchecked w... Advisory CVE-2026-106117 covers v3.1.6 (fixed in e8892ecd8a95dee95c4480fda51cfe0b32f3b846); fix commit e8892ecd8a95 removes lines that are present in src/ImageSharp/Formats/Tiff/Compression/Decompressors/ModifiedHuffmanTiffCompression.cs:89-93 at frozen SHA 313a7e8daaae (fix-diff comparison).

cJSONUtils_MergePatch accepts a patch that may be a subtree of the target object. When the patch is not an object, merge_patch calls cJSON_Delete(target) first and then cJSON_Duplicate(patch, 1): if patch lived inside target (a scalar or array child), the delete frees it and the duplicate reads freed memory (heap-use-after-free, CWE-416). The cited fix duplicates the patch into a local variable before deleting the target; frozen lines 1327-1329 are the removed delete-then-duplicate block.

AjpProcessor.prepareRequest compares the client-supplied AJP secret with tmpMB.equals(secret), a non-constant-time comparison, so an attacker on the local network can mount a timing attack and recover the secret byte by byte (CWE-208). The cited fix replaces the call with ConstantTime.equals on the byte chunk; frozen line 837 is the removed comparison.

clean_ipv6_address converts an arbitrary-length string with int(ipaddress.IPv6Address(ip_str)) with no length limit, so a very long IPv6-like value forces disproportionate parsing work when the value is validated (CWE-770). The cited fix adds MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH and rejects longer inputs in _ipv6_address_from_str before parsing; frozen line 27 is the removed unbounded conversion.

The vendored fastify-middie engine copies sanitizeUrl(req.url) into holder.url and matches path-scoped middleware against it. For an absolute-form request target such as 'GET http://host/path', the URL still carries scheme and authority, so middleware mounted on /path never runs while Fastify's router routes the request to /path (CWE-288/CWE-436) - a path-scoped middleware bypass. The cited fix removes the vendored engine and depends on @fastify/middie 9.3.4, which resolves absolute-form targets before matching; frozen line 113 is the removed raw-target assignment.

ListPublicMembers serves GET /orgs/{org}/public_members and delegates to listMembers without checking whether the doer can see the organization. For a private organization any authenticated user can therefore enumerate the users who declared public membership - a membership attribute of an organization they cannot see (CWE-200/CWE-863). The cited fix inserts a HasOrgOrUserVisible check that answers 404 before listMembers; frozen line 120 is the unguarded call. The same fix adds the identical guard to IsPublicMember.

GET /api/v1/user/subscriptions lists the doer's watched repositories with IncludePrivate=true, and WatchedReposOptions.ToConds then applies no access condition at all, so a repository the user watched while they had access is still described (name, description, clone URLs, owner, counters) after a team downgrade removes that access (CWE-862). The cited fix adds an Actor field and ANDs AccessibleRepositoryCondition in the private branch; frozen line 73 is the `if !opts.IncludePrivate` branch that returns the private rows unfiltered. The starred listing (line 35) shares the defect and the fix.

The web route POST /{username} dispatches to ActionUserFollow, which calls FollowUser or UnfollowUser after only the sign-in middleware; the profile visibility check that gates GET /{username} is never applied, so an authenticated user can follow or unfollow a limited or private user and read full_name, location, website and description from the response (CWE-200). The cited fix begins ActionUserFollow with HasOrgOrUserVisible / IsUserVisibleToViewer and answers 404; frozen line 327 is the switch that dispatches the action without a visibility check.

Seven routes under /api/v1/users/{username} (keys, gpg_keys, followers, following, following/{target}, starred, subscriptions) are registered in the /users/{username} group with only UserAssignmentAPI and checkTokenPublicOnly, so the individualPermsChecker middleware that hides limited and private users is not applied; any authenticated user can read the social graph, stars, watches and public keys of a user they cannot otherwise see (CWE-862). The cited fix appends individualPermsChecker to the group closure; frozen line 1046 is that closure.

ServeAttachment resolves the attachment's linked unit and repository and then enforces only perm.CanRead(unitType); draft releases are hidden from listings and API lookups but their UUID-based web download endpoints are served to any reader, so anyone holding the UUID (returned by the API as browser_download_url) can download a draft release attachment even unauthenticated (CWE-200/CWE-639/CWE-862). The cited fix adds a TypeReleases branch that loads the release and answers 404 when it IsDraft and the doer lacks write; frozen line 170 is the read check that stands in for it.

ChangeTargetBranch updates a pull request's base branch but never recomputes the `official` flag stored on existing approve and reject reviews, which was derived from the old branch's approval whitelist; a write-capable user can obtain an official approval on an unprotected branch and retarget the PR to a protected branch, where the stale flag satisfies the required approvals (CWE-863). The cited fix adds RecalculateReviewsOfficial and calls it before the retarget comment; frozen line 325 is the point where the retarget proceeds.

DeleteLabel(ctx, id, labelID) is called with a repository ID for repo labels and an organization ID for org labels, and compares that single id against both namespaces: when an organization label's OrgID equals the repository ID in the request, the org guard passes and the label is deleted from the organization (CWE-863). The cited fix splits the call into DeleteRepoLabel and DeleteOrgLabel; frozen line 250 is the shared-namespace comparison.

GetReleaseAttachments builds `In("release_id", sortedRels.ID)` from every passed release without dropping releases whose ID is 0; the zero ID matches every attachment with release_id = 0, so creating a draft release through the API returns the name, UUID, size, upload time and download count of issue and comment attachments and abandoned uploads from other repositories (CWE-200). The cited fix skips ID-0 releases and returns early; frozen line 403 is the unfiltered IN query.

With [oauth2_client] UPDATE_AVATAR enabled, oauth2UpdateAvatarIfNeed fetches the OAuth2/OIDC picture claim with http.Get, Go's default client, with no host or IP restriction, so a user who controls their own picture claim can make the server GET loopback, RFC1918 and link-local (169.254.169.254) URLs (CWE-918). The cited fix replaces the package-level client with a hostmatcher/proxy-protected client built from security.ALLOWED_HOST_LIST; frozen line 308 is the unrestricted http.Get.

CreateAccessToken accepts any requested scope and stores it on the new token without comparing it with the authenticating token's scope; because a token presented as Basic <token>:x-oauth-basic sets IsBasicAuth, reqBasicOrRevProxyAuth does not stop a token-authenticated caller from minting a broader-scoped (or all-scoped) token without knowing the password (CWE-287). The cited fix adds a CanCreateChildScope ceiling and EnforcePublicOnlyFrom for API-token callers before NewAccessToken; frozen line 127 is where the request scope is adopted unchanged.

CheckAuthToken rotates the remember-me hash when a token is presented; if the presented hash does not match (a stolen token was already used and rotated), the function returns ErrAuthTokenInvalidHash without invalidating the token, so the attacker's rotated token with the same ID keeps working after the victim presents the stolen one (CWE-613). The cited fix deletes the auth token by ID in that branch; frozen line 57 is the mismatching-hash branch.

UpdateCommentAttachments takes the UUIDs from an edited comment and sets IssueID and CommentID on each attachment after only a repository-agnostic fetch by UUID; an attachment of another repository's issue or comment whose UUID the caller knows can be re-linked to the attacker's own comment, after which access checks use the attacker's repository and the private file content is exposed (CWE-639/CWE-862). The cited fix loads the issue and calls validateAttachmentForIssue per attachment; frozen line 614 is the unvalidated re-link.

The /orgs/{org}/labels group in Routes registers the label read endpoints with reqOrgOwnership on mutations but no organization-visibility middleware, so a non-member can GET /api/v1/orgs/{org}/labels and /labels/{id} for a private organization and read label names, colors and descriptions (CWE-200/CWE-862). The cited fix appends reqOrgVisible() to the group; frozen line 1665 is the group registration without it.

The route /{username}/-/repositories is handled by the organization Repositories handler, which calls home(ctx, true); for an individual user ctx.Org.Organization is nil and home dereferences it, so an unauthenticated request panics and returns 500 repeatedly (CWE-248/CWE-476). The cited fix renames home to orgHome and returns 404 when the organization is nil; frozen line 50 is the unchecked dereference source.

The POST /{owner}/{repo}/topics group is registered with RepoAssignment, reqRepoAdmin and RepoMustNotBeArchived but not optSignIn, the middleware that provides the CSRF check for cookie-authenticated web POSTs; a third-party page can therefore change a repository's topics for an administrator who visits it (CWE-352). The cited fix adds optSignIn to the group; frozen line 1411 is the route registration.

ChangeIssueReaction authorizes only signed-in users who can read the issue (or the poster) and never tests issue.IsLocked, so a reader without write access can add or remove reactions on a locked issue and its comments, bypassing the lock's interaction restriction (CWE-863). The cited fix replaces the read check with issue_service.CanSelfChangeOrAccessContent(..., AccessModeRead), which denies locked content to non-writers; frozen line 494 is the read-only check that omits the lock test.

SearchPublicKeyByContentExact looks up a principal by `content = ?` across all stored public keys instead of only principal keys; with SSH_TRUSTED_USER_CA_KEYS configured and SSH_AUTHORIZED_PRINCIPALS_ALLOW=anything, a user can register another user's public key line as their principal and then authenticate as that user through HTTP signatures or the built-in SSH server (CWE-287). The cited fix restricts the query with AND type = KeyTypePrincipal; frozen line 161 is the unfiltered content lookup.

AddReleaseAttachments checks repository and release ownership of an attachment but, for attachments not yet linked to a release, never checks whether it is already linked to an issue or comment; a user with release write access who knows an attachment UUID can link it to a release and then see, rename or delete the private attachment (CWE-639). The cited fix rejects attachments with IssueID, CommentID or ReleaseID set; frozen line 204 is the narrower ReleaseID-only check.

The Migration Restore downloader builds each pull request's PatchURL as file:// plus a path from the restored repository's own YAML and then calls CheckAndEnsureSafePR(pr, "", r). CheckAndEnsureSafePR delegates to hasBaseURL, which with an empty baseURL reduces to strings.HasPrefix(toCheck, "") and therefore accepts every URL; the file:// PatchURL is then read from disk during the restore, so a crafted archive can make the server read an arbitrary local file as a PR patch (CWE-22/CWE-73). The cited fix passes "file://"+r.baseDir as the allowed base and makes hasBaseURL answer false for an empty baseURL; frozen line 238 is the call with the empty base.

The Docker image ships a generated app.ini whose [security] section sets REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES = * while also accepting REVERSE_PROXY_AUTHENTICATION_USER from the request. Gitea treats every source address as a trusted reverse proxy, so when proxy authentication is enabled any client that can reach the container can set X-WEBAUTH-USER and be authenticated as that user (CWE-290/CWE-306). The cited fix deletes REVERSE_PROXY_LIMIT and REVERSE_PROXY_TRUSTED_PROXIES from both Docker templates, making reverse-proxy auth opt-in; frozen line 55 is the removed = * default.
