setup_dp() resolves every nameRelativeToCRLIssuer distribution point against the certificate issuer while OpenSSL builds its cached X.509 extension values, so decoding a peer-supplied certificate allocates and re-encodes one X509_NAME per relative CRLDP. A certificate that fits the ~100 KiB accepted peer-certificate budget can drive several hundred MiB of heap growth (CWE-770). The fix defers the relative-name resolution until the distribution point is actually needed for CRL processing; frozen line 387 is the removed eager DIST_POINT_set_dpname() call.

When the QUIC server runs without client address validation, ossl_quic_handle_frames() adds the length of the whole received datagram to the unvalidated-path credit once per packet that datagram carries, instead of accounting each datagram once. A peer that packs several packets into one datagram therefore inflates the RFC 9000 3x anti-amplification budget in proportion to the packet count (CWE-440), which a spoofing attacker can use for DDoS amplification. The fix deletes the per-packet add_unvalidated_credit() call from frame handling; frozen line 1501 is the removed call.

ossl_sframe_list_insert() locates the insertion point for an incoming STREAM frame with a head-to-tail linear walk of the fragment list, and only the append case is optimised, so a peer that delivers frames out of order makes every insert O(n) and the reassembly of one connection O(n^2) in the number of buffered fragments (CWE-407). Low attacker bandwidth inside the advertised receive window is enough to burn connection-scoped CPU. The fix replaces the doubly-linked list with the ordered quic_strm_reas implementation; frozen lines 117-118 are the removed walk.

ossl_ec_scalar_mul_ladder() copies the secret scalar with BN_copy() and then runs the ladder additions on values whose BIGNUM top depends on the scalar magnitude, so the number of words processed - and therefore the signing time - varies with the per-signature nonce for curves that have no dedicated constant-time implementation (CWE-208). Over many signatures this is a lattice / hidden-number-problem key recovery path. The fix pins k and lambda to fixed word counts with bn_set_top_fixed() before the additions; frozen lines 216-219 are the BN_copy() the fix hardens.

stream_frame_new() takes a reference on the QRX packet buffer that carries each STREAM frame, and stream_frame_free() only drops that reference when the application consumes the data or the stream is destroyed. A peer can therefore pin an unbounded number of packet buffers, with the retention time under its own control, by sending stream data the application does not read (CWE-770). The 3.5-branch fix introduces QUIC_RSTREAM_QPARAM and moves chunks off the packet buffer once ~64kB of overhead accumulates per stream; that code lives in ssl/quic/quic_strm_reas.c, which entered the branch with the CVE-2026-42772 reassembly rewrite, so the frozen line 42 is the equivalent retention site in the 3.5.8 implementation.

ecp_sm2p256_point_add() and the neighbouring point routines branch on is_zeros() tests of field elements derived from the secret scalar, so on ARM64 and RISC-V the timing and the cache-line access pattern of SM2 scalar multiplication depend on the private key or the per-signature nonce (CWE-208). The fix removes the is_zeros() special cases and selects results with constant_time_select_64(); frozen lines 283-291 are one of the removed branches.

SSL_set_SSL_CTX() swaps sc->cert for a duplicate of the replacement context's certificate but leaves the per-connection valid_flags array at the size recorded when the connection was created from the original SSL_CTX. If the replacement context knows about more provider TLS-SIGALG entries than the original, later certificate lookups index past the end of that array - an out-of-bounds read and, in some paths, a fixed-value out-of-bounds write on the server heap (CWE-787). The fix re-sizes valid_flags when the certificate is swapped; frozen lines 5526-5529 are the cert swap the inserted resize follows.

ossl_quic_rxfc_get_error() reports only the stream receiving flow controller's own error code and never consults rxfc->parent, the connection-level controller that owns it. A connection-level flow control violation raised on the parent is therefore invisible to the stream layer, and a peer that stays inside the per-stream window can make the stack hold ~100MB instead of the advertised 768KiB connection window (CWE-770). The fix propagates the parent error code and clears both levels; frozen lines 396-397 are the removed stream-level-only handling.

A CMP client that revokes a certificate named by a PKCS#10 CSR (OSSL_CMP_CTX_set1_p10CSR, or `openssl cmp -cmd rr -csr`) has no issuer name, because a CSR does not carry one. When the server names the revoked certificate in its response, OSSL_CMP_exec_RR_ses() hands the response CertId's issuer to X509_NAME_cmp() unconditionally and dereferences the NULL local issuer, crashing the client (CWE-476). The fix guards the comparison for NULL values; frozen line 1002 is the removed unguarded comparison.

tls1_cipher() passes the record length to the AEAD cipher before checking that the record is long enough to contain the explicit IV and the authentication tag. For a DTLS 1.2 datagram whose encrypted fragment is shorter than that overhead the cipher rejects the impossible length, and the resulting failure tears down an established association without any key material (CWE-1284). The fix rejects records shorter than rl->eivlen + rl->taglen before AEAD processing; frozen lines 259-261 open the AEAD branch the inserted guard precedes.

sm2_sig_gen() computes r + k and the rest of the signature value with variable-time BIGNUM operations on the per-signature nonce and the private key, so the time taken to produce an SM2 signature depends on those secret values (CWE-208). Over many signatures the nonce leaks through a lattice / hidden-number-problem attack. The fix makes the signing arithmetic constant time; frozen lines 289-292 are the removed variable-time BN_add() on the nonce.

dtls1_retransmit_message() rebuilds a queued handshake message into s->init_buf and leaves s->init_off wherever a suspended write left it. A retransmit that fires while a write is parked mid-fragment therefore resumes from a stale offset: the message can be read past the end of the buffer, and the retransmission overwrites s->init_off / init_num that the parked write needs to resume (CWE-125). The fix resets init_off to the start of the message when retransmitting and skips the retransmit timer while a write is still parked; frozen lines 1218-1219 are the memcpy the inserted reset follows.

ossl_quic_channel_on_new_conn_id() walks from ch->cur_retire_prior_to up to the peer-supplied Retire Prior To value, enqueues one RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame per step and advances ch->cur_retire_prior_to immediately, before any of those frames is sent. A peer that floods NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames with increasing Retire Prior To values therefore pushes an unbounded backlog of retire frames into the channel frame queue and exhausts local memory (CWE-770). The fix advances only a local counter and moves cur_retire_prior_to forward when the queued frame is freed; frozen lines 3384-3388 are the removed unbounded loop.

Curl_fopen() derives the temporary file name by appending a random suffix to the full target path (frozen line 71: aprintf("%s.%s.tmp", filename, randsuffix)). When the target file name is long enough that the derived temp name exceeds the file-system NAME_MAX, the temp file cannot be created and the HSTS store rewrite path clears the existing HSTS file, so a later curl invocation trusts HSTS hosts that the store should have pinned (CWE-311). NVD CPE and the curl advisory both place 8.3.0 in 7.84.0 <= v < 8.5.0. The fix (73b65e94, released in 8.5.0) replaces the target-name-derived temp name with a directory prefix plus 40 random characters and ".tmp", via the new dirslash() helper; curl-8_5_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

Curl_vsetopt() parses CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS_STR into a local curl_prot_t and assigns data->set.allowed_protocols only when protocol2num() succeeds (frozen lines 2693-2698). protocol2num() returns CURLE_BAD_FUNCTION_ARGUMENT when the parsed mask is empty (frozen lines 183-186), which is exactly the "-all,-http" case, so the caller keeps the default protocol set and the explicitly disabled protocols stay usable (CWE-115/CWE-436 misinterpretation of the option value). NVD CPE and the curl advisory both place 8.3.0 in 7.85.0 <= v < 8.7.0. The fix (17d302e5, released in 8.7.0) passes the destination mask directly to protocol2num() and clears it before parsing, so the empty set survives the error path; curl-8_7_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

Curl_gtls_verifyserver() parses the stapled OCSP response only when gnutls_ocsp_status_request_is_checked() returns 0 (frozen line 928); when GnuTLS reports the response as already checked, the else branch at frozen lines 1024-1025 records "server certificate status verification OK" without inspecting the OCSP certificate status, so a response whose status is an error other than revoked (for example unauthorized) is accepted as valid (CWE-295). NVD CPE and the curl advisory both place 8.3.0 in 7.41.0 <= v < 8.10.0. The fix (aeb1a281, released in 8.10.0) drops the is_checked() gate, always imports the response, and returns CURLE_SSL_INVALIDCERTSTATUS unless the status is GOOD; curl-8_10_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

on_header() doubles the PUSH_PROMISE header array as headers arrive; once the allocation count exceeds 1000 it frees the array with Curl_safefree() and aborts the push (frozen line 1458). Curl_safefree() frees only the array block, not the up-to-1000 header strings it holds, and push_headers_used keeps its value, so every aborted push leaks its headers and the error is silent (CWE-772). NVD CPE and the curl advisory both place 8.3.0 in 7.44.0 <= v < 8.7.0. The fix (deca8039, released in 8.7.0) adds free_push_headers(), which frees each used string and resets the counter, and calls it on the too-many-headers path, the realloc failure path and stream teardown; curl-8_7_0 ships that code and the frozen 8.3.0 tree does not.

AddPackageTag() reads the dist-tag publish body with io.ReadAll(ctx.Req.Body) and no size bound (frozen routers/api/packages/npm/npm.go:336); the body is only a quoted version string, so an authenticated package owner can post an arbitrarily large body and exhaust the process memory (CWE-770). The fix in f69e15afe7 bounds the read with io.LimitReader(maxDistTagBodySize+1) at 4 KiB and rejects an oversized body with 413 before parsing. v1.27.0 ships the bounded read and the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

showUserFeed() derives includePrivate from organisation membership and passes it straight into feed_service.GetFeeds(GetFeedsOptions{IncludePrivate: includePrivate}) (frozen routers/web/feed/profile.go:44-48); it never consults the API token scope, so a public-only token still receives private activity of its owner, the same confinement #37698 added elsewhere (CWE-200/CWE-862). The fix in f69e15afe7 inserts `if includePrivate && context.TokenIsPublicOnly(ctx) { includePrivate = false }` before the query (and the same guard in routers/web/user/profile.go). v1.27.0 ships the guard, the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

internalAPITransport (the sync.OnceValue function literal at frozen modules/private/internal.go:56-63) builds the internal-API TLS config with InsecureSkipVerify: true and ServerName: setting.Domain unconditionally (lines 60-61), so whenever LOCAL_ROOT_URL is a non-loopback host the bearer INTERNAL_TOKEN in X-Gitea-Internal-Auth can be intercepted by a network attacker (CWE-295). The fix in f69e15afe7 adds internalAPIConnectionIsLocal(protocol, localURL) and skips verification only for a unix-socket or loopback target, verifying the certificate for a real network hop. v1.27.0 ships the conditional skip; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

InfoOAuth() answers the OIDC userinfo request by building userInfoResponse directly from ctx.Doer (frozen routers/web/auth/oauth2_provider.go:101-107) without checking the API token scope carried in ctx.Data["ApiTokenScope"], so a token explicitly restricted away from read:user still receives the identity claims (CWE-200). The fix in f69e15afe7 reads the scope, calls tokenScope.HasScope(auth.AccessTokenScopeReadUser) and returns 403 with a WWW-Authenticate challenge when the claim is missing; standard OIDC tokens map to the "all" scope and are unaffected. v1.27.0 ships the check; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA publishes no CVSS score or vector.

In AddTime(), when a repo admin or site admin adds time for another user, a failed user_model.GetUserByName() is reported with ctx.APIErrorInternal(err) and execution falls through into the time-tracking path with a nil user (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/issue_tracked_time.go:209), dereferencing the nil pointer and crashing the request handler (CWE-476). The fix in f69e15afe7 switches the call to ctx.APIErrorAuto(err) and adds the missing return, so the handler stops after the error. v1.27.0 ships the return; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

AddEmail() (and the sibling DeleteEmail() handler in the same file) processes the email management request without consulting the ManageCredentials user feature, so an instance that disabled user credential management still lets the caller add or remove addresses through the REST API (frozen routers/api/v1/user/email.go:60 is the form parse the request reaches immediately). The fix in f69e15afe7 inserts user_model.IsFeatureDisabledWithLoginType(ctx.Doer, setting.UserFeatureManageCredentials) with a 404 response at the top of AddEmail, DeleteEmail and the other email handlers. v1.27.0 ships the guard; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA page for this CVE is not published (the GitHub advisory API returns 404); the CVE/OSV record supplies CWE-284 and the CVSS v3 vector.

ListJobs() runs db.FindAndCount[actions_model.ActionRunJob] with only the owner/repo filters parsed from the request (frozen routers/api/v1/shared/action.go:50); a bare organisation member can therefore enumerate runs and jobs of organisation repositories they cannot read, and a public-only token of a site admin is not confined either (CWE-200/CWE-863). The fix in f69e15afe7 sets opts.AccessibleRepoIDsSubQuery through the new actionsOwnerAccessibleRepoIDsSubQuery() in both ListJobs and ListRuns, backed by repo_model.FindUserActionsAccessibleOwnerRepoIDsSubQuery. v1.27.0 ships the sub-query on both endpoints; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

StarredReposOptions.ToConds() filters only with `if !opts.IncludePrivate { repository.is_private = false }` (frozen models/repo/user_repo.go:35), so when IncludePrivate is true the /user/starred query returns every starred private repository regardless of whether the caller still has access; WatchedReposOptions.ToConds() has the same shape at frozen line 73 for /user/subscriptions. After a collaborator is removed from a private repository the former collaborator keeps receiving its name, description, visibility and later metadata changes (CWE-200/CWE-862). The fix 362539b78e adds an Actor field and gates the private branch on AccessibleRepositoryCondition(opts.Actor, unit.TypeInvalid) in both option types; the backport is 500a09e044. v1.27.0 ships the actor-gated condition; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA publishes a CVSS v4 vector and a LOW rating but no numeric v3 score.

UpdatePullRequest() loads the head repository with pr.LoadHeadRepo(ctx) (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go:1248) and then proceeds to the update logic without checking that the request token may access that head repository, so a public-only token scoped to the public base repository can push into the private repository that owns the PR head branch (CWE-863). The fix in f69e15afe7 inserts `if !ctx.TokenCanAccessRepo(pr.HeadRepo) { ctx.APIErrorNotFound(); return }` immediately after the head repo load. v1.27.0 ships the guard; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The fix parent has drifted from v1.25.5 (the style parsing around the hunk differs), so the anchor is the frozen LoadHeadRepo line, the statement whose result the new guard checks.

Home() serves the repository home page and reaches checkHomeCodeViewable() (frozen routers/web/repo/view_home.go:369) after only the web-session checks, without context.CheckRepoScopedToken(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository, auth_model.Read); a personal access token that is scoped or public-only therefore gets private repository content through the web route even though its scope forbids it (CWE-863). The fix in f69e15afe7 inserts the scoped-token read check before the viewability check and returns when ctx.Written(). v1.27.0 ships the check; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

DeleteIssueLabel() resolves the label with issues_model.GetLabelByID(ctx, ctx.PathParamInt64("id")) (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/issue_label.go:181) without constraining the ID to the route repository or its owning organisation, and the error branch distinguishes a missing label (422) from other failures (500), so an issue writer can probe label IDs of foreign repositories (CWE-203/CWE-639). The fix in f69e15afe7 replaces the lookup with GetLabelInRepoOrOrgByID(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository.ID, ctx.Repo.Owner.ID, ctx.Repo.Owner.IsOrganization(), labelID) and reports every error through ctx.APIErrorAuto, so a foreign ID is rejected exactly like a nonexistent one. v1.27.0 ships the scoped lookup; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The fix parent wraps the error in err.Error() while v1.25.5 passes err itself, so the 8-line span was read from the frozen file instead of matched as a pre-image.

goGet() looks the repository up by owner and name and, on success, writes repo.DefaultBranch into the go-import meta tag (frozen routers/web/goget.go:55-57) without any access check, so an unauthenticated caller learns the existence and default branch of a private repository (CWE-200/CWE-284). The fix in f69e15afe7 replaces the inline read with goGetDefaultBranch(ctx, repo), which returns the neutral instance default unless the caller can read the repository: it loads the owner, checks goGetTokenCanReadRepo (token scope), public-only confinement, code-read permission and owner visibility. v1.27.0 ships the helper; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

runSync() resolves the mirror remote URL once with gitrepo.GitRemoteGetURL() and passes it to proxy.EnvWithProxy(remoteURL.URL) and the git fetch command (frozen services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:272) without re-checking the migration allow/block lists; a mirror whose hostname now resolves to an internal address (DNS rebinding) or an instance whose allow list changed after the mirror was created is fetched anyway, giving server-side request forgery (the second SSRF of the same CVE record; CWE-284 per the CVE record). The fix in f69e15afe7 re-validates the remote URL on every sync with migrations.IsMigrateURLAllowed() for the http/https/git schemes and aborts the sync on a rejected host. v1.27.0 ships the re-validation; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA page for this CVE is not published; the CWE and CVSS v3 vector come from the CVE/OSV record.

When updateRepository() flips a repository from public to private it clears the stars in the `if repo.IsPrivate` block (frozen services/repository/repository.go :316 ClearRepoStars) but never clears the watches, so users who watched the public repository keep receiving activity and metadata for the now-private one (CWE-200/CWE-281/CWE-359). This is the API EditRepo path of the GHSA-8fwc-qjw5-rvgp fix, which had only been applied to the web path. The fix in f69e15afe7 adds the matching repo_model.ClearRepoWatches(ctx, repo.ID) call next to ClearRepoStars. v1.27.0 ships the watch clearing; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

ToHook() reads the stored webhook secret with w.HeaderAuthorization() (frozen services/webhook/general.go:407) and copies it into the API response as api.Hook.AuthorizationHeader (frozen line 419), so anyone who can list the hooks receives the authorization header in plaintext (CWE-200). The fix in f69e15afe7 removes the read and sets AuthorizationHeader: "" in the returned structure, matching the policy already applied to the webhook secret. v1.27.0 ships the redaction; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The fix parent already carries the Name: field in the api.Hook literal and the frozen tree does not, so the span was read from the frozen file (secret read at 407-410, leaking field at 419) instead of matched as a pre-image.

GET /orgs/{org}/members is registered with only reqToken() and ListMembers() serves it through listMembers() with no organization-visibility check (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:1644-1648; routers/api/v1/org/member.go:93), so any authenticated user can enumerate all members of a private organization (CWE-200/CWE-863). Fix 122ebcf0 attaches reqOrgVisible() to the /members and /public_members groups (which 404s when HasOrgOrUserVisible is false) and drops the now-redundant per-handler checks from member.go. v1.27.0 ships the gate; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

GetTeamRepos() calls repo_model.GetTeamRepositories with a SearchTeamRepoOptions that carries only ListOptions and TeamID (frozen routers/api/v1/org/team.go:562-564), and ListTeamActivityFeeds sets IncludePrivate: true without ApplyPublicOnly (frozen line 867), so a public-only token receives private team repository metadata and private activity entries (CWE-863). GET /teams/{id}/repos/{org}/{repo} likewise returned private repo metadata without ctx.TokenCanAccessRepo. Fix f452c369 adds PublicOnly: ctx.PublicOnly to the search options/count and TokenCanAccessRepo to the single-repo handler, and calls opts.ApplyPublicOnly(ctx.PublicOnly) on the feed options. v1.27.0 ships all three; the frozen v1.25.5 tree ships none.

AddTeamRepository() only requires access_model.AccessLevel >= admin before calling repo_service.TeamAddRepository (frozen routers/api/v1/org/team.go:682-689) and never consults the organization setting RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess, while the repo-side team routes do check it (routers/api/v1/repo/teams.go:190). A repository admin of a non-owner organization can therefore link the repository to a team even when the organization disabled repository-admin team access (CWE-862). Fix aab3242f adds canChangeTeamRepository() (setting OR org owner) and calls it in AddTeamRepository and RemoveTeamRepository. v1.27.0 ships the guard; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA page is a 404; the row is sourced from the CVE/OSV record (CWE-862, CVSS vector published without a score).

BatchHandler() auto-links an existing LFS object to the requested repository when git_model.LFSObjectAccessible(ctx, ctx.Doer, p.Oid) reports the claimed user can read it (frozen services/lfs/server.go:267-284); for deploy keys ctx.Doer is the repository owner (routers/private/serv.go sets results.UserID = repo.OwnerID), so a write deploy key for one repository yields the owner identity and can pull LFS objects from every repository that owner can see (CWE-266/CWE-639). Fix 66a3723c removes the cross-repo accessibility shortcut in BatchHandler and UploadHandler and requires proof of possession: an object not already linked to this repository must be uploaded and hash-verified. v1.27.0 ships the check; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

HookPostReceive() applies the repo.private and repo.template push options to any existing repository (frozen routers/private/hook_post_receive.go:210-225), updating is_private/is_template through UpdateRepositoryColsNoAutoTime, so a repository owner or admin collaborator can flip visibility with a plain git push and bypass the audit log, webhook events, team re-sync and watcher notifications that a settings change triggers (CWE-284). Fix f452c369 returns early unless repo.IsEmpty, confining the options to push-to-create. v1.27.0 ships the guard; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

RemoveDependency() checks only the current repository's CanCreateIssueDependencies (frozen routers/web/repo/issue_dependency.go:99) and then deletes the dependency row by depID (frozen line 133) without verifying that the doer can read the dependency's repository, so an attacker who can post the form in a repository they control can remove cross-repository links belonging to private repositories they cannot access (CWE-862). Fix aab3242f inserts a GetDoerRepoPermission + CanReadIssuesOrPulls check for issue.RepoID != dep.RepoID before issues_model.RemoveIssueDependency. v1.27.0 ships the check; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not. The GHSA publishes low severity without a score; the CVSS vector is taken from the CVE record.

GetPullRequests() in the restore-repo path validates each pull against the dump with CheckAndEnsureSafePR(pr, "", r) (frozen services/migrations/restore.go:238); strings.HasPrefix(x, "") is always true, so the check silently accepts any Head.CloneURL and services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go later runs git remote add + fetch against that dump-supplied URL (CWE-918). Fix aab3242f passes "file://"+r.baseDir as the common base URL (and hasBaseURL now rejects an empty base), so a cloneURL outside the dump is cleared before the uploader runs. v1.27.0 ships the check; the frozen v1.25.5 tree calls it with "". The fix parent also carries the #38215 PatchURL guard, so the span was read from the frozen file.

checkByAllowBlockList() starts ipAllowed at false and ORs each resolved address (frozen services/migrations/migrate.go:89-94), so a hostname whose DNS answer contains one allow-listed address and one blocked/internal address passes validation whenever the host name itself is not allow-listed; Init() also never adds private/loopback networks to the block list when AllowLocalNetworks=false (frozen lines 494-497) (CWE-918/CWE-200). Fix aab3242f starts ipAllowed from len(addrList) > 0, ANDs the allow-list match across every address, returns the blocked error immediately, and appends the private/loopback matchers to the block list in the else branch. v1.27.0 ships the hardened logic; the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not.

Clone() builds its git clone command without disabling HTTP redirects (frozen modules/git/repo.go:141), so a migration URL that passes IsMigrateURLAllowed can redirect the clone to a blocked or internal Git endpoint and exfiltrate that repository; the pull-mirror fetch/prune/remote-update commands (frozen services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:117-125) behaved the same way on scheduled syncs (CWE-918). Fix 9e84deb9 adds -c http.followRedirects=false to the clone command and 97078b96 adds the same config to mirror fetch, prune and remote update. v1.27.0 ships both; the frozen v1.25.5 tree ships neither.

The refresh_token branch of the OAuth2 token endpoint parses the submitted token and only checks that it parses (frozen routers/web/auth/oauth2_provider.go:548 `if err != nil`), never that its kind is a refresh token, so an unexpired access token for the same application and grant can be exchanged for a new access and refresh token and outlive its original lifetime (CWE-287). Fix 89363035105 (and backport 2d58c8c3) requires token.Kind == KindRefreshToken. The fixed release postdates the v1.27.0 tag, so the check is the marker added by the patch.

The built-in SSH server authenticates by looking the presented key up with `content LIKE ?` (frozen models/asymkey/ssh_key.go:145), which is case-insensitive on SQLite and other databases, so a case variant of another user's registered RSA key whose private key the attacker can derive matches the victim account (CWE-287). Fix 448f8c67 requires the key to be looked up by fingerprint (SearchPublicKeyForSSH). The fixed release postdates v1.27.0, so the evidence is the fingerprint lookup the patch adds in place of the LIKE comparison.

serveBlob sends the blob with a Content-Type taken from the manifest-declared media type, both as the S3 presign `response-content-type` and as the response header (frozen routers/api/packages/container/container.go:708 and :717), so a user who can push images can serve HTML/JavaScript from the Gitea origin and run script against an authenticated victim (CWE-79). Fix 71065941 makes the caller pass an explicit content type (blobs always application/octet-stream, manifests only a valid media type). The fix parent drifted (OpenBlobForDownload now takes ServeDirectOptions), so the anchor was read from the frozen file.

NewGiteaDownloader trusts the source server's max_response_items as the page size that ends its paginated downloads (frozen services/migrations/gitea_downloader.go:110-112), so a source that reports 0 makes the loops never terminate and exhausts server memory from one migration request (CWE-400/CWE-835). Fix 89363035105 only uses the value when it is positive and caps it at 100. The fixed release postdates v1.27.0; the marker is the added condition.

POST /{owner}/{repo}/tags/delete requires only Code write and shares the release deletion handler: deleteReleaseOrTag calls DeleteReleaseByID with isDelTag=true for whatever release id is submitted (frozen routers/web/repo/release.go:654) without checking that the target is a plain tag, so a collaborator without Releases write can destroy published releases and their attachments (CWE-732/CWE-863). Fix 89363035105 refuses when isDelTag and !rel.IsTag. The fixed release postdates v1.27.0; the marker is the inserted guard.

attachmentBelongsToRepoOrIssue only rejects attachments with IssueID == 0 (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/issue_attachment.go:389), so the issue-scoped attachment API also accepts attachments that belong to comments on the issue; the issue author, who may edit and delete the issue's own attachments, can then rename or delete other users' comment attachments (CWE-639/CWE-863). Fix 89363035105 also rejects CommentID != 0. The fixed release postdates v1.27.0; the marker is the widened condition.

checkByAllowBlockList accepts a hostname that matches ALLOWED_DOMAINS without requiring any resolved address to pass the local-network block list (frozen services/migrations/migrate.go:101 `if !allowList.MatchHostName(hostName) && !ipAllowed`), and when LookupIP yields nothing the address side is vacuously satisfied, so an allow-listed hostname that resolves (via the proxy path or DNS rebinding) to loopback or a private address reaches internal services though ALLOW_LOCALNETWORKS is false (CWE-918). Fix 1b1274486c40 replaces the lookup with egress.NewMigrationPolicy().CheckHostIPs, which validates the addresses actually used. The fix deletes the whole helper, so the anchor was read from the frozen file.

listUserRepos builds a SearchRepoOptions with only Actor/Private/ListOptions (frozen routers/api/v1/user/repo.go:25-29) and never applies the public-only restriction, so a public-only token reading /api/v1/user or /users/{name}/repos receives private repositories (CWE-863). The same omission existed in the starred and watched lists. Fix f2a1271f builds the options in a variable and calls searchOpts.ApplyPublicOnly(ctx.PublicOnly) in all three handlers. v1.25.5 is inside the stated range; v1.26.2, which postdates the snapshot and the v1.27.0 tag, ships the guard.

checkTokenPublicOnly is a value-less `switch` over ContainsCategory, so it enforces only the first scope category the token carries and silently skips the rest (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:274-314); combined with /user/orgs not applying the public-only filter to its query, a public-only token still reads non-public organizations, the incomplete fix of CVE-2025-68941 (CWE-862). Fix f2a1271f loops over every required category and also applies ApplyPublicOnly to the user-org listing. v1.25.5 is inside the range; the guard ships in v1.26.2, after v1.27.0.

The web archive endpoints call the archiver service without checking the API token scope that the corresponding API route enforces (frozen routers/web/repo/repo.go:367 in Download, and the same shape in InitiateDownload), so a token without repository scope can still download a private archive (CWE-863). Fix c3d9d077 inserts `if !checkDownloadTokenScope(ctx) { return }` in both handlers. v1.26.2 ships it, after the frozen tag.

ParsePackageInfo appends every `provides` and `depend` line of the decompressed .PKGINFO to the package metadata (frozen modules/packages/alpine/metadata.go:188 and :192) without any entry bound, and the size quota is enforced only after parsing, so a small highly compressed .apk expands into a disproportionate number of strings held in memory and can exhaust the process (CWE-400). The fix adds maxPackageInfoEntries = 1024 and returns ErrPackageInfoTooLarge once the combined count reaches it.

findActionKeywords runs the close/reopen keyword regular expressions over content[:start] for every reference found (frozen modules/references/references.go:572 and :578), so a body with many Markdown links costs time quadratic in its length and one ~1 MB issue or comment keeps a CPU core busy for minutes inside a database transaction (CWE-407). The fix computes issueKeywordWindow from the longest keyword and scans only a bounded prefix ending at the reference.

The Gitignores field of the repository-creation API and web form carries no length bound (frozen modules/structs/repo.go:143, services/forms/repo_form.go:29), while initialization splits it into template names and reads and buffers each referenced template, so an oversized value amplifies work and memory for anyone who can create repositories (CWE-400). The fix adds binding MaxSize(1024) to both declarations.

The POST /repos/migrate route is registered with reqToken() only (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:1186), so a public-only token can submit MigrateRepoOptions with private=true and create a private repository and migration task, unlike the ordinary private-creation route (CWE-863). The fix inserts rejectPublicOnly() in the /migrate chain and adds the repository scope requirement to the organization repo-creation route.

individualPermsChecker admits any signed-in doer to a Limited-visibility individual (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:870-882 only rejects an anonymous doer), and its user-data group did not run the checker at all, so a restricted account reads activity feeds and contribution heatmaps that the profile routes hide (CWE-200). The fix delegates to user_model.IsUserVisibleToViewer, which applies the restricted-viewer rule, and attaches the checker to the users/{username} routes.

oauth2LinkAccount decides whether the second factor is pending with auth.GetTwoFactorByUID (frozen routers/web/auth/linkaccount.go:181), which does not consider WebAuthn credentials and is deliberately not replaced by the skip-local-2FA setting there, so a WebAuthn-only account signing in through an external identity flow links the identity and gets a full session without a passkey challenge (CWE-287). The fix uses auth.HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn and a shared handleTwoFactorRequired, and the same commit moves WebAuthn user verification to a per-request setting instead of VerificationDiscouraged.

When the hook pipeline resolves the pusher it looks up opts.PusherID as a user (frozen services/repository/push.go:113 for tag refs and :160 for branches; the pusher was already populated with the repository owner by the SSH/HTTP layer for deploy keys), so protected-tag allow lists and push-option permission checks evaluate the owner instead of the deploy key, letting a writable deploy key create protected tags and flip repository visibility (CWE-863). The fix resolves the pusher through user_model.GetPossibleUserByID, which distinguishes deploy keys from user ids.

When the named new owner lacks access, StartRepositoryTransfer grants temporary read access by adding a collaborator (frozen services/repository/transfer.go:452), but rejecting or cancelling the pending transfer only resets the repository status, so the recipient keeps persistent read access to the private repository and can clone it (CWE-672/CWE-863). The fix records RecipientAccessGranted on the pending transfer and calls removeTransferRecipientCollaboration on accept and on reject/cancel, which deletes only that read collaboration.

ShowRepoFeed renders the repository activity feed after only the normal context checks (frozen routers/web/feed/repo.go:19) and never runs the API token scope check that the corresponding API routes perform, so a token without repository scope reads private repository commit data from the .rss/.atom feed (CWE-863). The fix adds checkRepoFeedTokenScope, which wraps context.CheckRepoScopedToken, to the repo, branch, file and release feeds.

When an issue search is not restricted to accessible repositories, applyRepoConditions adds only the is_private=false condition (frozen models/issues/issue_search.go:231), which ignores the owner visibility that profile and repository listings apply, so a restricted account searches titles and bodies of issues owned by Limited-visibility users and can confirm hidden content by keyword (CWE-200). The fix uses repo_model.PublicRepoUnderPublicOwnerCond, which also filters by owner visibility, in issue search and in the public-repository condition helper.

CreatePushMirror validates the remote address with migrations.IsMigrateURLAllowed(address, ctx.ContextUser), where ContextUser is the repository owner (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:347), so a repository administrator who may not import local paths can create a push mirror to a server path when the owner may, and Gitea pushes the repository into the Git repository at that path (CWE-863). The fix passes ctx.Doer, the caller, so the local-path permission is evaluated for the requesting user.

AddPushMirror rejects the request only when the mirror feature is globally disabled (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:286 follows `if !setting.Mirror.Enabled`) and does not honour [mirror] DISABLE_NEW_PUSH, which the web handler enforces, so a repository administrator can still create push mirrors that send every ref to a caller-chosen remote (CWE-863). The fix returns 403 when setting.Mirror.DisableNewPush before reading the form.

showUserFeed starts from the includePrivate expression (frozen routers/web/feed/profile.go:31) with no visibility check on the profile owner, and the Accept: application/rss+xml or atom+xml path on GET /{username} reaches it directly, so anonymous, restricted and non-member viewers read limited/private users and private organizations activity even when ENABLE_FEED is off (CWE-200/CWE-863). The fix returns 404 unless ENABLE_FEED is set and the owner is visible to the doer.

PullRequestReview builds its notification with newNotifyInput(review.Issue.Repo, ...).WithRef(review.CommitID) (frozen services/actions/notifier.go:461) and never attaches the pull request, so run.isForkPullRequest() is false for workflows triggered by pull_request_review and pull_request_review_comment events and the first-time-fork-contributor approval gate is skipped, letting fork-controlled workflow code run on the base repository runners (CWE-863). The fix adds newPullRequestReviewNotifyInput, which sets WithPullRequest(pr).

The Basic authenticator accepts an OAuth2 access token as a password and only reads its user id (`_, uid := GetOAuthAccessTokenScopeAndUserID(...)`, frozen services/auth/basic.go:78), then stores LoginMethod/IsApiToken but never the token scope, unlike the personal-access-token branch below it, so the scope checks that read ApiTokenScope see an unrestricted token and a scoped OAuth2 token keeps full account permissions (CWE-284/CWE-863). The fix keeps the scope returned by GetOAuthAccessTokenScopeAndUserID and stores it in ApiTokenScope.

runHookPreReceive reads the pre-receive input with a bufio.Scanner and, when the input exceeds the batch buffer or the read fails, leaves the loop at the frozen `if count > 0` (cmd/hook.go:280) without inspecting scanner.Err(), so it processes the truncated prefix and can miss branch-protection rules for the remaining refs (CWE-703). The fix fails closed with "scanner error" after the loop in both the old-commit and new-commit passes.

GetWorkflowBadge renders the latest workflow status (frozen routers/web/repo/actions/badge.go:20) with only the web context checks and no API token scope check, so a token without repository read scope, or one restricted to public repositories, retrieves the workflow status of a private repository its owner can access (CWE-863). The fix calls context.CheckRepoScopedToken with Read before serving the badge.

parseCompareInfo resolves the head repository and compares owners (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go:1094 `isSameRepo := ctx.Repo.Owner.ID == headUser.ID`) without applying the token repository-access check used when updating a pull request, so a public-only token with read:repository reads commit history and diffs of a private head repository through /compare or pull-request creation with a public base (CWE-863). The fix rejects the request when !ctx.TokenCanAccessRepo(headRepo); 920b5f1e is the mainline fix and 320b44df its backport.

CanMaintainerWriteToBranch walks the open PRs from the head info and returns true when any has AllowMaintainerEdit and the doer can write the base repository (frozen models/issues/pull_list.go:90-116), never checking that the PR poster can write the head repository, so the maintainer-edit path authorizes commits to head repositories the doer can only read (CWE-863). The fix requires the poster to have code write on the head repository and the doer to have code write on the base repository, and the web blame/diff UI now calls the same helper. 926280362172 is the mainline fix and 74e515623bcf its backport.

PullRequestCodeOwnersReview evaluates every CODEOWNERS rule against every changed file with regexp2 and no time bound (frozen services/issue/pull.go:118), and CODEOWNERS is read from the pushed content, so a crafted pattern with catastrophic backtracking keeps a CPU core busy and blocks PR creation without authentication (CWE-407). The fix sets a 150 ms MatchTimeout per compiled rule and a 2 s aggregate budget across the rules x files loop, breaking out when it is exceeded.

DoerViewOtherVisibility returns Private, Limited or Public from the admin/self and nil checks only (frozen models/organization/org_list.go:80-86) and never lowers the visibility for a restricted viewer, so the user organization-list API and the profile org list return Limited-visibility organizations, names, descriptions and avatars to a restricted account even though the single-organization endpoint hides them (CWE-200/CWE-863). The fix returns VisibleTypePublic for doer.IsRestricted.

The /api/v1/orgs route registers org.GetAll as the handler and appends tokenRequiresScopes(...) as the *last* middleware (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:1636), and Gitea runs handler middleware before the chain middleware that the discovery builder orders, so the scope check never runs and a token limited to another category, such as read:misc, reads organization metadata; an administrator token also returns Limited and private organizations (CWE-285). The fix moves tokenRequiresScopes into front position and also applies it to the admin-only and user-orgs variants.

changeRepoTeam authorizes team link and unlink with !ctx.Repo.Owner.RepoAdminChangeTeamAccess && !ctx.Repo.IsOwner() (frozen routers/api/v1/repo/teams.go:190; the fix parent spells it ctx.Repo.Permission.IsOwner()), which treats a repository administrator who is not an organization owner as allowed whenever the organization disables REPO_ADMIN_CHANGE_TEAM_ACCESS, so such an admin changes which organization teams receive repository access (CWE-266/CWE-863). The fix routes both the API and the web setting through Organization.CanChangeRepoTeamAccess, which requires ownership unless the setting allows repository admins.

renderRepoIssueIconTitle loads the issue and only re-checks CanReadIssuesOrPulls when the referenced repository differs from the repository of the request (frozen services/markup/renderhelper_issueicontitle.go:45-52, which calls access.GetUserRepoPermission and checks perms), so a member who can read the repository but lacks the Issues/Pull Requests unit, for example Wiki-only access, sees private pull request titles and state icons through the markup preview (CWE-863). The fix starts from webCtx.Repo.Permission, reassigns it only for cross-repository references, and applies the check unconditionally.

ParsePackage rejects a manifest entry larger than maxManifestFileSize (frozen modules/packages/swift/metadata.go:130) but iterates every matching zip entry and reads each one into memory with no cap on the number of manifests or their aggregate uncompressed size, so a highly compressed package with many manifests allocates far more than the upload and exhausts memory (CWE-400). The fix rejects archives above maxManifestFiles (64) or maxManifestSize before reading them.

The organization repository-creation route is registered as Post(reqToken(), bind(api.CreateRepoOption{}), repo.CreateOrgRepo) (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:1643) and requires only write:organization, while every other repository-creation route also requires the repository token scope, so a token without repository-write scope creates organization-owned repositories when its user may (CWE-863). The fix adds tokenRequiresScopes(auth_model.AccessTokenScopeCategoryRepository) to the route (the same commit also adds rejectPublicOnly to /migrate, which is CVE-2026-70400, promoted in batch 5 from the backport).

createDelegateHooks creates the <hook>.d directory with os.ModePerm (0777) and writes both hook scripts with 0o777 (frozen modules/gitrepo/hooks.go:121, 139 and 150), relying on the process umask, so with a permissive umask another local user who can reach the repository storage adds or replaces a delegate hook that Gitea later executes as the service account (CWE-732). The fix uses 0o755 for the directory and both scripts and chmods the directory explicitly; the fix commit moves the file to modules/git/hooks.go while the frozen path is modules/gitrepo/hooks.go.

syncGitConfig sets core.commitGraph and the other runtime options but never enables object consistency checks (frozen modules/git/config.go:56), so a push can store a tree with two entries of the same name, which Git considers inconsistent: the web diff and file views resolve the first entry while checkout, Gitea Actions and release archives use the last, letting a contributor show benign content in review while CI executes attacker-controlled content (CWE-436). The fix sets transfer.fsckObjects=true, with the Gitaly ignore list for harmless historic objects, for every repository.

getStarredRepos converts every starred repository for the requesting user after only loading the individual permission (frozen routers/api/v1/user/star.go:34-38 writes repos[i] = convert.ToRepo(...)) and never drops entries the user can no longer access, and the tracked-time handlers in routers/api/v1/repo/issue_tracked_time.go likewise return stored times without a current permission check, so a user whose access to a private repository was revoked still reads its metadata through /api/v1/user/starred and private issue titles through /api/v1/user/times (CWE-863). The fix skips repositories without HasAnyUnitAccessOrPublicAccess and filters tracked times the same way.

handleWorkflows decides whether a fork pull request run needs approval by calling ifNeedApproval with input.Doer, the user who triggered the event (frozen services/actions/notifier_helper.go:341), so a maintainer triaging a fork pull request (adding a label, for example) has write permission and the run is created without approval even though the workflow definition comes from the fork head (CWE-441/CWE-863). The fix collects the event actor and the pull request author through getApprovalUsers and requires approval if any of them does.

RegisterOpenIDPost registers the account with the submitted password and immediately calls user_model.AddUserOpenID (frozen routers/web/auth/openid.go:370) without checking whether the user has TOTP or WebAuthn enrolled, and the existing account sign-in branch calls handleSignIn the same way, so an attacker who knows the password links an attacker-controlled identifier and afterwards signs in with it without the password or the second factor, surviving a password change (CWE-304/CWE-696). The fix adds openIDRequireTwoFactor, which calls auth_model.HasTwoFactorOrWebAuthn and routes through handleTwoFactorRequired, storing openidPendingURI so the identifier is attached only after the second factor succeeds.

Clone builds its git clone command without disabling HTTP redirects (frozen modules/git/repo.go:141), so the migration endpoint validates the submitted clone address with IsMigrateURLAllowed and then lets git follow a 302 from that public host to 127.0.0.1 or an RFC1918 address, importing an internal repository into a repository the attacker owns (CWE-918). This is a second CVE (GHSA-rqhx-647v-wx32, 1.26.x train) for the same defect already promoted as CVE-2026-57894 (GHSA-82f7-87hm-852x, 1.27.0); both advisories cite the same 9e84deb9 hunk and both cover v1.25.5, so this row records the second advisory against the frozen line. The fix adds -c http.followRedirects=false to the clone command.

ToNotificationThread converts a notification repository only when the user still has access (frozen services/convert/notification.go:33) but falls through to the subject switch in every case, so a user whose access to a private repository was revoked still receives the private issue or pull request title, the API and HTML URLs, the state and the latest-comment URLs through /api/v1/notifications/threads (CWE-200). The fix returns early when the permission check fails, so neither the repository nor the subject is populated.

handleOAuth2SignIn sets opts.IsActive = optional.Some(true) for every inactive user (frozen routers/web/auth/oauth.go:351-354), and the frozen v1.25.5 tree does not even contain the #38009 refresh-token gate, so an administrator-deactivated account is reactivated and receives a full session the next time it signs in through any OAuth2 source, including GitHub and OIDC sources without offline_access (CWE-863). The fix requires the auto-sync signature (access token, refresh token and expiry all cleared) before reactivating, which the cron that disables users on invalid_grant is the only writer of.

FindRenderizableReferenceRegexp assumes capture group 2 always participated in the match and slices content with match[2]:match[3] (frozen modules/references/references.go:381-383), so an external issue-tracker pattern whose alternatives place the reference in a later group, for example (A-(\d+)|B-(\d+)), yields -1 and panics with an invalid slice index whenever matching content is rendered, crashing the instance for every user (CWE-129). The fix scans the group pairs for the first group that participated and returns nil when none did.

When the install form is reachable against a database that already has users, SubmitInstall creates the admin account with CreateUser and, on ErrUserAlreadyExist, loads the existing user of that name and then creates an auth token and sets the session cookie for it (frozen routers/install/install.go:545-573, with the "Admin account already exist" branch at 553-554) without ever verifying the submitted password, so anyone who can reset INSTALL_LOCK to false and reach the installer becomes an existing administrator (CWE-287/CWE-863). The fix rejects a non-empty AdminName when db_install.HasPostInstallationUsers reports users, and also requires the reinstall confirmation for single-user databases.

individualPermsChecker only rejects anonymous callers in its api.VisibleTypeLimited branch (frozen routers/api/v1/api.go:877-881), so any signed-in restricted account can call /api/v1/users/{username}/keys and /api/v1/users/{username}/gpg_keys for a Limited-visibility user and read public keys, key titles, fingerprints and the e-mail addresses embedded in GPG keys, which the web equivalents do not disclose (CWE-200/CWE-863). The fix replaces the inline visibility switch with user_model.IsUserVisibleToViewer, which treats a restricted viewer as unable to see a Limited user, and applies the checker to the route group that carries the key endpoints.

Verify hands the caller-supplied OpenID endpoint to the openid-go library, which performs server-side discovery and an assertion POST with Go's default client (frozen modules/auth/openid/openid.go:26), so an unauthenticated attacker points the identifier at an internal HTTP service reachable from the Gitea host and uses the server as a blind SSRF proxy (CWE-918). The fix constructs the library with an http.Client whose transport is hostmatcher.NewHTTPTransport backed by security.ALLOWED_HOST_LIST, and uses it for both Verify and RedirectURL.

storeAtts measures the local part with an int counter (`for (i = 0; localPart[i++];)`) and then combines it with the binding URI length for an allocation, so a namespace URI or local part longer than INT_MAX wraps the total length and the copy writes past the allocation (CWE-190). The fix counts in size_t, rejects values above INT_MAX, and checks the multiplication and addition before memcpy.

addBinding counts the URI length in an int loop (`for (len = 0; uri[len]; len++)`) and adds one for the namespace separator without bounding the counter, so a namespace URI close to INT_MAX overflows the subsequent allocation size (CWE-190). The fix rejects len == INT_MAX inside the loop and before the separator increment.

getAttributeId scans a prefixed attribute name with an int index (`for (i = 0; name[i]; i++)`) and uses that index for pool appends without a bound, so a name longer than INT_MAX overflows the counter and the prefix length it feeds (CWE-190). The fix rejects i == INT_MAX inside the scan loop.

XML_ParseBuffer adds the caller-supplied len to m_bufferEnd/m_parseEndByteIndex without the overflow check XML_Parse performs, so a large len wraps the byte index and the parser reads past the buffer (CWE-190). The fix copies the length check from XML_Parse into XML_ParseBuffer before the buffer pointers are advanced.

doProlog stores an entity replacement text length by casting the pool length to int (`textLen = (int)(poolLength(&dtd->entityValuePool))`) without bounding it, so an entity value longer than INT_MAX truncates the length the entity declaration handler receives (CWE-190). The fix rejects pool lengths above INT_MAX in both doProlog and storeEntityValue.

copyString computes the character count, multiplies it by sizeof(XML_Char), and allocates without checking the multiplication, so a string long enough to make the product wrap yields a short allocation and the following memcpy overflows it (CWE-190). The fix rejects charsRequired > SIZE_MAX / sizeof(XML_Char) before the allocation.

xmlwf joins -d outputDir and the input file name into a malloc size by adding both lengths and 2 without guarding either the addition or the multiplication, so long operator-supplied paths wrap the size and the following tcscpy/tcscat write past the buffer (CWE-190). The fix lengths both strings once and guards the sum and the product before allocating.

resolveSystemId sizes the joined external-entity path with `(tcslen(base) + tcslen(systemId) + 2) * sizeof(XML_Char)` and no overflow guard, so a base or system identifier close to SIZE_MAX wraps the allocation and the subsequent tcscpy/tcscat overflow it (CWE-190). The fix computes the length once, guards the sum per operator and guards the multiplication.

endDoctypeDecl counts NOTATION declarations into an int and multiplies the count by sizeof(NotationList *) for the sort array without a multiplication guard, so a DTD with a huge notation list wraps the size and the fill loop writes past the allocation (CWE-190). The fix counts in size_t and rejects counts above SIZE_MAX / sizeof pointer before malloc.

The DTD scaffolding index is reallocated to the calling parser's private m_groupSize (`REALLOC(parser, dtd->scaffIndex, parser->m_groupSize * sizeof(int))`) even though the DTD is shared with external-entity sub-parsers, so a shallower sub-parser shrinks the array and the parent's next element-content write lands past it (CWE-821/CWE-787). The fix tracks the array size in the shared DTD and grows it by a guarded doubling, never down.

basis: dtdCopy sizes the copy of an element type's default attributes with `oldE->nDefaultAtts * sizeof(DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTE)` where nDefaultAtts is an int, so on 32-bit platforms (UINT_MAX == SIZE_MAX) a DTD declaring more than UINT_MAX/sizeof(DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTE) defaults wraps the multiplication and the following copy writes past the allocation (CWE-190). The fix rejects counts above (size_t)-1 / sizeof(DEFAULT_ATTRIBUTE) before the malloc; the guard is compiled out on 64-bit platforms, which is why the advisory limits the issue to 32-bit builds.

nextScaffoldPart allocates the scaffold index with `MALLOC(parser, parser->m_groupSize * sizeof(int))` where m_groupSize is an unsigned int, so on 32-bit platforms a content model that drives m_groupSize above UINT_MAX/sizeof(int) wraps the size and the zero-initialisation writes past the allocation (CWE-190). The fix rejects m_groupSize above (size_t)-1 / sizeof(int) before the malloc; the guard is compiled out on 64-bit platforms.

doContent grows the tag-name buffer with `bufSize = (int)(tag->bufEnd - tag->buf) << 1`, an int shift that has no overflow check, so a tag name long enough to make the shift wrap produces a small or negative bufSize, REALLOC returns a short buffer and the converter keeps writing into it (CWE-190/CWE-787). The fix computes the size in size_t and returns XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY when size > SIZE_MAX / 2.

The UTF-16 encodings report a 4-byte character (BT_LEAD4) for a high surrogate but never verify that the next code unit is a low surrogate: xmltok_impl.c falls back to `#define IS_INVALID_CHAR(enc, ptr, n) (0)` for them and the little2/big2 vtables carry NULL for isInvalid4 (frozen expat/lib/xmltok.c:825). A lone high surrogate therefore consumes the following code unit, so a following `<` is hidden from the tokenizer and unpaired surrogates reach XML_UNICODE applications (CWE-20). The fix adds LITTLE2_IS_INVALID_CHAR/BIG2_IS_INVALID_CHAR and swaps NULL_VTABLE for UTF16_NULL_VTABLE, whose isInvalid4 is real. The fix site is a file-scope vtable initializer, hence no enclosing function.

Hash flooding protection derives the SipHash key from m_hash_secret_salt, an unsigned long of 4 bytes on ILP32 and 8 bytes elsewhere, and copy_salt_to_sipkey puts that single word in k[1] with k[0] = 0 (frozen expat/lib/xmlparse.c:7156-7157). SipHash accepts 16 bytes, so only 32 to 64 bits of the key are unknown and a crafted document can collide hash-table entries to degrade parsing to quadratic time (CWE-331/CWE-407). The fix stores a full struct sipkey in m_hash_secret_salt_128, fills 16 bytes of entropy, and adds XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes; the removed k[0] = 0 / k[1] = get_hash_secret_salt(parser) pair is the pre-image.

basis: DEFINE_UTF16_TO_UTF16 holds back a trailing surrogate pair as XML_CONVERT_INPUT_INCOMPLETE when the previous two bytes look like a high surrogate, and tests that with `& 0xF8`, which also accepts the low-surrogate range 0xDC00..0xDFFF. A document ending in a lone low surrogate therefore never completes: storeAttributeValue keeps asking for more input, reads past the supplied buffer and loops (CWE-125). The fix narrows the mask to 0xFC so only 0xD800..0xDBFF count as high surrogates, and relaxes the exit condition in storeAttributeValue accordingly. Reported by Mozilla (bug 2053153).

XML_ParseBuffer performs no capacity check before `parser->m_bufferEnd += len`: the caller-supplied len is only compared with XML_INDEX_MAX through m_parseEndByteIndex after the pointers have already moved. Once an XML_GetBuffer call has installed a buffer, a second XML_ParseBuffer call with a len larger than the remaining capacity pushes m_bufferEnd past m_bufferLim, and callProcessor reads past the heap allocation (CWE-125). The fix rejects len > EXPAT_SAFE_PTR_DIFF(m_bufferLim, m_bufferEnd) with XML_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT before touching the pointers.

Curl_hsts() walks the HSTS cache and returns the first entry whose tail matches the requested hostname, without comparing the tail length. When x.example.com and example.com both exist in the cache, the subdomain entry (an includeSubDomains match) can be selected for the parent host, so the subdomain Strict-Transport-Security expiry and includeSubDomains bit are applied to example.com. The fix keeps the longest matching tail in `bestsub`/`blen` and also requires an exact host match when updating an existing entry in the parser.

Curl_sasl_start() reads STRING_BEARER unconditionally when the target protocol is IMAP, LDAP, POP3 or SMTP. After an HTTP(S) transfer with an OAuth2 bearer token is redirected to one of those schemes, the same token is offered to the new host even though it was issued for the first one. The fix only uses the bearer token when this is not a follow or when auth-to-other-hosts is explicitly permitted.

myssh_statemach_act() selects public-key authentication whenever the server offers it, then authenticates through whatever libssh finds, so a locally running SSH agent is used even when the caller asked for a private key only. The fix requires either CURLOPT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY or CURLSSH_AUTH_AGENT before taking the public-key branch, and otherwise keeps looking for an acceptable method.

gtls_send() passes the caller buffer and length straight to gnutls_record_send() and only ever rejects negative results. After a blocked send GnuTLS can report more bytes sent than were handed over; the WebSocket upload path then advances its offset past the buffer, reading heap memory beyond the send area. The fix compares the returned count with the requested `remain`, fails the transfer with CURLE_SEND_ERROR and logs the mismatch.

url_proto() parses the user URL with CURLU_GUESS_SCHEME and CURLU_DEFAULT_SCHEME, so for a schemeless URL the tool layer infers http or https instead of honouring --proto-default sftp/scp. The SSH options keyed off the inferred scheme (knownhosts, host public key SHA-256) are therefore never set, while libcurl really connects over SFTP/SCP because CURLOPT_DEFAULT_PROTOCOL is set, yielding an unverified SSH host. The fix (moved into config2setopts.c) parses with CURLU_NO_GUESS_SCHEME and falls back to the configured default protocol before tokenizing the scheme.

ConnectionExists() carries NTLM state checks but no equivalent for SPNEGO: a request authenticated with Negotiate can be paired with a pooled connection that is still mid-handshake or was authenticated with other credentials. The fix adds the NEGOTIATE counterpart (url_match_auth_nego) and consults want_nego_http / want_proxy_nego_http before accepting a reusable connection; the shipped commit corrects the copy-pasted NTLM flags in that new matcher.

Curl_http_auth_act() adds the bearer Authorization header whenever the picked auth is CURLAUTH_BEARER, without asking whether the current host may receive the credentials. On a redirect to a host present in .netrc (machine or default), the token set for the first host is passed to the second. The fix guards the bearer header with Curl_auth_allowed_to_host(), the same helper that gates other credential types.

socks_proxy_info_matches() compares the proxy host and port and then returns TRUE from the shared proxy_info_matches() without comparing the SOCKS proxy username and password. A CONNECT tunnel created with one set of proxy credentials is therefore reusable by a request that specifies another. The fix folds the credential comparison into the host-matching branch of proxy_info_matches() and drops the separate socks helper.

Curl_pretransfer() restores the request credentials inline before every transfer and always restores the proxy credentials of the previous request. When a redirect moves from a scheme served by an authenticated proxy to a scheme served by a different credential-less proxy, the first proxy's credentials are sent to the second. The fix splits the restore into Curl_reset_userpwd() and Curl_reset_proxypwd() and calls the proxy reset on every redirect hop in lib/http.c, so the new proxy sees only its own configured credentials.

Curl_hsts_parse() accepts any max-age up to TIME_T_MAX and stores it as an absolute expiry. An authenticated origin can then supply a value whose absolute time cannot be formatted; Curl_hsts_save() truncates the target file before serializing, hsts_out() fails on the entry, and the callers ignore the error, leaving an empty or partial HSTS cache. The fix caps max-age at two years (CAP_HSTS_MAX_AGE) at parse time, makes hsts_out() skip only the unformattable entry and return void, and stops treating the cleanup save as fatal.

imap_perform_append() derives the APPEND literal from Curl_mime_size() for MIME uploads and from the transfer upload size for plain files, neither of which accounts for the extra bytes added by CURLOPT_CRLF. curl then sends a `{N}` literal smaller than the data it writes, so the server consumes only N bytes and interprets the remaining transformed bytes as further IMAP commands inside the authenticated session. The fix (creader API, introduced after 8.3.0) sizes the literal from Curl_creader_total_length() and refuses APPEND outright when CRLF conversion makes the size unpredictable.

The ASN.1 parser compares a length byte read as `unsigned char` against `size_t` after promoting the parsed header fields, and the DER walking code stores byte offsets in `char *` pointers. A manipulated validity length field lets the second parse of the peer certificate extract a different public key than the TLS stack validated, so CURLOPT_PINNEDPUBLICKEY can be satisfied by a key the peer does not possess. The fix migrates the parser and the certinfo extraction paths to `const uint8_t *` and performs the length check on the unsigned byte, so the re-parsed view matches what the backend verified.

Curl_cookie_add() feeds the raw Domain attribute to psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable(), so `Domain=example.com.` with a trailing dot fails the public-suffix comparison against the host and is accepted as a domain cookie, producing a super cookie that is then sent to unrelated hosts. The fix trims trailing dots from both the request host and the cookie domain, lowercases them and re-runs the PSL and domain checks on the normalized names.

tool_header_cb() opens the remote-name output file as soon as the Content-Disposition header arrives, and the -J no-clobber check is only consulted once. A 103 Early Hints response or an ETag header processed by --etag-save before Content-Disposition makes curl decide the filename earlier, so a server can make it overwrite an existing file that -J promised not to touch. The fix buffers headers until the final response selects the filename and defers opening the output file until the content-disposition decision is complete.

GTime2str() accepts a fraction separator without a following digit and can compute fracl as -1; the value is later used as a length and a strlen() runs past a heap buffer that is not NUL-terminated. The fix advances past the separator explicitly and computes the fraction length from the timezone boundary only when the digits are present, rejecting a malformed timezone with a defined error.

The OpenSSL backend caches one X509_STORE per connection filter for reuse across transfers, keyed on the CA file and path but not on CURLSSLOPT_NO_PARTIALCHAIN. Calling curl_easy_setopt() to change that flag and reusing the handle or share keeps the previously configured store, so a partial chain can be accepted against the user's stated policy. The fix records no_partialchain in the cached-store bookkeeping, invalidates the store when it differs and copies the setting into the shared store.

CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS and CURLOPT_STREAM_DEPENDS_E build a libcurl-side tree of `data_priority` nodes in lib/url.c. curl_easy_reset() runs data_priority_cleanup() and frees the nodes, but the easy handle still participates in HTTP/2 priority updates and the cleanup path at curl_easy_cleanup() time walks them again, giving a use-after-free. The fix removes the dependency tree entirely (h2_pri_spec() always sends the default parent, the setopt cases accept but ignore the options and the tree helpers are deleted).

Curl_input_digest() keeps the Digest state in data->state.digest across transfers and never records which origin it was negotiated with. Reusing an easy handle for a second transfer to a different origin therefore keeps the cnonce/response material and sends the Authorization header meant for hostA to hostB. The fix stores the origin and credentials in the digest state, flushes it when the new destination differs, and unlinks both on cleanup.

oldap_perform_sasl() advances the LDAP state as soon as Curl_sasl_continue() returns any progress other than SASL_INPROGRESS, without distinguishing SASL_DONE from the failure and idle states. A man-in-the-middle can inject a premature challenge/response sequence and the client stops negotiating and proceeds as authenticated. The fix switches on the returned progress, marks the session authenticated only for SASL_DONE and aborts for the cancelled/idle results.

h2_duphandle() clones the HTTP/2 data for a duplicated easy handle but does not link the new handle to the parent share that owns the server-push bookkeeping. Push streams then hold references into the original handle's share structures; when the parent is freed the duplicate's cleanup walks released memory. The fix links the duplicate to data->share through Curl_share_easy_link() so the shared HTTP/2 state outlives either handle.

The reuse matcher in ConnectionExists() compares scheme families and the PROTOPT_SSL flag only, so a transfer that requires TLS via CURLOPT_USE_SSL (IMAP/SMTP/POP3 STARTTLS) can pick up an existing plaintext connection to the same host that was opened by an earlier non-TLS request. The fix adds a req_tls bit to the connection match, records it from CURLUSESSL_CONTROL/ALL, refuses to reuse connections that did not upgrade and refuses to reuse a TLS-upgraded connection for a non-TLS match.

ConnectionExists() accepts a pooled connection as the "upgrade candidate" when its NTLM state is idle, but never inspects the SPNEGO state. A request that asks for any auth method with different credentials can therefore reuse a connection that is mid-Negotiate or already authenticated with the previous credentials, and the new request rides the old security context. The fix adds the `negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE` condition next to the NTLM idle test of the candidate connection under USE_SPNEGO.

Curl_http_host() stores the custom Host header value in the request-scoped `state.aptr.cookiehost`, which is not reset by the per-request state cleanup, and Curl_http_cookies() consults it when choosing the cookie domain. A second transfer on the same easy handle without a custom Host header therefore keeps the first host as the cookie host and sends cookies belonging to it. The fix moves the value into `data->req.cookiehost`, frees it in the request cleanup and reads it through the same request pointer.

Curl_follow() clears the user/password it copied out of the request when a redirect changes port or scheme, but the .netrc path fills the credentials in later and the port/scheme comparison alone does not identify a host change. A redirect to a different host that keeps the same port and scheme therefore carries the first host's .netrc password. The fix (moved into lib/http.c by the time of the fix) compares the full origin with Curl_url_same_origin() and resets the credentials whenever the origin differs and auth-to-other-hosts is not allowed.

Setting CURLOPT_PROXY goes through setopt_cptr_proxy(), which only stores the new proxy string. The Digest proxy state kept in `data->state.proxydigest` and the negotiated `authproxy` bits are left untouched, so a fresh transfer through proxyB reuses the Proxy-Authorization digest material computed for proxyA. The fix routes the option through a setproxy() helper that compares the old and new proxy strings, and on a change clears the digest state and the proxy auth state before storing the new value.

servercert() reads the pin from `data->set.str[...PINNEDPUBLICKEY...]` directly. When the server presents no certificate and both CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER and CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST are 0, the function returns success before the pin is ever consulted, so an unauthenticated connection is accepted despite a configured pin. The fix factors the pin lookup into pinned() (proxy-aware, connection-scoped) and adds `!pinned(cf, data)` to the no-certificate acceptance test so a configured pin fails the connection.

The OpenSSL backend builds the X509 store from the handle-level `ssl_config->native_ca_store`, and the connection-reuse matcher in lib/url.c does not include the Native CA Store bit in the filter it compares. Flipping CURLSSLOPT_NATIVE_CA and issuing a second request to the same host reuses the existing connection and therefore the previously built trust store. The fix moves the setting into the connection configuration (`conn_config`), reads it in populate_x509_store()/Curl_ssl_setup_x509_store() and adds it to the connection match.

Curl_cookie_add() consults the Public Suffix List from the request host side, but a `Domain=` attribute that names the public suffix exactly (for example `Domain=co.uk` on a response from co.uk) passes with tailmatching still enabled, so libcurl stores a `.co.uk` domain cookie it then sends to attacker.co.uk. The fix adds is_public_suffix(): when the cookie domain is itself a public suffix the cookie is forced to host-only scope (tailmatch cleared), matching the PSL rule.

ConnectionExists() distinguishes SSL from non-SSL handlers with PROTOPT_SSL only, which says nothing about a clear-text protocol the new request wants to upgrade with STARTTLS. A second transfer that requires TLS can therefore reuse a pooled connection that was opened without the TLS options, or with different ones. The fix records may_tls and require_tls in the connection match from CURLOPT_USE_SSL, only reuses upgraded connections when the new request tolerates clear text and compares the SSL configuration when either side may upgrade.

Curl_sasl_start() derives the SASL/GSSAPI service name from the handle-level STRING_SERVICE_NAME, and the connection-reuse matcher never compares it. Two requests to the same host with different service names, or with the service changed between them, share one Negotiate-authenticated connection and the second request runs under the first service identity. The fix moves the service into the connection credentials (Curl_creds_*) and has both Curl_sasl_start()/Curl_sasl_continue() and the HTTP Negotiate/NTLM code read it from the connection.

The CURLOPT_AWS_SIGV4 case in Curl_vsetopt() sets httpauth to CURLAUTH_AWS_SIGV4 when the string is non-NULL but does nothing when it is cleared, so the SigV4 bit survives and the next request on the handle still sends an AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Authorization header to whatever URL it targets. The fix clears the SigV4 bit from httpauth when the option is set to NULL.

on_resp_header() for the HTTP/1.1 proxy tunnel handled `WWW-Authenticate` on 401 and `Proxy-Authenticate` on 407 in one branch, and the auth handling then looks at `k->httpcode` to decide which credential set to use. A proxy that answers CONNECT with 401 and a WWW-Authenticate challenge makes curl build the origin Authorization header (Basic password or Negotiate ticket) and send it to the proxy. The fix restricts the tunnel branch to 407 Proxy-Authenticate, leaving origin 401 handling to the ordinary response path.

ssh_knownhost() builds the remote key from the session host key and calls libssh2_knownhost_checkp(). With a hashed known_hosts file an unrelated initial entry can make the lookup return MISMATCH for a host that is absent from the store, and the existing MISSING/MISMATCH mapping then hands that result to CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION as if the host had no entry. The fix adds a `store->key` branch that re-checks the stored key for the host and only reports MISSING when the store really has no key for it.

When the proxy comes from the environment, create_conn_helper_init_proxy() adopts the proxy URL per transfer but never records which proxy the `state.proxydigest` material belongs to. A handle used first through proxyA with Digest authentication and then through proxyB keeps the Proxy-Authorization computation and replays it to proxyB. The fix remembers the last environment proxy in `state.envproxy` and, when it changes, clears the Digest proxy state before the connection proceeds; the string is freed in Curl_close().

init_wc_data() swaps the application write callback for the internal LIST parser and backs it up in ftpwc->backup, and wc_statemach() restores that backup only on the success path. When the wildcard transfer fails, the handle keeps Curl_ftp_parselist as fwrite_func with `data->set.out` pointing at the easy handle; reusing or cloning the handle then crashes, reads a dangling handle on the duplicate (use-after-free) or interprets server bytes into the application write-data pointer. The fix centralises the decision in Curl_ftp_listmode() (lib/ftplistparser.c) and the rewritten wildcard plumbing restores the callback on the error path too.

tftp_send_first() and tftp_receive_packet() never compare the packet event with the requested transfer direction: the ACK ("connected for transmit") and DATA ("connected for receive") cases are accepted for either mode. A malicious server answering a read request with an ACK drives the client into upload mode, and libcurl then sends bytes from the persistent CURLOPT_READDATA pointer, including leftovers of an earlier request on the reused handle. The fix adds an upload-direction check before each transition and returns CURLE_TFTP_ILLEGAL on a mismatch.

curl_mime_free() deletes the parts in a loop but recurses through curl_mime_free() for every MIMEKIND_MULTIPART part, so a deeply nested multipart structure built with curl_mime_subparts() consumes one stack frame per level and crashes the process during shutdown or cleanup. The fix replaces the recursion with an explicit loop that walks the part list, unbinds subparts (mime_subparts_unbind) and pushes nested lists onto an iterative work list.

getinfo_char() answers CURLINFO_EFFECTIVE_URL by returning the stored `state.url` verbatim. Redirect handling can leave user:password in that URL even when neither the original URL nor the redirect target had any, so the application receives credentials through a getinfo call that documents a sanitized effective URL. The fix adds effective_url(), which parses the URL, clears CURLUPART_USER and CURLUPART_PASSWORD and caches the sanitized copy in `info.effective_url` (freed on reset and close).

myssh_connect() sets only SSH_OPTIONS_KNOWNHOSTS from CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS. libssh keeps a separate global known_hosts list that it consults as well, so a host absent from the file the application specified is still accepted when it appears in /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts, defeating the user's allow-list. The fix sets SSH_OPTIONS_GLOBAL_KNOWNHOSTS to the same file so libssh has no additional trust source.
