In single_transfer() the tool installs the SSH security options (CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS via findfile(".ssh/known_hosts") and the host public key checks) only when the transfer starts out as SCP or SFTP. A transfer that begins over HTTP and is then redirected to sftp:// or scp:// reaches libssh2 without CURLOPT_SSH_KNOWNHOSTS and without the hostpubmd5/hostpubsha256 checks, so the server host key is not verified at all. The fix moves the option setup into ssh_setopts() and keys it on the global proto_scp/proto_sftp flags instead of the per-transfer use_proto, and it falls back to $HOME/.ssh/known_hosts instead of failing. Advisory scope: the tool only, CWE-297, severity Low.

The Java SockJS client builds its session id in SockJsUrlInfo from a shared AlternativeJdkIdGenerator, which seeds one SecureRandom and then draws every subsequent id from a plain java.util.Random. The sequence is predictable from a few observed ids, so an attacker who sees their own session id can compute another user's and post messages into that session. The fix switches the static generator to JdkIdGenerator (UUID.randomUUID per id).

AbstractMarshaller.createXmlReader only disables external general entities. Inline DTD declarations are still parsed, so a document that declares nested entities can expand exponentially (billion laughs) and exhaust memory/CPU before unmarshalling fails. The fix adds http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl keyed on a new supportDtd flag (default false), so DTDs are rejected outright.

ResourceHttpRequestHandler.isInvalidPath is a single expression that rejects only paths whose cleanPath() starts with "..". getResource never percent-decodes the path before this check, and cleanPath() treats backslashes as ordinary characters, so an encoded traversal such as "%2e%2e%5c" (or a mixed separator path) survives validation; PathResourceResolver.createRelative then resolves it against the file-system location and on Windows escapes the configured root. The fix decodes and revalidates the path (isInvalidEncodedPath) and normalises separators before the check.

ConstructorReference.createArray reads each dimension of a SpEL array constructor and multiplies the sizes without any cap, so an expression such as new int[2147483647] (or a multi-dimensional equivalent) makes the evaluator allocate an array until the JVM throws OutOfMemoryError. The fix introduces MAX_ARRAY_ELEMENTS (256K) and calls checkNumElements() for the single-dimension size and for the running product of the dimensions.

When Introspector reports the properties of java.lang.Class, the CachedIntrospectionResults constructor drops only "classLoader" and "protectionDomain" by name. Every other Class property is published to the BeanWrapper, including "class" itself, so a request parameter such as class.module.classLoader.resources.context.parent.pipeline.first.pattern reaches the webapp class loader on JDK 9+ and lets an attacker rewrite Tomcat access-log settings (RCE). The fix restricts Class properties to name variants and rejects ClassLoader/ProtectionDomain property types.

fromHttpUrl and fromUriString parse with a regex whose userinfo and IPv4 host character classes still admit "[" and "]", and the only host check is that an http(s) URL has a non-empty host. A crafted authority such as http://user@[::1] or a bracket-containing host is parsed into components whose getHost() differs from the authority an application validates, so an application that whitelists the parsed host can be redirected to an arbitrary host. The fix tightens USERINFO_PATTERN/HOST_IPV4_PATTERN and routes both entry points through checkSchemeAndHost(), which rejects an unterminated IPv6 literal.

createArray allocates the requested array before consulting the evaluation context at all, so a SpEL expression that constructs a large array bypasses restricted contexts (SimpleEvaluationContext) that deliberately provide no ConstructorResolver. The fix rejects array construction when getConstructorResolvers() is empty, so an application that evaluates user-supplied SpEL in a restricted context can no longer be driven into an allocation DoS through new T[...].

DataBinder.isAllowed matches the configured disallowedFields with PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch, which is case sensitive. Spring MVC canonicalises the property name but preserves the case supplied in the request parameter, so a model attribute protected by setDisallowedFields("password") still accepts "Password" or "PASSWORD" and binds the field. The fix routes the disallowed check through simpleMatchIgnoreCase so every case variant of a disallowed pattern is rejected.

javaScriptEscape() escapes quotes, backslashes, control characters and the U+2028/U+2029 line separators, but it emits backtick and "$" unchanged. When the escaped value is embedded in a JavaScript template literal, a crafted value can close the literal or start a ${...} substitution and execute script in the victim's browser. The fix adds \u0060 and \u0024 to the escaped set.

writeOptionalAttributes renders the style attribute with TagWriter.writeOptionalAttributeValue and ObjectUtils.getDisplayString, neither of which HTML-escapes the value, while the other optional attributes go through writeOptionalAttribute. A cssStyle (or cssClass/cssErrorClass) value supplied by the application from user input therefore lands in the tag unescaped and can break out of the attribute to inject script. The fix routes the style through writeOptionalAttribute and resolveCssClass through the escaping getDisplayString helper.

AntPathMatcher compiles the supplied pattern and matches it against the request path directly, so a pattern containing nested quantifiers combined with a long path makes java.util.regex backtrack exponentially and pins a request thread; applications that build AntPathMatcher patterns from attacker-influenced input are open to ReDoS. The fix wraps the input in a MaxAttemptsCharSequence that throws after 1,000,000 character access attempts, bounding the regex engine's work.

When a /** mapping renders XsltView without an explicit view name, the view URL comes from the request path and getStylesheetSource() passes it straight to getApplicationContext().getResource(url). A URL such as an absolute http:// or file: location is resolved and parsed by the TransformerFactory, giving an attacker SSRF against internal endpoints and, with a malicious stylesheet, XSLT code execution in the application process. The fix normalises the URL with ResourceHandlerUtils and rejects paths that should not be resolved as resources.

FormHttpMessageConverter.generateMultipartBoundary() fills the boundary from a single java.util.Random held in a field of the converter, seeded by the default constructor (time-based). Applications that forward user input into a multipart request to a second server therefore use a boundary an attacker can reproduce, which lets the attacker insert an extra part in the content and make the downstream server act on the wrong value (for example a username or role part), i.e. request smuggling through the multipart body. The fix switches the boundary generator to SecureRandom; in 4.3+ the generator lives in MimeTypeUtils.RND, which is the file the fix patch edits, while at 4.1.1 the same defect is in FormHttpMessageConverter.

UriComponentsBuilder splits an externally supplied URL with the pattern USERINFO_PATTERN = "([^@\[/?#]*)" assigned to the URI_SPLIT_PATTERN of java.net.URI, whose userinfo production is "([^/?#@]*)" (RFC 3986). The two classes disagree on "[" and "\", so an authority crafted around those characters is split into components whose host is not the host a browser or a proxy resolves; an application that parses a URL and then validates only getHost() can be redirected to, or made to fetch, an arbitrary host. The fix changes the pattern to "([^@/?#]*)" so the split agrees with RFC 3986; the sibling fixes CVE-2024-22259 and CVE-2024-22262 tighten the scheme, IPv4-host and port classes the same way.

The scheme, userinfo, IPv4-host and port patterns used to split a URL in UriComponentsBuilder exclude "/?#" but not "\". Browsers and several proxies treat "\" as a path separator, so a URL whose authority contains a backslash is split by the builder into a different host than the one resolved by the consumer; an application that parses a URL, validates the parsed host and then redirects to or fetches it is exposed to open redirect and SSRF. The fix adds the backslash exclusion to all four character classes (gh-32616).

The Windows installer runs icacls.exe to set permissions on the install directory and on tomcat.ico/Uninstall.exe, but names the executable without a path. On Windows the loader searches the application directory and the working directory before the system directory, so an attacker who can place an icacls.exe next to the installer (or in the directory it is launched from) gets code execution with the installer's privileges, which are administrator because the installer also creates a service. The fix prefixes every invocation with $SYSDIR so the system copy of icacls.exe is always the one executed.

Request.parseParts holds the FileItem list in a try block and never records it for the failure path, so when parsing throws (including when a configured limit is exceeded) the temporary copies already written by the multipart parser are only reclaimed by garbage collection. A client can stream uploads that fail the limit check faster than GC removes the files and fill the work directory, exhausting disk and taking the process down. The fix hoists the list out of the try block and adds a finally that clears the parts and calls delete() on every FileItem when parsing did not succeed.

When the node is draining, LoadBalancerDrainingValve builds the redirect target from request.getRequestURI() after stripping a ;jsessionid parameter. The URI is used verbatim, so a request whose path starts with multiple slashes ("//evil" or "/\evil") produces a Location header that browsers resolve as a scheme-relative or backslash-normalised absolute URL, redirecting the user off-site; the jsessionid stripper also stops at a semicolon followed by a slash, leaving crafted parameters in place. The fix collapses leading slashes to one and stops the jsessionid strip at the first slash or semicolon.

The JSON access log writer appends the request URI, the query string and the request URI element with a plain buf.append, without the JSON escaping applied to the value elements. When the connector is configured with relaxedPathChars or relaxedQueryChars, characters that JSON treats as syntax (a double quote, a backslash, a newline) reach the log line, so a request can close the JSON string and inject arbitrary fields and records into the access log, poisoning downstream log processing. The fix routes all three appends through escapeAndAppend.

RealmBase.getDigest reads the stored password and, when it is null (user unknown to the realm), concatenates it into the digest input as the string "null". A client that sends the literal password "null" therefore produces exactly the digest the server computes for the unknown user, and the DIGEST authenticator authenticates them. The fix reads the password once and returns null before the digest is built when the realm has no password for the user, so unknown users cannot authenticate.

NonceInfo.nonceCountValid clears the slot for count % seen.length and only then increments count, so the slot it clears is the one the current nonce maps to rather than the one leaving the window. The nonce that was just accepted is marked reusable, and the check that rejects counts above the window can be satisfied again, so a captured DIGEST request can be replayed inside the nonce window. The fix increments count before clearing the slot, so the entry that leaves the window is the one invalidated.

Http2Parser.readPriorityUpdateFrame parses the priority payload with Priority.parsePriority outside any catch block, so an invalid priority field value raises IllegalArgumentException out of the frame reader. The failed request is not cleaned up, leaking its buffers, and a client can repeat the frame until the heap is exhausted. The fix wraps the parse and the subsequent priorityUpdate in a try that catches IllegalArgumentException and ignores the frame, which is what RFC 9218 permits for invalid priority values.

AprEndpoint.stopInternal closes every open socket wrapper while holding only the wrapper's blocking-status write lock, and the populateRemote*/populateLocal*/doClose paths read the native socket without any lock. A close that runs while another thread is inside APR native code frees the socket under that thread and crashes the JVM. The fix overrides AprSocketWrapper.close() to take the wrapper lock and moves the isClosed() check inside the lock in the populate methods, so native socket access and close are serialised.

On connection start Http2UpgradeHandler installs the configured MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS and INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE through the ACK-dependent setter, so the limits do not apply until the client acknowledges the SETTINGS frame. A client that never sends the ACK can open as many streams as it likes and exhaust connection memory. The fix calls the forced variant of the setter for both initial settings, so the limits are in effect from the first stream.

The HTTP/2 overhead accounting only charges SETTINGS, PRIORITY and PING frames, and the CONTINUATION bookkeeping is filed under the HEADERS frame type. A client that sends a stream reset for every request therefore never accumulates overhead and can keep a connection in the request path forever, pinning server threads (DoS). The fix charges RESET frames with overheadResetFactor and separates CONTINUATION from HEADERS in the small-frame accounting.

ChunkedInputFilter treats everything after the first semicolon of a chunk header as an opaque extension: it just counts bytes and never checks the extension grammar, and the counted size is compared against maxExtensionSize only after the fact. A chunk extension containing bare CR/LF or a nested chunk-size line is therefore accepted by Tomcat but parsed as a new chunk by an intermediary, which is the classic request-smuggling desync. The fix hands the extension to the new ChunkExtension state machine, which accepts only the RFC 9112 chunk-ext grammar.

The cluster EncryptInterceptor treats a bare algorithm name (the documented default AES) as CBC, which is malleable: an attacker who can submit messages to the cluster receiver can use the padding oracle to recover plaintext and to forge messages without the shared key. The fix defaults to GCM and rejects the unauthenticated modes (ECB, CBC/NoPadding, CTR, and the other blocked combinations), so a correctly configured interceptor uses an authenticated cipher.

The cloud membership provider logs the request headers at debug level every time it opens a connection to the Kubernetes API. The headers map carries the service-account bearer token, so anyone able to read the Tomcat log (including an attacker who reached the log file through another defect) obtains a credential that authenticates as the cluster member. The fix drops the headers argument from the log message and from the localised strings.

HpackDecoder turns every literal into a String and hands it to the stream as a header without checking that the name is a lower-case HTTP token or that the value contains no CR/LF or other control characters. A client can therefore send header names with uppercase or separator characters and values with embedded line breaks, which the request layer then treats as distinct or additional headers, bypassing header-based security controls or injecting response headers. The fix passes an isFieldName flag to the string reader and rejects non-token or upper-case code points in names.

WebXml.toXml writes an auth-constraint only when findAuthRoles() is non-empty, so a constraint that uses the special roles "*" or "**" (all roles / all authenticated users) or a constraint with an empty authorization (deny all) is logged without its auth-constraint element. The effective web.xml written to the log is what administrators audit when application descriptors are not readable, so the log understates who may reach a resource. The fix emits the special role names and the empty <auth-constraint/> element.

The cluster EncryptInterceptor decrypts and accepts every well-formed message; nothing binds a message to the time it was sent, so a message captured on the cluster network can be replayed later and the receiver acts on it again (session state overwrite, repeated membership changes). The fix prefixes each encrypted payload with a timestamp, tracks recently seen messages in a bounded window and drops a message whose timestamp is outside the window or whose ciphertext was already received.

When a security collection maps "/" (the default servlet), RealmBase.findSecurityConstraints sets matched = true without consulting the methods configured on the collection, so a constraint that was meant to limit or deny specific methods is applied to every method. Depending on whether the constraint grants or denies, this either grants access the administrator did not intend or blocks methods that were allowed. The fix requires the collection to match the request method as well.

When unixDomainSocketPathPermissions is configured, NioEndpoint creates the socket with the process umask and only afterwards calls setReadable/setWritable on the path. Between bind and the permission change the socket is reachable by any local user, so a local attacker can connect during the window and talk to the connector irrespective of the configured permissions. The fix creates and validates the parent directory with the derived permissions before the socket exists, so the socket is never exposed.

The [N] flag (restart rule processing) sets the loop index to 0 and then the for-loop increments it, so the second pass starts at rule 1 and never re-evaluates the first rule. A configuration that relies on the first rule to deny or to normalise a request therefore lets a crafted request through on the restart pass, bypassing the access control the first rule implements. The fix sets the index to -1 so the next pass starts at rule 0.

RealmBase.hasRole resolves a role alias with wrapper.findSecurityReference(role), which only sees the security-role-ref elements declared on that servlet. The Context-level role-name mappings configured in the application (Context.findRoleMapping) are never applied, so a declarative security constraint that names the application role is evaluated against the platform role and can be bypassed, or granted to the wrong users. The fix resolves through the enclosing Context first.

JDBCRealm.getPrincipal builds a GenericPrincipal from whatever getPassword/getRoles return. When the database is unavailable or the role query fails, getRoles returns null (or an empty list after refactor) and the principal is still returned, so the user authenticates with no roles instead of failing closed; any constraint that relies on a role being present is then evaluated on an incomplete principal. The fix verifies the user exists, fails when the role lookup returns null and, in DataSourceRealm, propagates the failure as an authentication failure.

reserveWindowSize consumes the window allocation a stream has been granted even when the stream can no longer write, and replaceStream (used for a reset stream) leaves the stream in the backlog without returning its request or allocation. The connection window and backLogSize therefore shrink with every cancelled stream, so a client that repeatedly resets streams starves the connection of capacity and the backlog accounting grows without bound (DoS). The fix returns unused allocations, removes reset streams from the backlog and decrements backLogSize when the allocation is made.

WsServerContainer keys authenticated WebSocket sessions by the HTTP session id and only removes them when the WebSocket itself closes or the container is stopped. When the HTTP session times out or is invalidated, the WebSocket session whose principal came from it stays open and keeps the authenticated identity, so a shared or expired browser session leaves a usable authenticated channel behind; a new HTTP session that reuses the id can also attach to the old WebSocket. The fix registers a session listener on the HTTP session and closes/binds the WebSocket sessions when that session ends.

When the FFM (panama) OpenSSL integration cannot load the configured certificate revocation list file or directory, addCertificate only logs errorLoadingCertificateRevocationListWithError and continues with X509_V_FLAG_CRL_CHECK set on a store that has no CRL loaded. The handshake then proceeds without any revocation checking, so a revoked certificate is accepted even though the administrator configured CRL checking. The fix raises IllegalArgumentException instead of logging, so a broken CRL configuration fails the connector start-up rather than silently disabling revocation.

RewriteRule.evaluate evaluates a condition and, when it matches, skips every following condition marked [OR] with a while loop that runs even when the matching condition was not itself an OR member. The rule immediately after an OR group is therefore dropped from evaluation and the substitution is applied even though a condition that must hold for the rule did not run, which lets a crafted request reach a target the rewrite configuration was meant to guard. The fix enters the skip loop only when the condition that matched is part of an OR chain and consumes the group with an explicit do/while.

The bundled number guess example binds every request parameter to the NumberGuessBean with jsp:setProperty property="*". The bean exposes its properties as strings and the page later prints them, so an attacker can set an arbitrary bean property (or a property that the page echoes) through the query string and inject script into the example page. The fix binds only the guess parameter, so request parameters can no longer populate the bean.

The Jsonify form serializer marks a submitted field with $redact only for type="password" inputs and elements carrying complex-password-field; the multi-line secret widget renders a plain textarea with neither marker. A validation error for a secretTextarea field therefore carries the raw secret value in the $redact-exempt part of the JSON, and the server-side redaction sanitizer leaves it intact, so multi-line secrets reach the error message and the system log. The fix tags the textarea with secretTextarea-redact and adds the matching branch to the serializer so the field is redacted.

createProjectFromXML combines the ACL hasCreatePermission2 result and TopLevelItemDescriptor.isApplicableIn into a success flag, but when either check fails it only deletes the item from disk: the item stays registered in memory and is reachable by its name. A user with Item/Create can therefore create an item type the authorization strategy or descriptor disallows, and with Item/Configure persist it. The fix evaluates both checks separately and throws AccessDeniedException before the item is retained.

The view side panel renders the RSS header, the executors widget and the build-history task without an Overall/Read check. A view can intentionally be readable by users who lack Overall/Read, and the executors widget of that page then lists agent names. The fix wraps the header, the widget loop and the build-history task in h.hasPermission(app.READ), so the panel renders only for callers holding Overall/Read.

getPasswordValue masks a stored secret only when the nearest Item or Computer ancestor denies CONFIGURE. When an f:password field is rendered inside a View, or anywhere the nearest object of those types is not the access-controlled object that owns the value, the check consults the wrong ancestor and the concealed value is rendered to a user without CONFIGURE on the owning object. The fix walks the whole reversed ancestor chain and checks Item, Computer and View permissions at the first matching ancestor.

BuildAuthorizationToken keeps the token in a plain String, returns it from getToken(), writes it into config.xml and renders it in a textbox, so a user who can read job configuration sees the build trigger token directly. The fix stores a Secret, encrypts it on save, compares submitted tokens with a constant-time MessageDigest.isEqual, migrates existing plaintext values and renders a password field.

The job configuration form renders the build authorization token with f:textbox and the plaintext value from getToken(), so the token is visible on screen and in the page source to every user who can open the job configuration page. The fix renders f:password bound to the encrypted value, so the stored token is not displayed.

readFromTar builds the output path as new File(baseDir, entryName) and rejects it only when the normalized path does not start with a normalized baseDir. That check does not resolve symlinks inside the base directory, and it accepts a name that escapes and re-enters the base path, so a crafted .tar/.tar.gz can write through a symlink to an arbitrary location; on the controller this reaches init.groovy.d or plugins and gives code execution. The fix adds the relative-escape check, rejects entries that normalize to the base itself, resolves the absolute base and rejects symlinks in the ancestor path and at the target.

isSafeToRedirectTo rejects a target only when it is an absolute URI or starts with a literal //. A target containing relative path segments such as ./ or ../ passes that check; the servlet container later collapses the segments into a URL starting with //, which browsers interpret as scheme-relative, so the default login flow redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled host. The fix normalizes the target before validating and rejects // anywhere in it.

isSafeToRedirectTo inspects the URL exactly as submitted. A target with a tab or newline between the two slashes of a scheme-relative URL does not start with // and passes validation, while browsers strip the control characters and treat it as //host, so the login flow redirects to an attacker-controlled site. The fix removes tab, newline and carriage-return characters before the check and rejects // anywhere in the result.

A POST config.xml submission is written to disk as submitted once it can be deserialized, and a GET config.xml response with CONFIGURE copies that file verbatim. Secrets submitted in plaintext therefore persist unencrypted and are served back, and the redacted branch seen by Item/Extended Read callers is built from the same plaintext file. The fix validates the submitted XML by re-reading it into the item and then re-serializes the item from memory, so secrets are encrypted before they are written and served.

setUp rejects a file parameter location only when the raw string matches a separator-delimited .. pattern or the FilePath is not a descendant of the workspace. A location that normalizes outside the workspace through other encodings, or through the controller-side destination computed by getLocationUnderBuild, still passes, and the parameter file is copied there. The fix normalizes the candidate and both bases with FilePath semantics, checks the controller destination against its base and compares the normalized paths with isWithin.

CaseInsensitiveIdStrategy.equals compares the raw IDs with equalsIgnoreCase, while every stored lookup uses keyFor(id) (lowercased with Locale.ENGLISH). The two notions of equality can disagree for IDs whose case folding differs from the key transformation, so a user can be treated as holding another account identity for permission checks. The fix compares keyFor(id1) with keyFor(id2) in equals and compare.

configure reads the $class value from the submitted JSON and passes the unconstrained Class to req.bindJSON, so a user with Overall/Manage can instantiate any class visible to the uber classloader and have Stapler bind attacker-controlled properties to it. The fix resolves the class with asSubclass(ProjectNamingStrategy.class) and turns a mismatch into a form error.

User is not declared a top-level persistence type, so RobustReflectionConverter will deserialize a user element nested inside another submitted XML document. A user with Overall/Read can therefore create user objects (with attacker-chosen IDs) that code resolving user references later picks up, even though they are not real accounts. The fix makes User implement PersistenceRoot, which together with SECURITY-3972 refuses document-root types as nested field values.

printLogRecordHtml splits each log record into metadata and message, and wraps the differing metadata parts in a span by concatenating the raw text into the page. Log metadata can contain user-controlled content (for example a record name derived from a request), so script in that content executes in the log viewer of an administrator. The fix escapes the part with Util.xmlEscape before embedding it.

The remember-me filter is registered without a SessionAuthenticationStrategy, so when a user is authenticated from the remember-me cookie the existing session id is kept. An attacker able to set a cookie on a sibling subdomain can plant a known session id, and once the victim is re-authenticated from the remember-me cookie the attacker holds an authenticated session. The fix attaches SessionFixationProtectionStrategy to the filter.

The Appearance configuration page checks Jenkins.MANAGE once and then enumerates every descriptor matching FILTER, rendering and configuring each one. A user who may manage appearance but not a specific descriptor can therefore read and submit that descriptor's configuration. The fix computes the writable descriptors from each descriptor's required global-config permission and restricts both the template and the submit path to that set, rendering the rest read-only for holders of SYSTEM_READ.

When the CLI client is interrupted, BuildCommand cancels the future for the build it triggered. Jenkins merges requests for the same job and parameters into one queue item, so a user holding only Item/Build can merge with another user's pending build and then cancel it by interrupting the CLI. The fix requires Item/Cancel when -s is used and re-checks it before canceling on interrupt.

RobustReflectionConverter.fieldDefinedInClass accepts any field that reflection can find, including transient fields, because it only asks whether the field exists. Jenkins unmarshals transient fields on purpose for data migration, but that means a submitted config.xml can overwrite runtime-derived configuration state, changing behavior after deserialization (for example replacing the agent or view objects a configuration holds). The fix lets a field opt out with XStreamNotDeserializable, optionally enforcing a strict transient mode in which only XStreamDeserializable fields are accepted.

The "copy agent" path re-serializes the source computer with XStream and submits the result as a new node. doCreateItem checks Computer/CREATE but not Computer/EXTENDED_READ on the source, so a user who may create agents can copy an agent whose configuration they are not allowed to read. The fix adds the missing permission check on the copy source.

The "copy agent" path serializes the source computer, including encrypted credentials stored in its configuration, and reuses the XML as the new node. A user with Computer/CREATE but without Computer/CONFIGURE on the source can copy it and obtain the encrypted secrets. The fix requires Configure on the source and refuses the copy when redaction would change the XML. This is the follow-up to the incomplete fix in SECURITY-3495.

Queue.Item.doCancelQueue only checks Item/CANCEL. A user with Cancel but without Read on the job owning the queue item can still cancel it, because the endpoint does not require Read first. The fix inserts an Item/Read check (via hasReadPermission) and cancels the request handling when it fails.

TimeZoneProperty.DescriptorImpl.doFillTimeZoneNameItems accepts an ancestor User from the request and reads that user's configured time zone without requiring Overall/Administer. A user with Overall/Read can therefore determine other users' time zones by selecting them in the form; the fix requires Administer whenever a user is supplied. The companion MyViewsProperty endpoint is fixed in the same commit.

Jenkins.readResolve accepts any deserialized Jenkins instance, so a forged configuration document that carries a Jenkins object can replace or shadow the running singleton. The fix refuses to resolve a second instance and adds a writeReplace/Replacer pair plus a PersistenceRoot guard in RobustReflectionConverter so objects that live in their own top-level files cannot be smuggled through nested XML.

Nodes.replaceNode removes the old name and then puts the new node under the new name without checking whether that name already belongs to another agent. A submitted agent configuration that renames an agent onto an existing name therefore overwrites the other agent. The fix rejects the update when the new name is already taken by a different node.

A Queue.Item is reachable through Stapler as a model object; because it does not implement StaplerProxy, its actions (including ParametersAction) are served without checking permission on the job that owns the item. A user with Item/Read on any job can read parameter names and values of builds they cannot access. The fix makes Item a StaplerProxy whose getTarget enforces DISCOVER/READ on the owning job and adds the supporting getRun accessor for templates.

CVE-2026-33002 (SECURITY-3674) is about how the CLI WebSocket endpoint computes the expected Origin. The vendor advisory states the affected weekly range starts at 2.442, and at 2.441 hudson/cli/CLIAction.java contains no Origin handling at all: grep for "Origin", getRootUrlFromRequest and expectedOrigin finds nothing, and the ACCEPT_URL_FROM_REQUEST escape hatch the fix introduces does not exist. The snapshot therefore predates the feature the advisory affects.
notes: Source review 2026-10-31: no WebSocket Origin validation at 2.441; advisory affected range begins at 2.442.

basis: WebSocketServerExtensionHandler keeps a per-channel ArrayDeque of the valid extension lists, offers one entry for every inbound HttpRequest in onHttpRequestChannelRead and polls one only when the application writes an HttpResponse. Nothing bounds the queue, so a peer that pipelines requests faster than the application answers (the normal case when the handshake does async work) grows it until the heap is exhausted. The fix caps the pending request queue.

readHeaders validates that chunked is the last transfer coding by iterating the Transfer-Encoding fields and keeping only the last field value. A request that splits the equivalent coding list across fields (Transfer-Encoding: chunked followed by Transfer-Encoding: gzip) is therefore accepted and decoded as chunked although chunked is not final, which is request smuggling against a peer that rejects or buffers the same message. The fix parses the final transfer-coding token across all fields instead of suffix-matching the last field value.

toHttp2Headers applies the generic request-target conversion to HTTP/1 CONNECT authority-form targets: the request-target is emitted as :path, :scheme is derived from the host:port string, and :authority is set from the Host header, so a gateway that authorises the CONNECT target forwards the tunnel to a different, Host-controlled authority with a malformed pseudo-header set. The fix special-cases CONNECT and builds :authority from the authority-form request-target, omitting :scheme and :path.

SmtpCommand.valueOf and the DefaultSmtpRequest constructors validate only request parameters through SmtpUtils.validateSMTPParameters; the command name is wrapped into an AsciiString verbatim and SmtpRequestEncoder writes it with ByteBufUtil.writeAscii, so CR/LF embedded in the command-name field injects whole SMTP commands onto the wire. The fix validates the command name like the parameters.

setMaxHeaderTableSize accepts any value up to MAX_UNSIGNED_INT and DefaultHttp2HeadersEncoder.maxHeaderTableSize propagates the peer SETTINGS value verbatim, so a client can force the server HPACK encoder to retain every unique response header and turn the linear getEntryInsensitive lookup into a CPU and memory DoS. The fix caps the table size, for example as a function of the array-size hint.

Value validation is opt-in: the public DefaultHttp2Headers constructors install ValueValidator.NO_VALIDATION and DefaultHttp2HeadersDecoder defaults validateHeaderValues to false, while name validation runs by default. NUL, CR and LF therefore pass through in both directions and become header injection at an HTTP/2-to-HTTP/1.1 translation boundary. The fix enables value validation in the HTTP/2 header layer by default.

When converting an HTTP/1 request with an absolute-form request-target, toHttp2Headers keeps the Host header as :authority and takes the request-target authority only when Host is empty, so a gateway that authorises the absolute-form target forwards the request over HTTP/2 to the Host-controlled authority. The fix gives the request-target authority precedence when it conflicts with Host.

RtspMethods.valueOf trims trailing control bytes through ObjectUtil.checkNonEmptyAfterTrim before the cache lookup, so a wire method token such as PLAY\x00 decodes as a successful PLAY with the cached singleton and the application cannot distinguish it from a clean request; the HttpMethod hardening did not reach this sibling. The fix rejects tokens with trailing control bytes instead of trimming them.

The RFC 9112 validation added for CVE-2026-42585 tests whether the last Transfer-Encoding field value ends with the bytes chunked instead of whether the final transfer-coding token is chunked, so a value such as chunked, xchunked is accepted and decoded as chunked although chunked is not final, enabling request smuggling against a peer that interprets the coding list correctly. The fix parses the final transfer-coding token.

contentLength is a long while alreadyReadChunkSize is an int, and the remaining length is cast to int at line 149. A content-length above Integer.MAX_VALUE wraps negative, the toRead cap never applies and the decoder keeps adding chunks for the frame forever. The fix rejects a content-length above Integer.MAX_VALUE (or widens the counter).

getChunkSize returns as soon as it meets a whitespace or control byte after the leading hex digits and never validates the rest of the chunk-size line, so a line such as "5 c" is parsed as size 5 and the remaining bytes are ignored, splitting the stream into a smuggled request. The fix rejects internal whitespace and control bytes after the chunk-size digits.

The inner catch of readNextTLV releases the collected child TLVs with releaseTlvs, whose skip counter is built for the flattened top-level list. On the tree-shaped encapsulated list a nested SSL child's grandchild count is treated as a skip over following siblings and the grandchildren are never released, so malformed PROXY-v2 headers pin the underlying header ByteBuf. The fix uses releaseDeep on the error path.

validateSignature verifies the responder certificate's signature and builds the chain to the issuer with CertPathBuilder, but never checks that a delegated responder carries id-kp-OCSPSigning, so any CA-issued certificate can sign a forged GOOD response for a revoked certificate. The fix enforces the RFC 6960 EKU requirement.

The age check applies the nextUpdate upper bound only when nextUpdate is non-null; a response without it passes, and constructing OcspResponse then throws inside the promise listener, so no OcspValidationEvent and no exception reach the application while the validator removes itself from the pipeline. The fix rejects a response without nextUpdate before accepting it.

decodeProperties trusts the Properties Length variable-byte integer and asks ReplayingDecoder for that many bytes, while maxBytesInMessage is checked only against the packet Remaining Length, so a small Remaining Length with a huge Properties Length buffers and parses millions of properties. The fix bounds the properties block by the remaining packet length and maxBytesInMessage.

decode accumulates every continuation line of a multi-line SMTP response into this.details, an unbounded ArrayList; only maxLineLength bounds each line, so a server that never sends the space-separated terminator grows the list until the heap is exhausted. The fix adds a maximum number of response lines.

HttpServerCodec enqueues the method of every decoded request into a per-connection ArrayDeque that is drained one entry per non-informational response; there is no pipeline-depth limit, so a peer that pipelines requests without reading grows the queue until heap exhaustion. The fix bounds the pending-request queue.

decodeRedisArrayHeader enforces maxElements and maxNestedArrayDepth independently, but AggregateState eagerly allocates new ArrayList<>(length) at the declared length, so nested 1,000,000-element headers up to the default depth reserve on the order of a billion slots from about 12 KB of input. The fix adds a total outstanding aggregate budget across active nested states.

localConcurrentStreams defaults to Integer.MAX_VALUE and the handler exposes no setter, so acceptStream never rejects remote-initiated streams and a peer can send millions of SYN_STREAM frames with FLAG_FIN=0, allocating unbounded heap and direct memory. The fix gives the local concurrent-stream limit a bounded default and a configuration API.

checkChunkExtensions returns immediately when the chunk-size line contains no semicolon, so the strict HttpChunkLineValidatingByteProcessor only runs when an extension is present. A line with a bare CR such as "0\rX" is accepted and the remainder splits into a smuggled request. The fix validates the whole chunk-size line regardless of extensions.

extractPath treats every CONNECT request the same: it returns the :authority as the HTTP/1 request URI, and the header translation keeps only :scheme as x-http2-scheme, dropping :protocol and the Extended CONNECT :path. A downstream handler therefore cannot distinguish an RFC 8441 Extended CONNECT from a plain CONNECT tunnel and applies the wrong policy. The fix preserves the Extended CONNECT semantics.

keyLength and extrasLength are read with readShort and readByte into signed types although the binary protocol defines them as uint16 and uint8. A response with extras_length 0x80 is treated as negative, the extras bytes are left unconsumed and valueLength gains 128, shifting every frame boundary and smuggling one response's data into another. The fix reads unsigned values into int fields.

ParseExtension drains chunk extensions by searching for CR and then accepts the extension whenever the byte after it is LF, so the sequence CRX is not distinguished from CRLF: "1a;ext\rX" ends the extension at the X, the X is left in the body pipe and the remaining bytes are parsed as another chunk or request. The 8.0.21 fix searches PositionOfAny(CR, LF), requires the pair CR then LF, and rejects the rest with BadChunkExtension.

WriteCore hands the caller token straight to MessageBuffer.WriteAsync without linking ConnectionAborted, so a stateful-reconnect client that stops reading leaves the write waiting on pipe backpressure or on the resend task; the buffered invocation messages are retained and the connection is never torn down. The 8.0.25 fix links ConnectionAborted and the caller token (and lets an OCE propagate) so an aborted connection releases the buffer.

When the buffered byte count exceeds the buffer limit, WriteAsyncCore waits on the ack channel with only the caller token and no deadline, so a stateful reconnect client that never acknowledges parks its writer indefinitely and holds the associated buffer. The 8.0.26 fix bounds the wait with a five-second CancellationTokenSource linked to the caller token.

ResendAsync takes _writeLock and replays every buffered message with PipeWriter.WriteAsync without a cancellation token, so a reconnecting client that does not read blocks the resend inside the lock forever; concurrent broadcasts then wait on _resend.Task (WriteAsyncCore line 152) and are blocked indefinitely while the backlog stays pinned. The 8.0.32 fix passes a five-second backpressure token to the lock acquisition, each WriteAsync and the FlushAsync, stops the loop on a canceled or completed flush result, and aborts the connection on failure.

OnParametersSetAsync sets isAuthorized to null and then awaits the cascading AuthenticationState and the authorization service with no generation or cancellation guard: when parameters change during the await (navigation or an authentication-state change), the older continuation still writes currentAuthenticationState and isAuthorized, so content authorised by the previous decision renders after the policy changed. The 8.0.32 fix cancels the previous evaluation and discards the result if the token was canceled before it stores either field.

ReadFormAsync hands the accumulated ReadOnlySequence to ParseFormValuesFast, which starts every search for the ampersand delimiter at offset zero; when the body arrives in small increments and holds no delimiter, each read rescans all previously seen bytes, giving quadratic CPU consumption in the body length. The 8.0.32 fix carries a scannedLength cursor so the next call resumes where the previous scan stopped (keeping only the delimiter-overlap tail for rescan).

The in-memory constructor path rents memoryThreshold bytes from the shared pool immediately (memoryThreshold is clamped to 1MB), so a multipart request that declares a large threshold pins the pooled array even when the body is small or empty; repeated requests exhaust the pool. The 8.0.32 fix replaces the eager rent and MemoryStream pair with the new PooledMemoryStream, which grows on demand and returns segments it no longer needs.

GetCultureInfo resolves an unsupported requested culture by walking its parents and calls CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo on the name, which materialises and caches a new CultureInfo in the process-wide runtime cache; unauthenticated requests with arbitrary culture names therefore grow that cache without bound. The 8.0.32 fix passes predefinedOnly: true so only cultures already known to the runtime are returned.

OnHeaderCore validates names and values only when both come off the wire: the trailer branch (line 1526) and the dynamic-table branch pass checkForNewlineChars: false, and HttpProtocol.OnTrailer does the same, so a value indexed from the HPACK dynamic table (or a trailer) containing CR or LF is accepted and later surfaces in the request trailers and any downstream HTTP/1.1 serialisation. The 8.0.32 fix turns newline checking on in all three places.

CancelRequestAbortedToken publishes _connectionAborted without clearing _keepAlive; the request loop skips draining the unread request body when the connection was aborted (ProcessRequests, line 763) but still treats the connection as reusable, so the leftover body bytes are parsed as the next request on that connection. The 8.0.32 fix sets _keepAlive = false before the volatile store so the loop condition observes it.

AbortCore runs the whole abort, including _http3Output.Stop() and the frame writer abort, while holding _completionLock; on the inline output path FlushAsync holds Http3OutputProducer._dataWriterLock and re-enters AbortCore, so the two locks are taken in opposite orders and the stream, its request and the connection handler block permanently. Repeated reset/abort sequences accumulate blocked threads. The 8.0.32 fix publishes the state transition and a completion source under the lock, runs the side effects outside it, and makes request finalization wait for an in-flight abort before pooling the stream.

Invoke unconditionally clears IHttpMaxRequestBodySizeFeature (comment: "IIS already limits this"), so with out-of-process hosting the Kestrel-side limit does not apply while IIS applies maxAllowedContentLength to the compressed request; a small compressed body that expands past the intended limit is buffered and decompressed, exhausting memory. The 8.0.31 fix makes the clear an opt-in AppContext switch so the server limit stays in force by default.

RetrieveClaimsAsync searches the configured domain by sAMAccountName and takes Entries[0] as the authenticated user without comparing its objectSid with the SID in the Kerberos principal, and the claims cache is keyed on the account name alone, so a same-named account (a different principal or a name-confusion target) supplies the role claims and a cached claim set can be reused across identities. The 8.0.32 fix verifies objectSid against the PrimarySid claim, keys the cache on (name, SID), and filters non-security-enabled groups.

RetrieveClaimsAsync builds the search filter by interpolating the Kerberos name local part without RFC 4515 escaping, and it strips the realm before the lookup so the name cannot be tied to the configured domain; a principal whose name contains filter metacharacters changes the query (for example to drop the objectClass clause or match a different object) and the resulting entry supplies the role claims. The 8.0.29 fix requires the realm to be present and equal to the configured domain and escapes \\ * ( ) and NUL.

GetNestedGroups looks each memberOf group up with a subtree search on sAMAccountName equal to the group common name, which is unique only per domain and is empty for name collisions, and it accepts any number of returned entries; the first hit decides which memberof list is followed, so a crafted directory entry can redirect nested expansion to an unintended group and grant its role claims. The 8.0.29 fix reads the group by its distinguished name with base scope and follows the memberof of exactly that object.

ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation look the user up by the address in the form and then hand that same Input.Email to the mail sender instead of the address stored on the user, so an unauthenticated caller can direct another user's password-reset or confirmation link to a mailbox they control (the Identity API endpoints do the same with resendRequest.Email and resetRequest.Email). The 8.0.32 fix reads the stored address with UserManager.GetEmailAsync and fails when it is missing.

When the browser-tab lookup fails, Display writes an HTML page that interpolates the exception through string interpolation into the response body without WebUtility.HtmlEncode, while the same file encodes the tab title, tab URL and target URL; the /_framework/debug endpoint mounted by UseWebAssemblyDebugging is unauthenticated, so a crafted request that makes the devtools host lookup fail with attacker-influenced text yields cross-origin script injection on the development server. The 8.0.32 fix encodes the exception text.

decode_pointer_inplace rewrites RFC 6901 escapes in place: the ~0 branch writes "~" to decoded_string[0], but the ~1 branch writes "/" to decoded_string[1] instead of decoded_string[0]. The byte at decoded_string[0] is therefore left as whatever the previous iteration wrote (the "~" itself, or the preceding character), so a path such as "/a~1b" names "~a/b"-style keys rather than "a/b" and cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches add/remove/replace/move operations act on a key the caller did not address, silently corrupting or deleting unintended members (CVE-2026-29036, CWE-706, affects 1.5.0 through 1.7.19). The same line is still present in master (2026-10-31), so there is no fix to diff against; the probe is the advisory text against the frozen source.

cJSON_Duplicate recurses into every child without a depth bound (line 2753; the CJSON_CIRCULAR_LIMIT=10000 guard that v1.7.19 adds does not exist in v1.7.16 at all) and cJSON_Delete recurses per child without a bound as well (cJSON.c:261), while the parser limits nesting to 1000 levels (cJSON.h CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT, parse checks at cJSON.c:1446 and cJSON.c:1606). apply_patch duplicates the value and from subtrees on every add/copy operation, so a patch that repeatedly adds or copies a growing subtree doubles the document depth per operation; after about ten operations a document whose parsed depth respected the parser limit reaches a depth that overflows the default thread stack in the recursive duplicate or delete and crashes the process (CVE-2026-67215, CWE-674, through 1.7.19).

The cJSON_Object branch of cJSON_Compare walks a's members comparing each against b and then walks b's members comparing each against a, recursing into every shared subtree once per direction. The work therefore multiplies by the branching factor squared at every level, so a small, deeply nested document (depth around 40) compared for equality against a structurally equal reference burns hours of CPU, and the cost doubles per added level; the function has no depth bound, unlike the parser's 1000-level nesting limit. Any application that calls cJSON_Compare on attacker-influenced JSON is exposed to algorithmic-complexity denial of service (CVE-2026-67216, CWE-407, through 1.7.19).

apply_patch handles REPLACE by detaching and deleting the existing member (lines 890-895) before it resolves the patch's "value" member, so a replace operation that omits value returns status 7 after the target member has already been deleted; MOVE likewise detaches the source subtree (line 918) before the destination parent is resolved, and a move whose destination cannot be resolved returns status 9 and deletes the detached subtree in cleanup. In both cases cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches mutates and destroys addressable members of the target document even though it returns a failure status, defeating the all-or-nothing contract callers rely on to reject bad patches (CVE-2026-67217, CWE-696, through 1.7.19).

parse_number copies the number literal into a fixed 64-byte stack buffer and stops after 63 bytes (line 309 and the bounded loop at line 321). For a grammar-valid document whose number literal is longer than 63 characters, strtod sees only the truncated prefix and input_buffer->offset advances by that prefix length, so the remaining digits are then parsed as trailing garbage and cJSON_Parse rejects a document that other conforming parsers accept (the advisory's data-out-of-sync / denial-of-service case). The bounded copy is unchanged from v1.7.15 through v1.7.19 and master, so the behaviour is present at the frozen v1.7.16 (CVE-2023-26819, CWE-440).

serialize_key_and_certificates_to_pkcs12 builds the PKCS#12 structure with PKCS12_create (backend.py:1812) and then, when an hmac_hash override is in effect, feeds the result straight to PKCS12_set_mac at backend.py:1829. When the certificate public key does not match the private key, PKCS12_create returns NULL; the NULL check (self.openssl_assert(p12 != NULL)) sits after the set_mac call at backend.py:1845, not before it, so the C call dereferences NULL and the process dies with SIGSEGV instead of raising. The 42.0.4 fix (commit 97d23167, PR 10423) reads the OpenSSL error queue and raises ValueError before set_mac is reached. The advisory range 38.0.0 < 42.0.4 covers 41.0.5 (CVE-2024-26130, CWE-476).

_enc_dec_rsa_pkey_ctx is the whole RSA encrypt/decrypt path of the OpenSSL backend: it sets the padding mode on the EVP_PKEY context, calls EVP_PKEY_decrypt, and at rsa.py:162-163 turns every non-positive return value into ValueError("Encryption/decryption failed."). PKCS#1 v1.5 decryption fails exactly when the recovered block does not carry valid 0x00 0x02 padding, so the exception (and its timing, measured at roughly 400 ns in pyca issue 9785) separates valid from invalid padding and yields the Bleichenbacher oracle that the CVE-2020-25659 fix did not close. cryptography 42.0.0 moved the path to Rust and, more importantly, shipped wheels built against OpenSSL 3.2.0, whose implicit rejection stops EVP_PKEY_decrypt from reporting padding failures; the advisory range 0 < 42.0.0 covers 41.0.5 (CVE-2023-50782, CWE-203). The sdist source at this tag is the code line the advisory describes, so the row is anchored on the Python path rather than on the wheel.

EllipticCurvePublicNumbers.public_key() reaches load_elliptic_curve_public_numbers (backend.py:1093) and then _ec_key_set_public_key_affine_coordinates, which at backend.py:1248 installs the point with EC_POINT_set_affine_coordinates and at backend.py:1254 with EC_KEY_set_public_key. OpenSSL validates only that the point lies on the curve; for curves with cofactor > 1 (the SECT curves the advisory names) a point of small order therefore passes, and the resulting key is used by ECDH and ECDSA without a subgroup test. load_elliptic_curve_public_bytes (backend.py:1105) and the DER/PEM loaders have the same gap. cryptography 46.0.5 added check_key_infinity plus, when the group cofactor is not 1, EC_KEY_check_key in ECPublicKey::new (src/rust/src/backend/ec.rs). The advisory range 0 < 46.0.5 covers 41.0.5 (CVE-2026-26007, CWE-345).

ServerPlatformLocation builds its state from INITIAL_CONFIG.url through parseUrl (location.ts:23), which resolves the untrusted string against the synthetic base "resolve://" with new URL (location.ts:31-34). A request URL such as "//attacker.example/app" is parsed as protocol-relative: hostname becomes attacker.example while the protocol maps back to "" at location.ts:38, and the constructor copies hostname/pathname/port into PlatformLocation (location.ts:69-77). Any same-origin decision or URL built from PlatformLocation.hostname therefore uses the attacker domain. The 19.x fix f3a5bfb (2026-04-14, shipped in 19.2.21) rewrites parseUrl to prepend the document origin whenever the input starts with "/" so the host cannot be replaced; its regression test asserts hostname "" and pathname equal to the raw input for ["/\\attacker.com/deep/path", "//attacker.com/deep/path"]. The pre-image of that fix is this exact file. At 19.2.15 the resolution runs against the non-special resolve: base, so the backslash spelling alone does not produce a foreign host (node: new URL("/\\evil.com/", "resolve://").hostname === ""), while the protocol-relative spelling does (new URL("//evil.com/x", "resolve://").hostname === "evil.com"). Advisory range 19.0.0-next.0 < 19.2.21 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-41423, CWE-918).

parseUrl (location.ts:23-44) hands INITIAL_CONFIG.url and replaceState arguments to new URL(urlStr, "resolve://") and returns the normalized pathname without collapsing leading slashes (location.ts:31-43); replaceState stores that pathname verbatim (location.ts:117-122). A path that satisfies a resolver after dot-segment removal but normalizes to a protocol-relative path, such as "/.//evil.test", therefore yields pathname "//evil.test" (node: new URL("/.//evil.test", "resolve://").pathname === "//evil.test"). The vendor fix d187e8ae (2026-05-26 on branch 19.2.x, shipped in 19.2.26) adds LEADING_SLASHES_REGEX = /^[/\\]+/ and collapses any leading run of forward and backslashes to a single "/" before resolution, which is what prevents the stored pathname from starting with "//". The advisory range ends at last_affected 19.2.25, so 19.2.15 is covered (CVE-2026-111754, CWE-601).

resolveSanitizers assigns op.sanitizer from the element security context only for the update ops listed in its switch: OpKind.Property, OpKind.Attribute and OpKind.HostProperty (resolve_sanitizers.ts:58-61). Two-way bindings are emitted as OpKind.TwoWayProperty and have no case here, so a binding such as [(innerHTML)]="value" or bindon-innerHTML="value" reaches the runtime without the sanitizer that the equivalent one-way binding receives, allowing a value the template compiler would otherwise sanitize to reach innerHTML, srcdoc, src, href, data or sandbox. Fix 3c70270c adds "case ir.OpKind.TwoWayProperty:" to this switch (a one-line change) plus compliance tests that compare the generated sanitizer calls of one-way versus two-way bindings. Advisory range 0 <= 19.2.25 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-54265, CWE-79).

formatDate (format_date.ts:80) takes the format string from the caller (the DatePipe and any SSR template binding) and loops while (format) stripping one matched chunk per iteration with DATE_FORMATS_SPLIT.exec(format) (format_date.ts:92-93). Nothing bounds the input length, so a very long repeating pattern keeps the regular expression and the parts array growing for the whole string, which exhausts CPU and heap on a server. Fix eeb03f4e adds MAX_DATE_FORMAT_LENGTH = 256 and calls assertValidDateFormatLength(format) before the parsing loop, raising SUSPICIOUS_DATE_FORMAT above the cap. Advisory range 0 <= 19.2.25 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-54268, CWE-1333/CWE-400).

In visitElement (meta.ts:106) the branch for attributes that start with the i18n prefix removes the prefix and rejects the name only when isTrustedTypesSink(element.name, name) is true (meta.ts:144-154). Event-handler attribute names are not trusted-types sinks, so an element that carries a static onerror="void 0" can also carry i18n-onerror and the attribute value becomes translatable; a lower-trust translation file can then replace the benign handler with arbitrary JavaScript. Fix 6c41f5ca extends the condition with name.toLowerCase().startsWith("on"), and 417a4071 refines it with isPossibleEventHandler (length > 2, not "only", starts with "on"). Advisory range 0 <= 19.2.25 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-69151, CWE-79).

formatNumberToLocaleString parses the caller-supplied digitsInfo (e.g. "1.2-4") at format_number.ts:60-73: the fraction bounds are parseIntAutoRadix results with no upper bound, and maxFraction is raised to minFraction at line 72 when needed. Both values are passed to roundNumber at format_number.ts:76, which pads the digits array up to maxFraction, so a digitsInfo such as "1.200000000-200000000" drives an unbounded allocation loop. Because DecimalPipe, PercentPipe and CurrencyPipe call this function, an SSR page that binds attacker-controlled digitsInfo exhausts the server. Fix dfdfbe34 adds MAX_ALLOWED_DIGITS = 100 and throws INVALID_DIGIT_INFO when minInt, minFraction or maxFraction exceeds it. Advisory range 19.0.0 < 19.2.23 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-50171, CWE-400/CWE-834).

transferCacheInterceptorFn decides whether to cache a request in the guard at transfer_cache.ts:131-143. The guard skips POST and disallowed methods and, when includeRequestsWithAuthHeaders is falsey, requests carrying Authorization or Proxy-Authorization (hasAuthHeaders, transfer_cache.ts:236-238), but it never inspects req.withCredentials. A credentialed, user-specific SSR response is therefore written to TransferState and serialized into the HTML, where any shared cache or CDN layer can serve it to another user. Fix 34090cb1 adds "req.withCredentials ||" to this guard. Advisory range 19.0.0 < 19.2.23 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-50170, CWE-524).

makeCacheKey joins method, responseType, mapped URL, serialized body and sorted query parameters into one string (transfer_cache.ts:266-283) and hashes it with generateHash (transfer_cache.ts:293-305). That function accumulates with "hash = (Math.imul(31, hash) + char.charCodeAt(0)) << 0" and forces a positive 32-bit result, so the whole TransferState key space is 2^32: distinct requests, including a search query chosen to collide with a sensitive endpoint, map to the same state key and one response can be served in place of the other. Fix 5f36274d replaces the key with a SHA-256 digest computed through crypto.subtle. Advisory range 0 <= 19.2.25 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-54266, CWE-328/CWE-345).

AssetGroup.newRequestWithMetadata rebuilds every intercepted request as "this.adapter.newRequest(url, {headers: options.headers})" (assets.ts:514-516), which is called from fetchAndCacheOnce (assets.ts:168), the redirect-following path (assets.ts:380) and cache busting (assets.ts:433). A client request that set credentials: "omit" or cache: "no-store" is therefore reissued with the browser defaults (same-origin credentials, default HTTP cache), so cookies can be attached where the application explicitly forbade it and cache policy is ignored. The later fix lineage adds the missing fields to this helper: 58bf5ecd forwards options.redirect and 31399c21 forwards options.cache after preserving an explicit credentials: "omit"; at 19.2.15 all three are dropped. Advisory range 19.0.0 < 19.2.23 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-50184, CWE-200/CWE-524).

AssetGroup.newRequestWithMetadata reconstructs an intercepted request with only the headers (assets.ts:514-515). The redirect policy is not copied, so a client request made with redirect: "error" or "manual" is reissued with the default "follow" policy and the service worker silently follows 3xx responses, acting as a confused deputy for cross-origin redirects and exposing cookies or credentials attached to the redirected request. Fix 58bf5ecd forwards options.redirect in this helper; its pre-image is exactly this line. Advisory range 19.0.0 < 19.2.23 covers 19.2.15 (CVE-2026-50169, CWE-200/CWE-441).

EmitHeader adds each parsed field to *frame_length_ and compares the running total with metadata_size_limit_ (hpack_parser.cc:1049-1055). frame_length_ is zeroed in BeginFrame (hpack_parser.cc:1282), and BeginFrame runs for every CONTINUATION frame as well as the initial HEADERS frame (parsing.cc:346 calls init_header_frame_parser(t, 1), which reaches BeginFrame at parsing.cc:623) while metadata_buffer_ keeps pointing at the same batch. The limit is therefore applied per frame, not per header block, and an attacker can chain unlimited CONTINUATION frames that each add up to the per-frame budget to the same metadata batch. The check also runs only after the field value has been buffered: ParseUncompressed (hpack_parser.cc:795-810) waits for the full declared string length before the size accounting happens, and ParseVarint (hpack_parser.cc:503-554) reads an unbounded run of 0x80 continuation bytes. The 1.53.2 security backport 6bb17232 (PR #33021, 2023-05-10; master PR #33597) replaces this accounting with RandomEarlyDetection soft/hard limits computed over the whole header block and rejects oversized metadata before the value is buffered; neither src/core/lib/backoff/random_early_detection.h nor the HpackParseResult type exists in the frozen tree. GHSA-496j-2rq6-j6cc ranges 0<1.53.2, 1.54.0<1.54.3, 1.55.0<1.55.2 and 1.56.0<1.56.2; v1.52.0 is in the first band (CVE-2023-33953, CWE-400).

on_read loops on grpc_accept4 and only re-arms the listener read closure for EINTR and for EAGAIN/ECONNABORTED/EWOULDBLOCK (tcp_server_posix.cc:203-208). Every other errno, including EMFILE and ENFILE, falls into the else branch at tcp_server_posix.cc:209-221, logs "Failed accept4" and jumps to the error label at line 296, which merely decrements active_ports (and deactivates all ports only when the server is already shutting down) and returns without calling grpc_fd_notify_on_read. The listener is left with no pending read notification, so after an attacker exhausts the process file-descriptor table with connection attempts the server stops accepting for the rest of its lifetime even though the fd limit is transient. Fix 2788b568 (PR #33656, 2023-07-12) adds an EMFILE branch that re-arms the read closure and retries accept4 from a one-second timer (kRetryAcceptWaitTime, retry_timer/retry_timer_armed), with the same change in posix_engine_listener.cc and backports #33667/#33669/#33670/#33672 to v1.56.x/v1.55.x/v1.54.x/v1.53.x (released 1.56.2/1.55.3/1.54.3/1.53.2). The frozen tree contains neither kRetryAcceptWaitTime nor a retry timer on grpc_tcp_listener. The CNA record marks every release from 1.23 up to 1.56.1 affected (CVE-2023-4785, CWE-400).

grpc_chttp2_rst_stream_parser_parse reads the four-byte error code and immediately closes the stream with grpc_chttp2_mark_stream_closed at frame_rst_stream.cc:126 (function body 87-130). Nothing is sent back and no per-connection state or cost is imposed on the peer, so a client can open a stream and cancel it with RST_STREAM at line rate; the server performs the full stream setup and teardown for each one. That is the HTTP/2 rapid-reset pattern of CVE-2023-44487. The gRPC C-core mitigation commit 6358f61d (PR #34637, 2023-10-10) adds ping_on_rst_stream_percent (internal.h) and, for server transports, requests a keepalive ping with probability percent/100 on every received RST_STREAM, which forces the peer to acknowledge protocol work; the change was rolled up for the v1.59.x branch by PR #34763 and first shipped in v1.59.2 (release notes: "Rollup of fixes for CVE-2023-44487"). The frozen tree has no ping_on_rst_stream_percent field and no ping request on this path. CWE-400.

CVE-2023-32732 / GHSA-9hxf-ppjv-w6rq places every affected line above 1.52.0: the PyPI/RubyGems/Maven ranges are 1.53.0<1.53.1 and 1.54.0<1.54.2, and the CNA record's custom range is 1.53<1.54. The frozen snapshot is v1.52.0, below every introduced version. For transparency, the 1.52.x tag line never received the fix either (v1.52.1 and v1.52.2 still contain forced_close_error and the RST_STREAM write in parsing.cc:728-729), and the header-error path exists at hpack_parser.cc:825-827, so the advisory metadata rather than code absence is what keeps this row out of the positives.
notes: Affected versions start at 1.53.0; frozen v1.52.0 is below the first affected release.

basis: CVE-2024-7246 describes HPACK table poisoning: the error status of a misencoded header is not cleared between header reads, so subsequent incrementally indexed entries are added to the table with the stale error. At v1.52.0 HPackTable::Memento is ParsedMetadata<grpc_metadata_batch> (hpack_parser_table.h:85) and has no per-entry parse status; a field whose value fails to parse returns nullopt before table_->Add (hpack_parser.cc ParseLiteralKey 1094-1110, FinishHeaderAndAddToTable 1061-1077), and a metadata validation error is only logged through ReportMetadataParseError without being stored on the entry. The poisoning mechanism the advisory names therefore does not exist at this SHA. The CVE record's affected list also starts at 1.53.0 (1.53.0 through 1.65.3 are listed, 1.52.0 is absent); the OSV GIT range that starts at 0 is a coarse repository range.
notes: No per-entry parse status in Memento at v1.52.0; CNA affected list starts at 1.53.0.

basis: The advisory's only implementation repository is grpc/grpc-go, the separate Go module. The frozen grpc/grpc tree has no Go server implementation: its 13 .go files all live under tools/http2_interop (an HTTP/2 test tool), there is no internal/ directory or http2_server.go, and the C-core (src/core) is the only transport code here. A grpc/grpc-go bug therefore has no anchor in this repository. CVE-2026-33186 / GHSA-p77j-4mvh-x3m3 is an authorization bypass in the gRPC-Go server caused by a missing leading slash in :path.
notes: grpc/grpc-go CVE; frozen grpc/grpc has no Go server internals.

basis: archive_write_zip_header() stores the pathname length in the 16-bit filename field with archive_le16enc(... (uint16_t)filename_length) at archive_write_set_format_zip.c:817, then calls cd_alloc(zip, filename_length) at line 821 and copy_path() at line 823. cd_alloc (lines 201-215) only ever creates a fresh segment of 64*1024 bytes and never sizes a segment to the requested length, while copy_path (lines 1504-1519) memcpy's the full strlen(pathname) bytes. An entry whose pathname exceeds 64 KiB therefore writes the excess past the heap segment with attacker-controlled content. The fix eb482315 (PR #2993, merged 2026-05-03) rejects filename_length > 0xffff with ARCHIVE_FAILED before either header is emitted and is present from v3.8.8; GHSA-xgqq-r5j8-3mch rates it low (AV:L/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R) with CWE-787 and lists <= 3.8.7 as affected, patched in 3.8.8. The frozen v3.7.7 tree has neither the length check nor a size-aware central-directory allocation.

list() in unzip/bsdunzip.c calls archive_entry_pathname(e) at lines 890, 897 and 901 and hands the result straight to printf's %s. libarchive returns NULL when the entry carries no pathname it can convert, so a crafted archive makes bsdunzip -l / -Z1 dereference NULL. The same function also passes localtime()'s result to strftime at lines 882/884 without a NULL check. Fix c9bc934e (PR #2532, 2025-03-10) caches the pathname, substitutes an empty string when it is NULL and guards ltime; the marker first appears in v3.7.8, and NVD lists libarchive through 3.7.7 as affected (CVE-2025-1632, CWE-476, CVSS:3.1 3.3, "null pointer dereference ... function list of the file bsdunzip.c").

list_item_verbose() (tar/util.c:661) formats the entry mtime into char tmp[100] (line 663) with strftime(tmp, sizeof(tmp), fmt, ltime) at line 751 and prints tmp unconditionally at line 752. strftime returns 0 and leaves the buffer contents unspecified when the formatted date does not fit, which a custom locale can cause, and the preceding localtime()/localtime_r() result is used without a NULL check. ecce4674 (PR #2710, 2025-07-30) checks the return value and substitutes "-- -- ----"; the ltime NULL guard was added earlier by c9bc934e. The combined form first appears in v3.8.2. NVD describes CVE-2025-25724 as an unchecked strftime return in list_item_verbose through 3.7.7 with possible denial of service (CWE-252, CVSS:3.1 4.0).

parse_filter() (archive_read_support_format_rar5.c:2939-2971) rejects a filter only when block_length < 4, block_length > 0x400000, the type is unknown, or is_valid_filter_block_start() fails (lines 2963-2966). It never compares block_length with the current window size, so a crafted RAR5 archive can declare a filter whose block length cannot be satisfied; the decompression loop then waits for data that is never produced and archive_read_data() spins forever on an archive that passes checksum validation. Fix 7273d048 (PR #2877, 2026-03-01, with regression test ef53e202) adds `(rar->cstate.window_size > 0 && (ssize_t)block_length > rar->cstate.window_size >> 1)` to the rejection test; the marker first appears in v3.8.6. NVD: CVE-2026-4111, CWE-835, CVSS:3.1 7.5.

archive_write_zip_header() adds the encryption header size to entry_compressed_size with a plain += at line 718 and decides Zip64 with `entry_uncompressed_size + additional_size > ZIP_4GB_MAX` at line 732, both in int64_t. With ZIP encryption enabled and an entry size close to INT64_MAX the additions overflow (signed UB), so the Zip64 decision and the stored sizes are wrong, which the advisory maps to incorrect Zip64 handling and potential memory corruption. Fix 1c6e7b49 (PR #3228, 2026-07-03) uses archive_ckd_add_i64() for the stored-size update and compares against ZIP_4GB_MAX - additional_size for the Zip64 test; the marker first appears in v3.8.9. NVD: CVE-2026-16517, CWE-190, CVSS:3.1 2.9.

tar_atol_base_n() (archive_read_support_format_tar.c:3290-3336) parses a caller-bounded numeric field. The loop at 3326-3333 loads the next digit with `digit = *++p - '0';` (line 3331) before char_cnt is decremented at line 3332, so when the digit run ends exactly at the field boundary the increment reads one byte past the caller-provided range. The function backs PAX attributes such as SUN.holesdata, so a crafted tar whose numeric attribute ends at the field boundary triggers a one-byte heap over-read. Fix f93abd16 (PR #3253, 2026-07-06; companion ffc1114f) restructures the loop so each digit is read only while char_cnt != 0; the marker first appears in v3.8.8. The frozen 3.7.7 code keeps the older `l>limit` overflow check instead of the 3.8.x archive_ckd_* calls, but the boundary read at line 3331 is the same construct. NVD: CVE-2026-15028, CWE-805/CWE-122, CVSS:3.1 3.9.

parse_codes() (archive_read_support_format_rar.c) allocates the LZSS window only when `!rar->dictionary_size || !rar->lzss.window` (line 2506), so when a later PPMd block raises dictionary_size the existing window stays smaller than the dictionary. copy_from_lzss_window() (lines 3099-3119) then copies `length` bytes out of that undersized window and run_filters()/parse_filter() accept filter block lengths larger than the window, reading past the allocation and disclosing heap memory. Fix d379dc0b (PR #2898, 2026-03-07) extends the guard with `(rar->lzss.mask + 1) < rar->dictionary_size`, adds a `length > lzss_size(&rar->lzss)` check in copy_from_lzss_window() and rejects blocklength > (uint32_t)(rar->lzss.mask + 1) in parse_filter(); the marker first appears in v3.8.7. NVD: CVE-2026-4424, CWE-125, CVSS:3.1 7.5.

archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata() frees entry->mac_metadata at line 1561 and only then allocates and memcpy's from p at lines 1567-1570. When p aliases the entry's own metadata, as in archive_entry_copy_mac_metadata(e, archive_entry_mac_metadata(e, &sz), sz), the source buffer has already been freed, so the copy is a use-after-free that can crash or disclose heap contents. Fix 45f7ec54 (PR #3318, 2026-07-21) allocates and copies into a temporary first and frees the old buffer afterwards, with a self-copy regression test; the marker first appears in v3.8.9. NVD: CVE-2026-17591, CWE-416, CVSS:3.1 3.6.

parse_rockridge_ZF1() (archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c:2753-2764) copies the pz_log2_bs byte of a Rock Ridge ZF entry into file->pz_log2_bs (line 2761) and enables zisofs with file->pz = 1 without checking the zisofs specification's 15..17 range. zisofs_read_data() later shifts by that value, `((int64_t)1) << zisofs->pz_log2_bs` at line 1529 and `>> zisofs->pz_log2_bs` at line 1530, and derives the block-pointer allocation size from the result, so an exponent >= 64 (>= 32 on 32-bit) is undefined behavior and produces an incorrect allocation. Fix c3cb1c56 (PR #2897, 2026-03-07) rejects exponents outside [15,17] by clearing file->pz and returning before pz_uncompressed_size is consumed; the marker first appears in v3.8.7. NVD: CVE-2026-4426 (CWE-1335, CVSS:3.1 6.5).

zisofs_read_data() sizes the zisofs block-pointer table as `xsize = (ceil + 1) * 4` at archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c:1531, where ceil derives from the attacker-supplied pz_uncompressed_size and pz_log2_bs, then mallocs ((xsize >> 10) + 1) << 10 bytes at lines 1537-1538 and fills the table with ~ceil block pointers. Because parse_rockridge_ZF1() does not validate pz_log2_bs, a small exponent with a large pz_uncompressed_size makes (ceil + 1) * 4 wrap size_t to 0 on 32-bit; malloc(0) returns a tiny buffer and roughly 4 GiB of block-pointer writes follow it. The fix a2a73a8f (PR #2934, 2026-03-19) adds the pz_log2_bs validation plus a regression ISO, and the same validation was added by c3cb1c56 (PR #2897); it disables zisofs before this allocation can run. The marker first appears in v3.8.7. This row anchors the allocation sink named by the advisory rather than the validation site shared with CVE-2026-4426. NVD: CVE-2026-5121, CWE-190, CVSS:3.1 7.5 (32-bit only).

archive_acl_from_text_nl() (archive_acl.c, function starts at line 1627) splits the ACL text into fields and computes st = field[n].start + 1 at line 1721 before testing len == 0 at lines 1724-1726. For a malformed ACL such as a bare "d" or "default" tag with no following fields, field[n].start is NULL, so the increment is pointer arithmetic on NULL — undefined behavior that UBSan reports and that the following switch can turn into a crash of any archive reader that parses ACL text (bsdtar). Fix 5f702554 (PR #2905, 2026-04-18; cherry-pick 0b0b888f) moves the increment after the length check and derives it from s; the marker first appears in v3.8.6.
