NVD: CVE-2026-5745, CWE-476, CVSS:3.1 5.5.

apply_substitution() (tar/subst.c, function starts at line 199) runs a `while (1)` loop and advances the subject with `name += matches[0].rm_eo` at line 293. A global (-s/.../.../g) rule whose regular expression matches the empty string yields rm_eo == 0, so name never advances while realloc_strcat(result, rule->result + j) at line 291 appends the replacement on every iteration; memory grows without bound until the process is killed by the OOM killer. Fix df996732 (PR #2787, 2025-11-20) tracks end-of-string and copies one character on zero-length matches, and its follow-up e108f0df (PR #2809, 2025-12-12) avoids the resulting one-past-end read; the guard first appears in v3.8.4 and is complete in v3.8.5. NVD describes CVE-2025-60753 as unbounded memory allocation in apply_substitution for crafted -s rules and claims bsdtar before 3.8.1 is affected, but the code guard only landed after 3.8.3; v3.7.7 is affected either way. CWE-400/CWE-835, CVSS:3.1 5.5.

UpdateRelease() (services/release/release.go:259) walks the editAttachments map built by the web form handler EditReleasePost (routers/web/repo/release.go:596-616, which copies every `attachment-edit-<uuid>` field) and writes each new name with repo_model.UpdateAttachmentByUUID(..., "name") at lines 321-329. The loop never calls upload.Verify(nil, newName, setting.Repository.Release.AllowedTypes), while the API edit path goes through attachment_service.UpdateAttachment, which does verify (routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go:349). A repository writer can therefore rename an allowed attachment to .exe/.html/.svg and the file is served under the forbidden extension. Fix e4ef995f (PR #38314) adds the upload.Verify call inside this loop before the database write and first appears in v1.27.0; GHSA-25gq-j9jx-43pg (CVE-2026-58428) lists <= 1.26.4 as affected, patched in 1.27.0. The frozen v1.25.5 loop carries no verification.

DeleteCollaboration() deletes the collaboration row, recalculates accesses, drops watches and unassigns issues (lines 74-99) but never disables or deletes webhooks the removed user created, and webhook delivery in services/webhook/deliver.go only tests w.IsActive (lines 223 and 249) without re-checking the creator's current repository access. An admin collaborator can register a webhook while they have access, lose access, and keep receiving every later repository event payload at their endpoint. GHSA-66m4-5jjr-2rg5 (CVE-2026-58440) rates it 6.8 and lists <= 1.26.4 as affected with a 1.27.0 patch, but no commit in the tree or on current main adds webhook cleanup here or a creator-access check to delivery, so no fix commit can be cited and the frozen v1.25.5 behavior is the behavior of the latest tree as well.

DownloadArtifactRaw() runs without the repo assignment middleware and checks the caller itself: it loads the repository by owner/name (line 1626), then getArtifactByPathParam (lines 1676-1693) fetches the row from the global action_artifact table by the numeric artifact_id and answers 404 when the row is missing, belongs to another repository, or is not upload-confirmed/expired. Only afterwards does the handler verify the HMAC over buildDownloadRawEndpoint(repo, art.ID) at lines 1645-1649 and answer 401. Artifact ids are global auto-increments, so an unauthenticated caller with a bogus sig gets 401 when the guessed id belongs to the named repository and 404 when it does not, which is an artifact-to-repository association oracle; bytes stay protected by the signature. Fixes 5fc3cec8 (PR #39049) and backport 6e2cf106 (PR #39053) verify the signature before touching the row and first appear in 1.27.3; GHSA-f8ph-p9p5-vg2p (CVE-2026-73504) lists <= 1.27.2 as affected. The frozen v1.25.5 handler keeps the lookup-first ordering.

Push() builds `git push [-f] [--mirror] <remote> [branch]` from the stored remote name and runs it with the caller-supplied environment (lines 205-218). Nothing sets http.followRedirects=false and nothing re-applies the outbound host policy, so a 301 served by an allow-listed smart-HTTP endpoint redirects the smart-HTTP request to an address the policy would reject. The ls-remote probe in IsRepoURLAccessible (lines 73-76) has the same property, and the whole frozen tree contains no reference to followRedirects (the 1.27-era HandleGitCmdHTTPRedirection stub does not exist yet). Fix 1b127448 (PR #39426, "use internal proxy for all git operations", released in 28.0.0) routes every git network operation through the new gitproxy/matchlist egress control and removes the per-call proxy environment; GHSA-g4hw-fg4c-89mq (CVE-2026-104636) lists <= 1.27.3 as affected, patched in 28.0.0.

runPushSync() reads the stored remote URL with gitrepo.GitRemoteGetURL (line 133), pushes LFS objects through NewMigrationHTTPTransport — which does enforce the migration allow/block list — and then calls git.Push with force+mirror at lines 159-165 without any IsMigrateURLAllowed or hostmatcher check. The address is validated only when the mirror is created (routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:347, routers/web/repo/setting/setting.go:274 and :454), so a hostname that resolved to a public address at creation and resolves to an internal git service at sync time is contacted on every scheduled sync, and `git push --mirror` force-writes and deletes refs there; a block-listed host is still reached. The pull mirror path revalidates before fetching; this path never has: the frozen tree has no IsMigrateURLAllowed or hostmatcher use in services/mirror/mirror_push.go. Fix 1b127448 (PR #39426, 28.0.0) moves all git egress into the internal gitproxy and strips the per-call proxy env at line 158; GHSA-hcgw-r9gf-8mph (CVE-2026-89430) rates it 8.5 and lists <= 1.27.3, patched in 28.0.0.

MigrateRepository revalidates repo.CloneURL after the downloader rewrites it (services/migrations/migrate.go:202) by resolving the hostname with net.LookupIP inside IsMigrateURLAllowed (migrate.go:84) and matching the check-time address list. The actual fetch happens later: RepositoryDumper.CreateRepo() passes the rewritten URL to git.Clone at lines 151-156 (and the wiki clone at line 172), and the git subprocess performs its own DNS resolution — nothing under modules/git uses hostmatcher, net.LookupIP or net.Dial — so an answer that changes between check and connect reaches the internal address. The in-tree TODO at migrate.go:498-499 documents the same gap for ALLOW_LOCALNETWORKS/ALLOWED_DOMAINS. Fix 1b127448 (PR #39426, 28.0.0) replaces the check-then-spawn model with the internal gitproxy that enforces the new matchlist policy at dial time; GHSA-p3pc-g8m5-hrrr (CVE-2026-70357) lists <= 1.27.3 as affected, patched in 28.0.0, with CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N.

rerunJob() resets a finished job to StatusWaiting at line 484 unless the caller passes shouldBlock, and Rerun (lines 401-472) only refuses a run that is not done (line 416) and only derives shouldBlock from job dependencies and the selected job — it never reads run.NeedApproval. ApproveRuns is the only place that clears NeedApproval (line 590); cancel leaves it set. A first-time fork PR whose jobs were inserted as Blocked (models/actions/run.go:320 includes run.NeedApproval) can therefore be cancelled and rerun by an Actions writer, the job becomes Waiting, CreateTaskForRunner selects `task_id=0 AND status=StatusWaiting` (models/actions/task.go:241) without any approval predicate, and a registered runner executes the workflow taken from the fork head. GHSA-pvjf-7jrm-6w9g (CVE-2026-104632) rates it 9.0 critical and lists <= 1.27.3, patched in 28.0.0; its suggested fix — treat NeedApproval as blocking wherever a job becomes Waiting — maps onto this handler pair, the only path in the frozen tree that can move a NeedApproval run's jobs back to Waiting.

checkByAllowBlockList() ORs the allow and block results over every address returned by IsMigrateURLAllowed's net.LookupIP (migrate.go:84): `ipAllowed = ipAllowed || allowList.MatchIPAddr(addr)` at line 92 and `ipBlocked` at line 93. A hostname that answers with one allow-listed public address plus one internal address passes the allow decision at lines 100-103, and the default empty block list never fires, so the later migration or mirror fetch follows the internal answer. The advisory's F1b (push-mirror write) and F1c (internal responses leaked through mirror last_error) are separate findings built on this same root cause; this row anchors the lead finding for a distinct CVE record, next to the earlier CVE-2026-58442 row on the same decision block. Fix 1b127448 (PR #39426, 28.0.0) removes the check-then-connect model: the migration HTTP client and the git subprocess both pass through the gitproxy/matchlist egress policy. GHSA-6g2h-xpg3-rm48 (CVE-2026-101029) rates it 8.5 and lists <= 1.27.3, patched in 28.0.0.

HostMatchList.checkIP() matches MatchBuiltinPrivate only through ip.IsPrivate() (lines 111-114). Carrier-grade NAT (100.64.0.0/10), link-local including the cloud metadata address (169.254.0.0/16), NAT64, Teredo and the other special-purpose ranges are not IsPrivate, and an address such as 169.254.169.254 is not IsGlobalUnicast either, so it matches neither the external nor the private builtin. migrations.Init appends the private and loopback builtins to the block list when ALLOW_LOCALNETWORKS=false (migrate.go:484-502), and checkByAllowBlockList then permits any host whose name matches ALLOWED_DOMAINS even though the resolved address was meant to be denied — the policy bypass the advisory describes. Fix 920b3f8c (PR #38039, "block reserved IP ranges from external/private filters") adds reservedIPNets and isPrivateIP() and routes both builtins through it; GHSA-54w9-6cc5-9wj9 (CVE-2026-96400) rates it 4.3 and lists <= 1.27.3, patched by the 28.0.0 matchlist rewrite (1b127448). The frozen v1.25.5 matcher has neither reservedIPNets nor isReservedIP.

newRenderPlugin3DViewer().render() dynamically imports the pinned online-3d-viewer@0.16.0 (package.json:43) and constructs OV.EmbeddedViewer(container, ...) directly inside the file-view container of the Gitea page at lines 50-56, so every DOM node the library writes — including the error message it builds from the unsupported `extensionsRequired` names of an uploaded .gltf — lives in the Gitea origin. The in-tree fallback renderer escapes its own message (web_src/js/features/file-view.ts:57), but that does not cover errors the library renders itself, which is the stored XSS GHSA-9cpj-qc93-vw8v describes for 1.25.x. Fix d5831b9385eb (PR #37233, released in 1.26.0) removes this plugin and runs the 3D renderer inside the sandboxed iframe renderer framework (web_src/js/render/plugins/frontend-viewer-3d.ts plus web_src/js/external-render-frontend.ts), so the viewer no longer shares the page origin. The advisory lists >= 1.25.0, < 1.26.0 as affected with the 1.26.0 patch and rates it 8.7.

HandleNode (src/singledocparser.cpp:48) parses leading tag and anchor properties with ParseProperties(tag, anchor) at line 75 and then reads the next token with m_scanner.peek() at line 77 without checking whether any node followed the properties. For the document `!2` the scanner emits only the TAG token: ParseProperties pops it, INPUT is exhausted, EndStream sets m_endedStream and pushes no further token, EnsureTokensInQueue returns with an empty queue, and the assert(!m_tokens.empty()) in Scanner::peek (src/scanner.cpp:32) fires and aborts the process (issue #519). In a release build the assert is compiled out and the same path evaluates m_tokens.front() on the empty queue, so the missing check is the defect, not the assertion. Fix c9460110e0 (2020-01-21, "Fix reading empty token stack with a node with properties but no scalar", regression test Load("!2")) inserts an empty check between ParseProperties and peek; the PR #806 attempt to replace the assertion was closed unmerged. The check is absent from the frozen 0.6.2 tree and from vanilla 0.6.3, and is present in 0.7.0. NVD CPE stops at versionEndIncluding 0.5.3 while Debian OSV publishes introduced 0, fixed 0.6.3-1 (a Debian backport), so 0.6.2 is inside the Debian range and the static path above confirms it.

HandleNode (src/singledocparser.cpp:48) dispatches FLOW_SEQ_START and FLOW_MAP_START to HandleSequence/HandleMap, which call HandleNode again for every nested collection, and the 0.6.2 parser carries no depth counter on the path: n nested collections create O(n) C++ frames until the thread stack is exhausted and the process dies with SIGSEGV (issue #459, reproduced against 0.5.3 and unchanged in 0.6.2). Fix 4edff1fa5dbfca16fc72d89870841bee89f8ef89 (PR #807, 2020-04-09) inserts DepthGuard<2000> as the first statement of HandleNode, bounding every recursive route at once; the 0.7.0 release ships the same guard with a limit of 500 (lowered by c2793a3), and neither the guard nor include/yaml-cpp/depthguard.h exists at the frozen 0.6.2 SHA. NVD CPE names only 0.5.3 and labels the issue CWE-119; Debian OSV publishes introduced 0, fixed 0.6.3-1, so 0.6.2 is inside the Debian range, and the crash is uncontrolled recursion (CWE-674), not a buffer error.

EnsureTokensInQueue (src/scanner.cpp:48) is the frame named in the 0.6.2 stack-overflow report (issue #655): every collection level calls m_scanner.peek() -> EnsureTokensInQueue while the unbounded HandleNode recursion descends, and the refill loop only returns once a valid token exists or m_endedStream is set, so the deepest frame of an exhausted stack is the scanner loop. The recursion is the parser's: HandleNode dispatches FLOW_SEQ_START/FLOW_MAP_START back into HandleSequence/HandleMap, which call HandleNode again, and 0.6.2 has no depth counter anywhere on that path. Fix 4edff1fa (PR #807) adds DepthGuard<2000> at the top of HandleNode (500 in the 0.7.0 release), which caps the cycle before the scanner is re-entered; the guard is absent at the frozen 0.6.2 SHA. NVD labels this record CWE-119 but the crash is uncontrolled recursion (CWE-674); Debian OSV publishes introduced 0, fixed 0.6.3-1, placing 0.6.2 in range, and Debian 0.6.3-1 is a backport of #807, so the first upstream fixed release is 0.7.0.

HandleFlowMap (src/singledocparser.cpp:275) consumes the FLOW_MAP_START token and calls HandleNode for the key at line 295 and for the value at line 303; HandleNode dispatches the next FLOW_MAP_START back into HandleMap and hence HandleFlowMap, so a document of n nested `{` builds O(n) frames with no depth limit and crashes with SIGSEGV (issue #654, reported against the frozen 0.6.2 commit). Fix 4edff1fa (PR #807) inserts DepthGuard<2000> as the first statement of HandleNode (500 in the 0.7.0 release), which bounds this cycle before it re-enters HandleFlowMap; the guard and depthguard.h are absent from the frozen tree and from vanilla 0.6.3. NVD labels the record CWE-119, a misclassification of uncontrolled recursion; Debian OSV publishes introduced 0, fixed 0.6.3-1, so the frozen 0.6.2 is inside the Debian range.

HandleCompactMap (src/singledocparser.cpp:324) is the first frame named in the 0.6.2 report (issue #657): it calls HandleNode for the key at line 330 and for an optional value at line 335, and HandleNode can re-enter the flow-sequence, flow-map and compact-map cycle, so nested `?`/`{` constructs exhaust the C++ stack with no depth counter anywhere in the parser. Fix 4edff1fa (PR #807) inserts DepthGuard<2000> at the top of HandleNode (500 in the 0.7.0 release), which bounds every path, including this one; the guard and depthguard.h are absent from the frozen 0.6.2 tree. Debian OSV publishes introduced 0, fixed 0.6.3-1, so 0.6.2 is inside the Debian range; the Debian package is fixed by backporting #807 and the first upstream release containing the guard is 0.7.0. This record shares the recursion family with CVE-2019-6285 (already a GT row at HandleNode/HandleFlowSequence) but is a distinct catalog entry with its own affected record.

Candidate sweep_3d7d3da44f43daa3 carries CVE-2018-20573, promoted from disc2_89b05e73df5fa26aa41d15f3 on the same snapshot (src/scanner.cpp:48-60). The two rows describe one advisory and one defect; the substantive decision lives on the promoted row.
notes: Second catalog candidate for one advisory; not a separate vulnerability.

basis: Candidate sweep_e4eeca19e3ac7a2d carries CVE-2018-20574, promoted from disc2_7f26fb7e7ae793d3258463d8 on the same snapshot (src/singledocparser.cpp:275-303). The two rows describe one advisory and one defect; the substantive decision lives on the promoted row.
notes: Second catalog candidate for one advisory; not a separate vulnerability.

basis: Candidate sweep_f1d0ad7d902925f9 carries CVE-2019-6292, promoted from disc2_bf26294ad497c77aa92b16b9 on the same snapshot (src/singledocparser.cpp:324-340). The two rows describe one advisory and one defect; the substantive decision lives on the promoted row.
notes: Second catalog candidate for one advisory; not a separate vulnerability.

basis: http2Transport.request (lib/adapters/http.js:457) builds the authority and calls http2Sessions.getSession(authority, http2Options) at line 468 with only the caller-supplied http2Options object. The DNS policy the adapter stores on the request options (options.lookup at line 897) and the proxy setProxy installs at lines 934-941 never reach that call, and Http2Sessions.js:41 hands the same object to http2.connect, so with httpVersion: 2 a configured lookup is never called and a configured proxy is bypassed while the request still "succeeds". Fix d19040bda7a8 merges lookup into http2Options when isHttp2 && lookup, passes allowEnvProxy = !isHttp2 into setProxy, and rejects an HTTP/2 request that would use a proxy (ERR_NOT_SUPPORT) instead of connecting around it.

shouldBypassProxy (lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:274) splits NO_PROXY into entries, separates host and port in parseNoProxyEntry (196-226), normalizes each entry host and matches exact hosts, "." suffixes, "*"-prefixed entries and loopback equivalences (lines 296-328). A CIDR suffix is never interpreted: the entry 10.0.0.0/8 normalizes to the literal host "10.0.0.0/8" and matches nothing, so a request to 10.1.2.3 that the operator excluded from the proxy is still sent through it (no CIDR branch exists at the frozen tree). Fix d19040bda7a8 adds normalizeCidrBase/parseCidrEntry/ipToBytes/isInSubnet and evaluates a CIDR entry as a subnet test ahead of the host comparisons.

resolveConfig (lib/helpers/resolveConfig.js:25) handles a FormData body for the shared pre-dispatch path: line 72 tests utils.isFunction(data.getHeaders) and line 74 calls setFormDataHeaders(headers, data.getHeaders(), ...) with no own-property guard. The fetch adapter runs resolveConfig(config) before dispatch (lib/adapters/fetch.js:211), so a body that passes utils.isFormData() through an inherited Symbol.toStringTag/append and resolves getHeaders from a polluted Object.prototype merges attacker-controlled headers into the outbound request. Fix d19040bda7a8 reads utils.getSafeProp(data, "getHeaders") and invokes it with data as this.

Http2Sessions.getSession creates the session with http2.connect(authority, options) at lib/helpers/Http2Sessions.js:41 and registers only session.once("close", removeSession) at line 107. No "error" listener exists on the ClientHttp2Session, so a network or protocol failure emitted as "error" (ECONNREFUSED to a closed port, a non-HTTP/2 endpoint) is an unhandled EventEmitter error: Node throws outside the axios promise chain and terminates the process, bypassing the rejected-request path (advisory repro: axios.get("http://127.0.0.1:1/", {httpVersion: 2, timeout: 1000})). Fix d19040bda7a8 adds session.once("error", removeSession) beside the close handler and gives the merged options a null prototype.

Axios.prototype._request (lib/core/Axios.js:82) sets config.method = (config.method || this.defaults.method || "get").toLowerCase() at line 147. config comes from mergeConfig with a null prototype (lib/core/mergeConfig.js:37), but this.defaults is the plain object literal exported by lib/defaults/index.js and owns no "method" key, so the read falls through to Object.prototype: with Object.prototype.method polluted elsewhere in the process, axios.request({url}) and axios({url}) send the polluted method (DELETE/POST/PUT/PATCH) instead of GET while the call site looks like a read. Fix d19040bda7a8 reads both config.method and this.defaults.method through utils.getSafeProp.

fromDataURI (lib/helpers/fromDataURI.js:21) matches the URL against DATA_URL_PATTERN at line 9, whose media-type groups are [^,;]+ on both sides of a required "/". Because both groups admit "/", a data: URL of n slashes with no comma forces the backtracking engine to try O(n^2) separator placements before failing; the match is synchronous and runs before any axios timeout, blocking the Node event loop. Fix d19040bda7a8 changes both groups to [^,;/]+ so the separator is unambiguous.

dispatchRequest (lib/core/dispatchRequest.js:34) normalizes the outgoing headers with config.headers = AxiosHeaders.from(config.headers) at line 37. Request interceptors may return a replacement plain-object config; nothing at that boundary re-establishes an own "headers" or a null prototype, so an inherited Object.prototype.headers is converted into the outgoing AxiosHeaders and sent, even though the merge-time config was hardened. Fix d19040bda7a8 flattens the interceptor-supplied config with utils.toSafeFlatObject at the top of dispatchRequest and reads utils.getSafeProp(config, "headers").

The Node HTTP adapter builds its request options as a null-prototype object at lib/adapters/http.js:883-894 but sets no own createConnection. Node's http client copies and normalizes these options into ordinary objects before connecting, so a function placed on Object.prototype.createConnection by a separate same-process prototype-pollution primitive is resolved and invoked as the socket factory: the connection goes to the attacker-controlled endpoint while the URL and axios config still name the legitimate origin, exposing request headers and bodies and returning attacker responses. Fix d19040bda7a8 adds createConnection: undefined to that literal so the prototype member is shadowed. This row re-anchors the 2026-10-31 promotion, whose previous anchor (http.js:551-565, the inline lookup wrapper moved to normalizeLookup by the same commit) was not the site the fix changes.

normalizeNoProxyHost (lib/helpers/shouldBypassProxy.js:253) normalizes a hostname with hostname.replace(/\.+$/, "") at line 262; normalizeIPAddress uses the same pattern at line 60. On a hostname of n dots followed by a non-dot the anchored regex restarts the dot run from every position before failing, giving O(n^2) synchronous work. setProxy calls shouldBypassProxy for every redirect hop when NO_PROXY is non-empty, so a malicious server can return a Location whose host stalls the event loop. Fix d19040bda7a8 replaces both uses with a linear trimTrailingDots loop.

The fetch adapter builds a hardened resolvedOptions at lib/adapters/fetch.js:423-431 and then dispatches with _fetch(request, fetchOptions) at line 436, passing the caller's raw fetchOptions object as the fetch init instead of resolvedOptions. Inherited members of that object therefore reach the platform fetch: in Node's undici-backed implementation an inherited fetchOptions.headers overrides the headers already set on the Request, dropping the caller's own headers for attacker-controlled ones. Fix d19040bda7a8 copies fetchOptions into a null-prototype object, deletes the axios-owned keys (body, headers, method, signal, duplex, credentials) and passes that object.

toFormData (lib/helpers/toFormData.js:94) flattens the caller options with utils.toFlatObject(options, {metaTokens: true, dots: false, indexes: false}, false, defined) at lines 103-115. utils.toFlatObject returns a plain {} (lib/utils.js:603) and, with filter=false, copies own properties only and stops before Object.prototype (lib/utils.js:620), so the reads that follow - options.metaTokens, options.visitor, options.dots, options.indexes, options.Blob and options.maxDepth at lines 117-123 - resolve inherited members of a polluted Object.prototype: dots/indexes/metaTokens change field naming, maxDepth can throw ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED, visitor becomes the serializer callback and Blob changes value handling. Fix d19040bda7a8 reads each option through utils.getSafeProp with explicit fallbacks.

context.RealIP (context.go:309) returns the first X-Forwarded-For or X-Real-IP header whenever Echo.IPExtractor is nil, the default of echo.New(), with no check that the request came from a proxy (legacy branch, lines 313-330). DefaultRateLimiterConfig (middleware/rate_limiter.go:46-51) builds its per-client identifier from ctx.RealIP(), so a client that rotates X-Forwarded-For on every request gets a fresh bucket and never hits the rate limit (CWE-290). The v4.16.3 fix ebbb855f adds extractIP and makes the nil-extractor path return the connection peer only; forwarding headers are honoured solely through a configured IPExtractor with trust ranges.

ProxyWithConfig (middleware/proxy.go:288) rewrites X-Real-IP only when the header is absent or Echo.IPExtractor is set (line 349); the adjacent comment states the legacy condition is kept for backward compatibility. With the default nil extractor an incoming X-Real-IP is forwarded to the upstream verbatim, so any client can forge the identity that upstream IP allowlists, rate limits and audit logs rely on (CWE-346, CWE-441). The v4.16.3 fix ebbb855f always overwrites the header with Context.RealIP() and re-sets it in a transport wrapper so Connection: X-Real-IP cannot suppress it.

StaticWithConfig (middleware/static.go:157) takes p from c.Request().URL.Path, which net/http has already percent-decoded, and unescapes it a second time at line 173 before path.Clean at 183. A double-encoded form such as /%252e%252e%252f or /..%252f is therefore decoded once by the server and again here, so the path the router matched as a single segment resolves to a different file; with the middleware registered globally that file can sit under a route whose middleware never ran (CWE-174). The v4.15.3 fix c3fa2a27 adds pathutil.HasEncodedPathSeparator and rejects %2F/%5C before unescaping; v4.16.0 additionally defaults EnablePathUnescaping to false so the path is used as the router matched it. The advisory links a9ede66a, the same change on the v5 line; the advisory and the maintainer note both record that reading files outside the configured root could not be reproduced, and the confirmed impact is the guarded-route bypass.

StaticWithConfig (middleware/static.go:157) resolves the requested file from URL.Path (decoded) through path.Clean("/"+p) at line 183, and path.Clean collapses "." and ".." segments. The router matches the raw path, so /public/%2E%2E/admin/secret.txt never matches the guarded /admin/* route and its middleware, yet it is cleaned to /admin/secret.txt and served from the static mount; at v4.15.2 the value is also unescaped at 173, so encoded dots become real dot segments after routing. Echo.StaticDirectoryHandler (echo_fs.go:59) has the same shape. The v4.16.0 fix b838391e2 (whose code comments name GHSA-3pmx-cf9f-34xr) adds hasUncleanPath/hasDotOrEmptySegment and refuses to open a file when the matched path or the unescaped path has a "." , ".." or empty segment.

sanitizeURI (middleware/slash.go:122) decides that a redirect target is not absolute by looking only at uri[0] and uri[1]. A leading TAB or other control byte shifts a "//" or "/\" sequence to offsets 1-2, the guard does not fire, and Context.Redirect writes the value to the Location header; browsers strip TAB before parsing and resolve /\t/attacker.example as //attacker.example, an open redirect (CWE-601). The same function is duplicated at echo_fs.go:155. The v4.16.0 fix b838391e2 adds escapeControlChars and percent-encodes C0 controls and DEL before the separator test (both copies).

BodyDumpWithConfig (middleware/body_dump.go:53) reads the complete request body with io.ReadAll at line 71 and tees the complete response through io.MultiWriter into a bytes.Buffer at line 80, with no capture limit. A route that opts into BodyDump therefore buffers attacker-sized request and response bodies in memory, and concurrent large requests exhaust the process (CWE-400, CWE-770). The v4.16.1 fix 3fb0ba7 adds BodyDumpConfig MaxRequestBytes/MaxResponseBytes (default 5 MiB, -1 disables), captures through io.LimitReader/bodyDumpLimitedWriter without truncating what the handler or client sees, and replays the captured request bytes.

ProxyWithConfig (middleware/proxy.go:260) selects proxyRaw from c.IsWebSocket() alone (switch at 386-391), before the upstream has accepted the upgrade. If the upstream answers with an ordinary HTTP response and keeps the connection alive, proxyRaw keeps tunnelling and subsequent requests on that connection reach the upstream without passing through the Echo router or its route/group middleware, so authentication enforced only there is bypassed (CWE-444, CWE-863). The v4.16.1 fix 3fb0ba7 deletes proxyRaw and sends every request through httputil.ReverseProxy, which tunnels only after a valid 101, and wraps the hijacked connection.

proxyRaw (middleware/proxy.go:134) hijacks the client connection, dials the upstream and copies both directions, then waits for both goroutines at lines 176-181 without closing the other side when one direction ends. If the upstream keeps its side open after the client disconnects, or a rejected upgrade keeps HTTP keep-alive, the handler, both copy goroutines and both connections are retained per request and accumulate into a denial of service (CWE-772). The regression was introduced by e2133320c7 (#2852) and shipped in v4.15.0, so v4.15.2 is in range. The v4.16.1 fix 3fb0ba7 removes proxyRaw and uses Go's reverse proxy, which closes both sides when either direction ends (proxyUpgradeResponseWriter hides CloseWrite).

DecompressWithConfig (middleware/decompress.go:50) replaces the request body with the gzip.Reader at line 93 without limiting the expanded size, so a small compressed request can decode to an unbounded stream that handlers read or bind, consuming memory or CPU and enabling denial of service (CWE-400, CWE-409). The v4.16.1 fix 3fb0ba7 adds DecompressConfig.MaxDecompressedSize (default 100 MiB, -1 disables) through limitedGzipReader, returns HTTP 413 on overflow (also through JSON/XML binding) and clears the compressed ContentLength.

Advisory GHSA-23wf-92cp-8pcj publishes v4 `< 4.15.2` (patched 4.15.2); the frozen snapshot IS the v4.15.2 tag commit 25685e6f5f7b, so the version range excludes it. Static review at the frozen SHA confirms the fix is present: context.go:274-305 adds isValidProto and Context.Scheme (context.go:288) returns a forwarded scheme header only when it is http, https, ws or wss, falling back to http otherwise; the v4.15.2 CHANGELOG records "Context.Scheme() should validate values taken from header" (#2962). This is source-level evidence, not only a version-range miss.

safe_join() accepts a UNC-style absolute pathname such as "//server/share" on Windows with Python < 3.11: ntpath.isabs() does not treat a leading "//" as absolute, and the guard at src/werkzeug/security.py:147-152 only rejects OS alternate separators, os.path.isabs(), ".." and "../". The pathname is joined onto the trusted directory and returned, so send_from_directory can serve data outside the root. The fix adds an explicit filename.startswith("/") rejection.

safe_join() does not reject Windows special device names: the per-pathname guard at src/werkzeug/security.py:143-153 checks only alternate separators, os.path.isabs(), ".." and "../", so a pathname equal to CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9 or LPT1-9 is accepted and joined. On Windows send_from_directory then opens the device and the read blocks indefinitely. The 3.1.4 fix adds a _windows_device_files set and rejects those names when os.name == "nt".

Follow-up to GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2: the device-name check that 3.1.4 added used os.path.splitext(filename)[0].upper(), so a pathname such as "CON.txt.html" (compound extension) or "CON " (trailing spaces) bypassed it, and the device-name set was incomplete. On Windows the request still opens the device and the read hangs. The 3.1.5 fix tests filename.partition(".")[0].strip().upper() and adds CONIN$, CONOUT$ and the superscript COM/LPT names. The frozen 3.0.2 tree has no device-name filtering at all, so the vulnerable behavior is present a fortiori.

Follow-up to GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2: safe_join() applies posixpath.normpath() to the whole pathname and validates it once, so a multi-segment pathname whose last segment is a device name (for example "example/NUL") passes the guard at src/werkzeug/security.py:143-153 and is joined; on Windows the read of the device blocks indefinitely. The 3.1.6 fix checks every "/"-separated segment against _windows_device_files and rejects backslashes outright. The frozen 3.0.2 tree has no device-name filtering at all, so the vulnerable behavior is present a fortiori.

Follow-up to GHSA-hgf8-39gv-g3f2: on NTFS an empty alternate data stream marker such as "NUL:" still names the device, and the 3.1.5 check p.partition(".")[0].strip().upper() does not strip the colon, so the pathname passes the guard in safe_join() and is joined; on Windows the read blocks indefinitely. The 3.1.9 fix tests p.partition(":")[0].partition(".")[0].strip().upper(). The frozen 3.0.2 tree has no device-name filtering at all, so the vulnerable behavior is present a fortiori.

basis: CookieJar accepts an unlimited number of Set-Cookie fields of unlimited size from one response and later serialises every match into one Cookie header with no length or count cap: extractCookies() stores each cookie unconditionally and withCookieHeader() appends name=value pairs without tracking the header length (src/Cookie/CookieJar.php:291-301). A malicious server can therefore drive memory growth and emit a Cookie header that later handlers, proxies or origins reject. The 7.15.1 fix adds MAX_SET_COOKIE_FIELD_LENGTH/MAX_SET_COOKIE_FIELDS in extractCookies() and MAX_REQUEST_COOKIES/MAX_COOKIE_HEADER_LENGTH in withCookieHeader().

RedirectMiddleware::modifyRequest() builds the Referer value with withUserInfo("") only, so when allow_redirects.referer is enabled the fragment of the referring URI survives into the Referer header on a same-scheme redirect (src/RedirectMiddleware.php:205-209). The fragment is client-side and was never sent to the original server, so a redirect destination controlled by an attacker learns one-time secrets, tokens or state values. The 7.15.1 fix adds withFragment("") before serialising the URI.

CookieJar does not record that a Set-Cookie without a Domain attribute (or with an empty one) is host-only: extractCookies() writes the request host into the cookie Domain and SetCookie::matchesDomain() then applies ordinary domain matching, so a host-only cookie set by example.com is also sent to child.example.com (src/Cookie/CookieJar.php:239-244). FileCookieJar and SessionCookieJar persist the widened scope as well. The 7.15.1 fix adds a HostOnly flag (SetCookie::getHostOnly/setHostOnly), sets it in extractCookies(), includes it in cookie identity, matches it case-insensitively in matchesDomain(), and persists it in the file and session jars.

SetCookie::matchesDomain() decides whether a cookie Domain is an IP literal or numeric host from the domain text alone: isIpAddressOrNumericHost() accepts FILTER_VALIDATE_IP or an all-numeric rightmost label and nothing else, so hexadecimal and mixed-base spellings such as 0x7f000001 and a percent-escaped Domain are treated as ordinary names and keep subdomain scope (src/Cookie/SetCookie.php:480-501). libcurl decodes both spellings to an address, so a sibling/parent-domain cookie is selected for a different host. The 7.15.2 fix adds an inet_aton-style numeric-host check (HostValidator::isNumericIpv4Host) and treats any percent-escaped cookie domain as exact-match-only.

CurlFactory::getDefaultConf() gives libcurl the request URI as text in CURLOPT_URL while the request headers (including Host) are passed separately in _headers (src/Handler/CurlFactory.php:1744-1747); libcurl percent-decodes and IDNA-maps the authority itself and connects to that host while the origin receives the unnormalised Host value. A URI such as http://127.0.0.%31/ is not an IP literal to filter_var() but reaches loopback, so an application allow/deny check on the URI text can be bypassed. The 7.15.2 fix adds HostValidator::assertRequestHost(), called from CurlHandler, CurlMultiHandler and StreamHandler, plus Client::shouldPreserveHost() so an aligned Host header is regenerated.

basis: importAnalysisPlugin records a URL-derived filesystem path in moduleGraph.safeModulesPath. At importAnalysis.ts:531-538 it calls normalizeUrl(specifier, start), then adds fsPathFromUrl(stripBase(url, base)) — the browser URL converted to a path — instead of the resolved module id. fsPathFromUrl only forces a leading slash, so an in-root import whose URL is /etc/hostname is recorded as the absolute host path /etc/hostname. isFileServingAllowed (static.ts:218) accepts safeModulesPath entries before consulting server.fs.allow, so a later /@fs/etc/hostname request returns the host file. The fix stores cleanUrl(resolvedId) instead.

getHtmlFilename() joins the request URL onto the project root without removing its query string: indexHtml.ts:100-104 runs path.join(server.config.root, url.slice(1)) so a request such as //evil.example/payload.js?/../../package.json resolves the .. segments and yields an existing project file (package.json), while Chromium treats /../../package.json as query text. devHtmlHook then reuses the attacker-supplied htmlPath as proxyModuleUrl (lines 192-195) and writes it into the generated inline-module src, so a malicious site can make the dev-server page load its own script. The fix cleans the URL before path.join and collapses leading // in htmlPath.

serveStaticMiddleware decides server.fs.deny access with ensureServingAccess on the request path before handing the request to sirv. A target such as /.env/. passes that check (the deny glob sees .env/. rather than .env) while sirv normalizes the path and serves root/.env, disclosing files matched by fs.deny patterns (CWE-22). The fix removes this pre-resolution check and enforces the deny decision inside sirv via shouldServe/checkLoadingAccess on the resolved file path; frozen line 151 is the removed call.

On Windows the fs.deny check does not normalize alternate NTFS path forms. isFileServingAllowed (static.ts:212-216) applies the deny globs to the URL-derived path and has no rejection for an alternate data stream suffix or an 8.3 short name, so /.env::$DATA?raw (or a short name containing ~) does not match .env in _fsDenyGlob, passes the allow check, and Windows resolves it to the original file. The fix rejects any path containing ~ and any path with a colon after an optional drive letter when running on Windows.

basis: Rack::Multipart::Parser.parse_boundary matches the Content-Type with the greedy MULTIPART regex (lib/rack/multipart/parser.rb:34) "\Amultipart/.*boundary=\"?([^\";,]+)\"?" and returns capture group 1 (parser.rb:84). The leading ".*" is greedy, so a header containing several boundary parameters resolves to the last one, while an intermediary that honours the first parameter inspects a different body structure than the one Rack parses. The 3.1.21 fix makes the prefix lazy, captures the whitespace between "boundary" and "=" to raise on it, and rejects a second boundary parameter with BoundaryTooLongError.

Rack::Multipart::Parser#handle_mime_head parses a quoted Content-Disposition parameter by repeatedly searching for the next quote or backslash with String#index, copying the prefix into a new string and deleting it with String#slice! (parser.rb:337-358). Each escape therefore re-scans and re-copies the remaining value, so a part whose name is a long run of backslash escapes costs super-linear time; with up to 4095 parts per request and a 1536-byte disposition cap the work stays within the default limits while the CPU cost grows with the square of the escape count. The 3.1.21 fix counts quoted escapes and raises Error once they pass CONTENT_DISPOSITION_QUOTED_ESCAPES_LIMIT (8 KiB).

Rack::Directory::DirectoryBody#each strips the configured root from the displayed path with path.sub(/^#{root}/, '') (lib/rack/directory.rb:54). The root is a developer-configured filesystem path that was expanded with File.expand_path and is interpolated into the regex without Regexp.escape, so metacharacters such as "+", "*" or "." change the match: the prefix is not removed and the absolute filesystem path is rendered into the directory listing HTML, exposing deployment layout. The 3.1.21 fix anchors the match at \A and escapes the root.

Rack::Multipart::Parser.parse wraps the body in BoundedIO only when content_length is non-nil (parser.rb:99), and read_data (parser.rb:258-261) reads @bufsize bytes per call with no cumulative accounting. A chunked multipart/form-data request without Content-Length therefore streams to disk through Tempfile with no total byte limit, so an unauthenticated client can fill the disk. The 3.1.21 fix adds PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT (10 GiB default, RACK_MULTIPART_PARSER_BYTESIZE_LIMIT), rejects a declared Content-Length above it in parse(), and counts bytes read in read_data.

Rack::Utils.select_best_encoding expands Accept-Encoding entries and, for every wildcard entry, recomputes accept_encoding.map(&:first) inside the loop (lib/rack/utils.rb:197-207). With N wildcard entries that is N scans of the parsed header, i.e. quadratic work, and the resulting expanded list is then walked again with per-entry delete. Rack::Deflater calls the method for every response when enabled, so one request with a crafted Accept-Encoding header burns CPU. The 3.1.21 fix truncates the parsed header to the first 16 encodings, expands the wildcard at most once, and replaces sort_by with a comparator that keeps the existing ordering.

Rack::Utils.forwarded_values splits the RFC 7239 Forwarded header on ";" before it parses individual name=value pairs (lib/rack/utils.rb:153) and then splits each field on "," and "=". A quoted value may legally contain semicolons, so Forwarded: for="127.0.0.1;host=evil.com;proto=https" is read as several directives instead of one quoted for value. In deployments where an upstream proxy or WAF validates the quoted value as a single string, the client smuggles host, proto, for or by parameters past that inspection and Rack applies them to the request URL. The 3.1.21 fix replaces the split-based scan with a stateful parser that handles quoted strings and backslash escapes, allows only by/for/host/proto through ALLOWED_FORWARED_PARAMS, and caps parameters and escapes at 1024.

Rack::Multipart::Parser#handle_mime_head extracts the part Content-Type and Content-Disposition values from the folded header block (parser.rb:309-311) and passes them straight to the parameter scanner, with no RFC 5322 Section 2.2.3 obs-fold unfolding. A header such as filename="test\r\n foo.txt" therefore yields a parsed filename that still contains CRLF, and an application that reuses that value in a response header is exposed to header injection or response splitting. The 3-1-stable backport adds OBS_UNFOLD = \r\n([ \t]) and gsubs both the content type and the disposition before scanning.

Rack::Files#fail builds the 404/405 response headers with CONTENT_LENGTH => body.size.to_s (lib/rack/files.rb:197). String#size counts characters, not bytes, so a body containing multibyte UTF-8 declares a Content-Length smaller than the bytes actually written. Rack::Files reflects the decoded request path in its error body, so a request for a missing path with percent-encoded UTF-8 characters triggers the mismatch, and a server that frames the response from the header desynchronises the connection. The 3.1.21 fix switches to body.bytesize.

ByteParser.run parses the 64-bit extended payload length as (upper << 8) + lower after rejecting only upper > 2^31 - 1 (lib/websocket/receiver.js:194-216 at v5.19.0). The shift is not a multiply by 2^32 and JavaScript turns it into a signed 32-bit value, so any upper word above 2^23 - 1 overflows to a negative or truncated payloadLength; the parser then leaves READ_DATA with a bogus length, consumes the wrong number of bytes from the socket buffer and the client throws an uncaught TypeError that terminates the process. A malicious WebSocket server chooses the length. The 6.24.0 fix rejects any non-zero upper word or lower > 2^31 - 1 and uses lower directly (5a97f0893b53ba7d1d5549d3df7e55d9c2673f89). The 5.x line has no fix.

The defect is in the retry interceptor: the 6.28.0 fix (1b5a5312c3a7d7a30c31bf0d000b39a8a2531e1c and its 7.x/8.x counterparts) touches only lib/handler/retry-handler.js and test/interceptors/retry.js. At v5.19.0 lib/handler/ contains just DecoratorHandler.js and RedirectHandler.js, lib/interceptor/ only redirectInterceptor.js, and index.js exports no RetryHandler and no interceptors namespace. The retry API whose response framing the advisory describes does not exist, so the root cause is absent rather than merely untriggered. The OSV range introduced 0 / fixed 6.28.0 is the GitHub first-branch row (< 6.28.0) rendered without its lower bound.
notes: Retry interceptor (lib/handler/retry-handler.js) does not exist at v5.19.0.

basis: The crash needs the client to negotiate permessage-deflate and then create an InflateRaw with an out-of-range server_max_window_bits. At v5.19.0 connection.js:83 sets permessageDeflate = "" with the TODO "enable once permessage-deflate is supported", the Sec-WebSocket-Extensions append at :87 is commented out, and a server that answers with the extension is failed at :159-161. ByteParser takes only (ws) and holds no extension map; there is no lib/websocket/permessage-deflate.js and no isValidClientWindowBits. The 6.24.0 fix (e9e2997ed18b) edits permessage-deflate.js and util.js, neither of which exists here.
notes: permessage-deflate is not negotiated at v5.19.0 (connection.js:83, :159-161).

basis: The decompression bomb needs permessage-deflate: PerMessageDeflate.decompress accumulates inflate output without a limit. At v5.19.0 the extension is never offered (connection.js:83, TODO at :82), an unsolicited extension in the response fails the connection (:159-161), and the receiver has no PerMessageDeflate at all. The 6.24.0 fix (4b4f93ae292f, maxDecompressedMessageSize) adds code to lib/web/websocket/permessage-deflate.js, absent from the frozen tree.

basis: The advisory states all releases starting at undici 6.17.0 are affected, and the fix backs that up: the 6.27.0 backport b7f252e7c084 ("Backport WebSocket maxPayloadSize fixes") changes the maxPayloadSize bookkeeping in receiver.js/websocket.js and adds test/websocket/fragments.js. maxPayloadSize does not exist at v5.19.0 at all (no occurrence anywhere under lib/), and the receiver constructor takes only (ws), so there is no byte cap for the fragment count to bypass. The frozen parser does accumulate #fragments with no cap, but that is a different, unassigned weakness; this CVE's root cause (a size check that ignores the number of continuation frames) is absent.

basis: Inner::complete calls State::set_complete, which at 1.8.0 is a single fetch_or(VALUE_SENT, AcqRel) (tokio/src/sync/oneshot.rs:854-860). Sender::send stores the value in the Inner UnsafeCell at :310-315 and then calls complete(); if Receiver::close or Receiver::drop has already set CLOSED, set_complete still sets VALUE_SENT, so both sides touch the cell: send sees prev.is_closed(), returns Err and takes the value back through consume_value() (:318-320, value.with_mut(...take()) at :800-801) while a concurrent poll_recv/try_recv that observed VALUE_SENT reads the same cell (:664, :734). Two with_mut accesses from different threads are a data race on the value (CWE-362; memory-corruption class). The fix e0cf906a replaces the fetch_or with a compare-and-swap loop that stops when CLOSED is already set, so VALUE_SENT is never published on a closed channel, and was released in 1.8.4/1.13.1. The pre-image at the frozen tag is identical to the fix hunk and the patch applies with git apply --check.

ServerOptions::pipe_mode assigns the whole dwPipeMode DWORD from the selected PipeMode (tokio/src/net/windows/named_pipe.rs:1449-1456), which silently clears PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS. That flag is set by default in ServerOptions::new (:1433) and is manipulated as a bit flag by reject_remote_clients() (:1730-1732), so a server that calls pipe_mode() after configuring, or without configuring, remote-client rejection ends up with dwPipeMode = PIPE_TYPE_BYTE only and accepts remote (SMB) clients, exposing a local IPC endpoint to the network. The fix 9ca156c0b80347bb7b1406c6050d602f22efc709 sets only the 0x4 PIPE_TYPE_MESSAGE bit with bool_flag! so unrelated flags survive, adds unit tests, and was released in 1.18.4/1.20.3/1.23.1. The module is cfg(windows) and not compiled on the Linux checkout, but the source is present at the frozen tag and the patch applies with git apply --check.

ReadHalf::unsplit reunites the halves by Arc::try_unwrap on Inner<T> and then calling UnsafeCell::into_inner on stream (tokio/src/io/split.rs:77-89; Inner is { locked: AtomicBool, stream: UnsafeCell<T> } at :52-55). The halves give out Pin<&mut T> through AsyncRead/AsyncWrite, and at 1.8.0 unsplit had no T: Unpin bound, so a !Unpin stream can be moved out after it has been pinned - a violation of the Pin contract that makes the public API unsound. The fix d6ea7a742b92d3e516035a584ab9347a96be363a adds `where T: Unpin` and was released in 1.18.5/1.20.4/1.24.2. The pre-image is identical to the 1.18.x fix hunk and the patch applies with git apply --check.

At 1.8.0 broadcast slots are Box<[RwLock<Slot<T>>]> (tokio/src/sync/broadcast.rs:297-300) holding a bare UnsafeCell<Option<T>> val (:327-346), and RecvGuard::clone_value calls T::clone through the shared read guard (:1060-1065; RecvGuard holds an RwLockReadGuard at :364-365). Because RwLock allows several readers, two receivers can clone the same value concurrently, while the channel only requires T: Send (unsafe impls at :468-472) - a Send-but-not-Sync T whose Clone touches non-atomic interior state is then cloned from two threads at once, which is undefined behaviour (RUSTSEC memory-corruption class). The fix 4b174ce2c95fe1d1a217917db93fcc935e17e0da replaces the RwLock with a Mutex so clones are serialized, stores the value as a plain Option<T>, and drops the manual Send/Sync impls; it was released in 1.38.2/1.43.1/1.44.2. The changed clone_value and drop lines are textually identical at the frozen tag.

AsyncFd::new / with_interest are safe functions that accept any T: AsRawFd and never require proof that the descriptor is owned and stays open (tokio/src/io/async_fd.rs:175-196). They cache inner.as_raw_fd() and hand it to Registration::new_with_interest_and_handle (:197-205); since RawFd itself implements AsRawFd, safe code can pass a bare descriptor it later closes or that the process reuses. The io driver packs a pointer to the ScheduledIo slab entry into the mio token when the source is registered (tokio/src/io/driver/mod.rs:320-340) and deregisters by descriptor number through SourceFd, so a caller-supplied descriptor that is closed or reused while the AsyncFd is alive leaves the driver with a stale token and can deregister another resource's descriptor - the I/O-safety violation RUSTSEC describes as leading to use-after-free in the readiness path. The fix fb57e675b0dcdd45f251e286b5ddcd96607e1e90 (PR #8587) makes registration an unsafe fn `register`/`register_with_interest` and deprecates the safe constructors; it was released in 1.51.6/1.53.3/1.54.0. The safe constructor half of the advisory applies at 1.8.0; the AsyncFd: AsFd half does not, because no AsFd impl exists anywhere in the 1.8.0 tree.

basis: In storeAtts, every attribute whose value is not already normalized and whose ATTRIBUTE_ID has maybeTokenized set searches elementType->defaultAtts linearly for a matching id to learn whether the attribute was declared as other than CDATA (expat/lib/xmlparse.c:3453-3461).  With N specified attributes and N matching default-attribute declarations that inner scan runs once per attribute, so one element carrying a few hundred thousand attributes costs O(N^2) comparisons and a document of a few megabytes pins a CPU core (CWE-407).  The fix f8f7c4ffd883e3c2c58f0ebb49416a6c1d248738 (PR #1321, merged as e97a6c45 and released in 2.8.4) replaces the scan with a lookup in elementType->defaultAttForName, a hash table keyed by attribute name; the preceding commit 98f5acc1 in the same PR renames that table from defaultAttsNames.  At the frozen 2.6.2 tree the loop is present verbatim except that the loop variable is declared as `int j` (the fix hunk's pre-image uses `size_t j`), and the defaultAttForName/defaultAttsNames table does not exist yet, so the 2.8.x patch does not apply wholesale; the defect site itself matches the fix pre-image.

doContent allocates a TAG (88 bytes on amd64) plus a separate INIT_TAG_BUF_SIZE buffer (32 bytes, expat/lib/xmlparse.c:260) for every opening tag that is not served from parser->m_freeTagList, and keeps each one on parser->m_tagStack until its end tag is seen (expat/lib/xmlparse.c:2981-2989).  A document made of deeply nested 3-byte tags (`<x>`) therefore pins at least sizeof(TAG)+32 = 120 bytes of dynamic memory per 3 input bytes, and at 2.6.2 nothing accounts for these allocations against the input size.  Upstream issue #1018 measured the effect with EXPAT_ACCOUNTING_DEBUG on a 240 KiB payload: direct 240562 bytes vs 16.7 MB indirect, amplification 70.77, and the existing billion-laughs accounting (which only counts DTD/entity expansion) does not stop it.  The shipped fix, PR #1034 merged as ac7a27e1f034c06e6be590ce98c36db9f8f5eedc and released in 2.7.2, does not change this block: it tracks dynamic allocations in the MALLOC/FREE macros (core commit cfce28e171676fe6f70d17b97ed8a59eaeb83f15) and aborts when tracked allocations pass 64 MiB and exceed 100x the direct input bytes, which caps the amplification that issue #1018 located at this allocation.  The anchor is that allocation site, verified verbatim at the frozen SHA; the evidence is source review, not a fix hunk at the site.

basis: At v/0.23.4 both public client session types derive Debug (Tls13ClientSessionValue at rustls/src/msgs/persist.rs:71-78 and Tls12ClientSessionValue at :138), and the ClientSessionCommon they embed derives Debug too (:204-210) while holding the resumption secret as `secret: Zeroizing<PayloadU8>` (:207).  PayloadU8 has a manual Debug that hex-dumps its bytes (rustls/src/msgs/base.rs:189-193) and zeroize 1.7.0 derives Debug for Zeroizing, so the derived Debug of a session value prints the TLS 1.3 resumption PSK (or the TLS 1.2 master secret) as hex.  The types are part of the public API - rustls/src/lib.rs:560 re-exports both from rustls::client, and ClientSessionStore returns them - so any application that logs a retrieved session value, or an error payload that contains one, writes the secret to its logs.  The v/0.23.46 fix dcdb9464 removes both derives and hand-writes Debug impls that skip `secret`; its regression test asserts that the formatted value does not contain the 0xa5 secret bytes.

handle_server_hello (rustls/src/client/tls13.rs:61) writes the group the server selected into the per-name session store with set_kx_hint (:150-154) immediately after completing the key exchange (:146) and before any certificate or Finished message is verified.  If the handshake later fails - for example a network attacker answers a connection attempt with a ServerHello it cannot authenticate and then drops the connection - the hint survives in the store.  initial_key_share (:200-220) then reads kx_hint (:207) for the same server name and starts exactly one key exchange in that group, so every later ClientHello for that name carries a share only for the attacker-chosen group even though the client supports others.  At v/0.23.4 the configured providers have no hybrid/PQ group, so the advisory's classical-only downgrade scenario cannot be reproduced literally at this tag; the pre-authentication cache-poisoning primitive and its effect on later ClientHellos are nevertheless present.  The v/0.23.46 fix f04804fa removes the early set_kx_hint call, threads kx_group through ExpectEncryptedExtensions and ExpectCertificateOrCompressedCertificateOrCertReq, and writes the hint only in ExpectFinished after the handshake is authenticated.

basis: ReadComments (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Gif/GifDecoderCore.cs:381) drives its loop with `while ((length = stream.ReadByte()) != 0)`, so the -1 that ReadByte returns at end of stream enters the body as a block length.  The only length guard is `length > GifConstants.MaxCommentSubBlockLength`, which -1 passes.  With SkipMetadata set, the body executes `stream.Seek(length, SeekOrigin.Current)` (:396) and rewinds one byte, so a comment extension with a missing terminator keeps the reader bouncing at the end of the stream instead of finishing the block; without SkipMetadata the negative length goes straight into `memoryAllocator.Allocate<byte>(length)` (:399).  A crafted GIF with an unterminated comment block therefore hangs (or faults) any decoder that identifies or loads untrusted input, for example an image service that re-encodes uploads.  The v3.1.11 backport f4a26847 adds an explicit `if (length == -1) throw ... "Unexpected end of stream while reading gif comment"` right after the max-length check, and its regression test asserts InvalidImageContentException for Identify and Load both with and without SkipMetadata.

TiffCcittCompressor.Initialize (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Tiff/Compression/Compressors/TiffCcittCompressor.cs:527) sizes the shared output buffer as `int maxNeededBytes = this.Width * rowsPerStrip`, i.e. one byte (eight bits) per pixel, while the Group 3 encoder emits up to a 13-bit terminating code per pixel plus a 12-bit EOL and an 8-bit zero-length white run per row.  T4BitCompressor.CompressStrip (T4BitCompressor.cs:39) then writes through WriteCode (TiffCcittCompressor.cs:466), which advances bytePosition and calls BitWriterUtils.WriteBit; that helper does `Unsafe.Add(ref MemoryMarshal.GetReference(buffer), bufferPos)` with no bounds check, so a bi-level image with alternating pixels (the worst case for the run-length codes) writes past the pooled buffer.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 adds an abstract GetMaximumEncodedBits, implements it for T4 as `12 + ((Width * 13) + 20) * rowsPerStrip` bits, sizes Initialize from it, and makes WriteCode throw InvalidMemoryOperationException when the remaining bits are insufficient.

ColorNumerics.GetBT709Luminance (src/ImageSharp/Common/Helpers/ColorNumerics.cs:29) returns `(int)MathF.Round(Vector4.Dot(vector, Bt709) * (luminanceLevels - 1))` without clamping the dot product to [0, 1] or rejecting NaN.  Floating-point pixel formats can hold components outside their normalized range (and operations such as Normalize or convolution can produce NaN), so the rounded value can fall below 0 or above luminanceLevels - 1.  GrayscaleLevelsRowOperation{TPixel} (src/ImageSharp/Processing/Processors/Normalization/GrayscaleLevelsRowOperation{TPixel}.cs:60) passes that value to `Interlocked.Increment(ref Unsafe.Add(ref histogramBase, (uint)luminance))`, an unchecked write into a 65536-entry histogram, so a crafted float image drives the histogram-equalization processor out of the histogram allocation; GlobalHistogramEqualizationProcessor{TPixel}.cs:133 and AutoLevelProcessor{TPixel}.cs:152 make the same call.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 replaces the expression with a body that returns 0 for NaN and clamps the luminance to [0, 1] before scaling.

TiffCcittCompressor.Initialize (src/ImageSharp/Formats/Tiff/Compression/Compressors/TiffCcittCompressor.cs:527) allocates Width * rowsPerStrip bytes for every CCITT strip, but the Group 4 encoder needs up to 16 bits per pixel plus row transition overhead and a final 24-bit EOFB.  T6BitCompressor.CompressStrip (T6BitCompressor.cs:53) emits pass, vertical and horizontal mode codes through WriteCode (TiffCcittCompressor.cs:466), whose bit writes go through BitWriterUtils.WriteBit and an unchecked `Unsafe.Add` on the destination span, so a bi-level image with alternating pixels drives bytePosition past the end of the pooled buffer.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 adds GetMaximumEncodedBits for T6 as `((Width * 16) + 24) * rowsPerStrip + 24` bits, sizes Initialize from it, and makes WriteCode throw when the remaining bits are insufficient.

ExifReader.ReadValues64 (src/ImageSharp/Metadata/Profiles/Exif/ExifReader.cs:199) seeks to the IFD offset, reads the 64-bit entry count from the file, and loops `for (ulong i = 0; i < count; i++) this.ReadValue64(values, offsetBuffer)`.  ReadValue64 (:418) starts with `if ((this.data.Length - this.data.Position) < 20) return;`, so once fewer than 20 bytes remain it returns without reading anything or advancing the stream position.  A BigTIFF whose first IFD declares a count larger than the remaining data therefore keeps iterating without progress for the full declared count (up to 2^64-1), pinning the decoding thread.  The v3.2.0 fix baa37cd1 bounds the count with the bytes actually available - `remainingDirectoryBytes = data.Length - data.Position` must cover the 8-byte next-IFD offset plus 20 bytes per entry - and throws InvalidImageContentException otherwise.

AuthenticationProcessingFilter2 (core/src/main/java/hudson/security/AuthenticationProcessingFilter2.java:55) is the Spring Security filter registered for the authentication gateway URL `j_spring_security_check` (SecurityRealm.java:223-228, instantiated at :599).  At 2.441 it extends UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter and overrides only successfulAuthentication (:66) and unsuccessfulAuthentication (:93); it does not override attemptAuthentication, so the POST that carries j_username/j_password is authenticated without any Jenkins crumb validation.  The login form (core/src/main/resources/jenkins/model/Jenkins/login.jelly:77-78) posts only `from`, `j_username` and `j_password`, and the setup wizard token form posts the same way, so neither carries a crumb.  A cross-site form can therefore submit the attacker's credentials to /j_spring_security_check with the victim's browser: the victim is silently logged into the attacker's account (login CSRF), and work the victim performs afterwards is stored in that account.  The fix 31598feb adds an attemptAuthentication override that fetches the CrumbIssuer, reads the crumb from the request parameter or header and throws InsufficientAuthenticationException when it does not validate (with a SKIP_CSRF_CHECK system property as an escape hatch), and adds the hidden `${h.getCrumbRequestField()}` / `${h.getCrumb(request2)}` inputs to login.jelly and SetupWizard/authenticate-security-token.jelly.

SECURITY-3625 fixes the authenticated-user profile dropdown by wrapping the action list of core/src/main/resources/jenkins/model/navigation/UserAction/jumplist.jelly in app.hasPermission(app.READ). Neither that file nor the jenkins/model/navigation package exists at 2.441 (git history: the file was introduced on 2025-04-18 by c42ab43c49, "Redesign the Jenkins header (#10245)"), and no jumplist/JumpList symbol appears anywhere under core/src at the SHA. The 2.441 header (core/src/main/resources/jenkins/views/JenkinsHeader/headerContent.jelly) renders only the profile link and the logout link, so the dropdown menu whose options the advisory says leak (e.g. whether the Credentials plugin is installed) does not exist at this snapshot.
notes: the affected dropdown UI was introduced after 2.441 by the header redesign

basis: In getResolveRoutes (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.ts:399-407) the i18n handling for a normal request prepends the default locale (lines 198-210), but for a /_next/data request it only records `__nextLocale` from normalizeLocalePath and never inserts the default locale into the path. The middleware therefore receives a different pathname than the one the page router resolves, so a middleware/proxy matcher can be bypassed by requesting the data route directly. The fix 6c72e0b4ee normalizes the data-route path with the same locale prefixing as a page request.

The INTERNAL_HEADERS list in packages/next/src/server/lib/server-ipc/utils.ts:42-51 has eight entries but omits `x-nextjs-data` and `x-next-resume-state-length`.  Those headers are therefore passed through from an untrusted request into the internal render/redirect path, where a middleware redirect can be turned into a response that a shared cache stores under the attacker's URL.  The fix ac51823b5b adds the two names to the internal-header filter.

Script (packages/next/src/client/script.tsx:340-344) serializes the props of a beforeInteractive script with JSON.stringify and interpolates the result into `(self.__next_s=self.__next_s||[]).push(...)` with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.  JSON.stringify escapes quotes but not `<`, so a `</script>` sequence in an untrusted prop closes the inline script element and executes attacker markup.  The fix 086dfa7f8f escapes `<` to `\u003c` (and the same for the second push site) before embedding.

getScriptNonceFromHeader (packages/next/src/server/app-render/get-script-nonce-from-header.tsx:43-50) accepts a nonce from the Content-Security-Policy request header unless it matches ESCAPE_REGEX `/[&><\u2028\u2029]/g`; `"` is not in that class, so a nonce containing a quote survives and is interpolated into the response CSP header and script tags, breaking out of the attribute.  The fix 79d7dff144 rejects the nonce when ESCAPE_REGEX matches and also strips a leading quote.

The upgrade handler in initialize (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts:699-700) proxies every request whose parsed URL has a protocol, including the URL taken from an upgrade request line.  An attacker that opens a WebSocket upgrade with an absolute `ws://`/`http://` URL makes the Next.js server issue the proxied request to that host.  The fix c4f69086cc restricts proxying to the configured host/basePath and rejects absolute URLs on the upgrade path.

fetchInternalImage (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:612) concatenates every buffered chunk of the internal image response into one Buffer with no length cap, and the surrounding call path has no readableLimit.  An attacker can point the image optimizer at a local route that streams an arbitrarily large body and exhaust server memory.  The fix 3f1b7b7501 enforces a maximum upstream body size before buffering.

fetchExternalImage (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:576) reads the entire upstream response with `res.arrayBuffer()` before any size check, so a remote host allowed by a broad remotePatterns entry can return a multi-gigabyte body and exhaust the server.  The 15.x fix 39a2f6a8d1 caps the upstream body size and rejects oversized responses for both the internal and external paths.

prepareDestination (packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/prepare-destination.ts:209) calls `compile(destHostname, { validate: false })`, so an attacker-controlled destination hostname supplied through a rewrite parameter is not constrained to a static pattern and the rewritten request can be sent to an attacker host.  The fix 35f501357e validates the compiled hostname and only allows parameters in the path portion.

handleAction (packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts:570) takes the edge branch and calls `await webRequest.request.formData()` with no body-size guard, while the node branches enforce `readableLimit` at lines 627 and 696.  A crafted multipart action request in the edge runtime is therefore fully buffered, blocking the worker.  The fix 57c31f724d adds the same size limit and streaming guard to the edge branch.

getFilePath (packages/next/src/server/lib/incremental-cache/file-system-cache.ts:442-461) builds the on-disk path with `path.join(this.serverDistDir, kind, pathname)` without checking that the resolved path stays under the cache directory, and escapePathDelimiters only rewrites `/`, `#`, `?` and their percent-encodings, not `\`.  On Windows a cache key containing `..\..\` therefore escapes the cache directory and lets an unauthenticated requester write attacker-controlled cache files, which the fix advisory ties to code execution.  The fix b0f3460a92 adds a path-containment check and treats `\` as a delimiter (second fix 968b9fcb26 backports it to 15.5.x).

In initialize (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts:303) the development branch forwards a request to the development bundler as soon as `developmentBundler` is set, without checking the Origin/Host of the request.  A malicious page can therefore read dev-server responses cross-origin.  The fix f523d4a142 inserts a `blockCrossSite` check (new lib/block-cross-site.ts) immediately after the `if (developmentBundler) {` line.

packages/next/src/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/package.json:50-51 pins the vendored React server-dom package to `18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218`.  That flight decoder has no guard against cyclic thenables / repeated `$$consumed` processing, so a crafted RSC request consumes unbounded CPU.  The 14.2.34 fix 8e43882798 updates exactly those two lines to the 2025-12-09 build (`3e107bf495`), which carries the upstream hardening; no source file in the 14.2.24 tree contains a `cyclic thenables` or `$$consumed` guard.

fetchServerResponse (packages/next/src/client/components/router-reducer/fetch-server-response.ts:87-93) derives the `_rsc` cache-busting parameter from `hexHash([...].join(","))`, and hexHash (packages/next/src/shared/lib/hash.ts:17-19) is djb2 reduced to 32 bits and then `toString(36).slice(0, 5)`.  Two different router states/prefetch URLs can therefore produce the same `_rsc` value, and a cached RSC payload for one URL is served for the other.  The 15.5.16 fix 8c96fec056 replaces the truncated hash with a full-length digest (the 15.x refactor moves it into a helper that does not exist at 14.2.24; the anchored hexHash design is the same defect, hence source_review evidence).

renderToHTMLOrFlightImpl (packages/next/src/server/app-render/app-render.tsx:811) sets `isRSCRequest` from `req.headers[RSC_HEADER.toLowerCase()] !== undefined`, accepting any header value, while base-server.ts:3501 uses the strict comparison `=== '1'`.  A request with e.g. `RSC: 0` is rendered as an RSC response and can be cached under a URL whose normal response differs.  The fix 3e247110b3 makes the app-render check use the same strict value test as the base server.

fetchInternalImage (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:594-599) builds the mocked internal request with `headers: _req.headers` (line 597), forwarding the caller's Accept and other headers to the image API route.  A page-router API route that serves images can therefore be made to answer with an attacker-chosen content type/filename and the optimizer returns it as a downloadable response.  The fix 6b12c60c61 removes the `headers` field from that mock.

The same header pass-through at packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:594-599 means the mocked internal request can vary by Cookie/Authorization while the optimizer caches the result only by href+width+quality+mimeType.  A response tailored to one user is then served to unauthorized users.  The fix 6b12c60c61 stops forwarding the caller headers, making the internal image response independent of the request.

In getResolveRoutes (packages/next/src/server/lib/router-utils/resolve-routes.ts:641-651) the presence of a `location` header on the middleware response unconditionally rewrites `parsedUrl` to that value and returns `finished: true`, regardless of the response status.  `NextResponse.next()` with a Location header that is not a redirect (e.g. copied from the request) therefore turns into an internal request to an attacker-controlled absolute URL.  The fix 9c9aaed5bb only treats Location as a redirect when the status is in `allowedStatusCodes`, otherwise it passes the header through.

ImageOptimizerCache.set (packages/next/src/server/image-optimizer.ts:388-401) writes every optimized variant with `writeToCacheDir` and never evicts or caps the number/size of entries.  An attacker can request many unique width/quality/URL combinations and fill the disk.  The fix 39eb8e0ac4 adds an LRU disk cache and the `images.maximumDiskCacheSize` option (new lib/disk-lru-cache.external.ts) and enforces it on write.

createServerModuleMap (packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-utils.ts:17-30) returns a Proxy whose `get` indexes the server actions manifest with the raw client-supplied id and returns a module entry for it without validating the id format or checking that the page may use it.  Combined with action ids present in public client chunks, an unauthenticated caller can invoke/locate Server Function endpoints that are normally behind auth.  The fixes ff12a6124e and 1b0c3ae912 add `mightBeServerReferenceId` validation and a `getInvalidServerReferenceIdError` to the manifest lookup.

IncrementalCache.fetchCacheKey (packages/next/src/server/lib/incremental-cache/index.ts:330-340) decodes each streamed body chunk with `new TextDecoder().decode(chunk, { stream: true })` and concatenates those strings into the cache key.  Non-UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD, so two different binary bodies can hash to the same key; a cached POST response body for one body is then returned for the other.  The fix 025bf4a5f7 replaces the decoded string with a byte-exact key computed from the raw chunks.

createPatchedFetcher (packages/next/src/server/lib/patch-fetch.ts:469-476) calls `incrementalCache.fetchCacheKey(fetchUrl, isRequestInput ? (input as RequestInit) : init)`, casting the Request object to RequestInit, so the init overrides passed as the second argument (method/body/headers) never enter the key.  Two calls to the same URL with different effective bodies share a key and the response body of one is served for the other.  The fix 062f6670 merges `new Request(url), init` into one effective Request before computing cacheability and the key (15.x backport 73b94872).

createForwardedActionResponse (packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts:182) computes the internal fetch origin as `process.env.__NEXT_PRIVATE_ORIGIN || `${proto}://${host.value}` `, and the redirect companion at :279 uses `originalHost.value`.  On a custom server without __NEXT_PRIVATE_ORIGIN the Host header is attacker-controlled, so a forwarded Server Action or app-relative redirect makes the server request an attacker host.  The fixes e3e5666cce and b512063218 derive the origin from the trusted `initURL` request meta instead.
