basis: HttpInvokerServiceExporter.readRemoteInvocation(HttpServletRequest, InputStream) at spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/remoting/httpinvoker/HttpInvokerServiceExporter.java:112-121 wraps the servlet request body in a CodebaseAwareObjectInputStream (createObjectInputStream(decorateInputStream(request, is))) and passes it to doReadRemoteInvocation, whose inherited implementation in RemoteInvocationSerializingExporter calls ois.readObject() on the attacker-supplied bytes (:139-147) with no ObjectInputFilter, allowlist or class restriction. A request to a Spring HTTP invoker service exported over HTTP therefore deserializes any gadget class on the server classpath. The advisory fixes this at 6.0.0 by removing the deprecated HTTP invoker; the 4.2.6/3.2.17 commits 5cbe90b2cd91 and 2b051b8b3217 only add a javadoc warning and deprecate the Sun JDK HTTP server support classes.

The private CachedIntrospectionResults(Class) constructor at spring-beans/src/main/java/org/springframework/beans/CachedIntrospectionResults.java:289-303 iterates every PropertyDescriptor returned by beanInfo.getPropertyDescriptors() and caches each one, skipping only Class.class classLoader and protectionDomain; read-only properties of non-bindable types are kept in the descriptor set used by data binding. The 5.2.22/5.3.20 fix 50177b1ad348 adds isInvalidReadOnlyPropertyType() (and a URL "content" skip), so read-only ClassLoader/ProtectionDomain/AutoCloseable properties are no longer introspected and cached. At 4.1.1 that guard does not exist, which is the state the advisory describes for applications that bind a MultipartFile or javax.servlet.Part field of a model object: repeated binding introspects the same non-bindable properties and exhausts CPU/memory.

SimpleBrokerMessageHandler.handleMessageInternal at spring-messaging/src/main/java/org/springframework/messaging/simp/broker/SimpleBrokerMessageHandler.java:156 handles every CONNECT frame by creating a CONNECT_ACK and sending it to the client outbound channel, with no check that the session is already connected; an authenticated client can loop CONNECT frames on one WebSocket session and make the broker allocate and dispatch unbounded acknowledgement/broker state. The 5.2.22/5.3.20 fix 159a99bbafdd adds `if (this.sessions.get(sessionId) != null) ... return;` to SimpleBrokerMessageHandler and the equivalent guard to StompBrokerRelayMessageHandler. At 4.1.1 the CONNECT branch has no duplicate-connection guard.

OperatorMatches.getValueInternal at spring-expression/src/main/java/org/springframework/expression/spel/ast/OperatorMatches.java:67 calls Pattern.compile((String) right) on every evaluation of the matches operator, and no pattern cache exists in 4.1.1: each evaluation of an attacker-supplied expression (or each distinct right-hand regex) compiles a fresh Pattern, so CPU time and temporary Pattern objects grow with the number of evaluations. The 5.2.23/5.3.26/6.0.7 fix 430fc25acad2 moves the cache into the parser as a shared ConcurrentMap<String, Pattern> patternCache passed to OperatorMatches, so each distinct pattern is compiled once. At 4.1.1 the compile call is unconditional and per-evaluation.

InternalSpelExpressionParser.doParseExpression at spring-expression/src/main/java/org/springframework/expression/spel/standard/InternalSpelExpressionParser.java:118-127 hands the whole expression string to the Tokenizer and builds the token stream without any length limit, so a user-supplied expression of arbitrary size is tokenized and parsed, consuming memory and CPU in proportion to the input. The 5.2.24/5.3.27/6.0.8 fix 965a6392757d adds MAX_EXPRESSION_LENGTH = 10_000 and checkExpressionLength() at the start of doParseExpression, rejecting longer expressions with SpelParseException. At 4.1.1 the method has no such guard.

StompSubProtocolHandler.handleMessageFromClient at spring-websocket/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/socket/messaging/StompSubProtocolHandler.java:184-228 decodes every client frame, stamps it with the WebSocket session id, session attributes and session.getPrincipal(), and forwards it to the client inbound channel; the CONNECT command only increments a statistics counter (:231). No per-session state tracks whether this session completed a CONNECT or which destination subscriptions belong to it, so a client can send MESSAGE/SUBSCRIBE frames without a valid CONNECT handshake, or reuse connection state across frames, and the STOMP application processes them as authenticated traffic (vendor: security bypass allowing unauthorized messages, CWE-352). The 6.2.12 fix c88bfc54c925 replaces stompAuthentications with a per-session SessionInfo map and guards both a repeated CONNECT and sends from an unknown session.

FileSystemResource.isReadable at spring-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/core/io/FileSystemResource.java:105-107 returns (this.file.canRead() && !this.file.isDirectory()) without checking that the file exists, so a path that has not been resolved yet is reported as a readable resource. When Spring MVC/WebFlux serves static resources from the file system on Windows, attacker-chosen paths that are slow to resolve are treated as resources and keep HTTP connections busy (vendor: denial of service while resolving static resources). The 6.2.18 fix 684b1e8a4b3d enforces the Resource#isReadable() contract by adding `this.file.exists() &&` to the check.

CachingResourceResolver.resolveResourceInternal at spring-webmvc/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/servlet/resource/CachingResourceResolver.java:64 builds the cache key as RESOLVED_RESOURCE_CACHE_KEY_PREFIX + requestPath only. The resolved resource also depends on the configured locations and on the request content coding, so two requests that differ only in those inputs share one cache entry and a client can be served a resource resolved for different inputs (CWE-524 information disclosure through the shared static-resource cache). The 6.2.19 fix 46867fad81dc includes Integer.toHexString(locations.hashCode()) and the content coding in the key.

AbstractVersionStrategy.removeVersion at spring-webmvc/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/servlet/resource/AbstractVersionStrategy.java:114-116 rewrites a versioned request path with StringUtils.delete(requestPath, "-" + version), which removes every occurrence of the version substring instead of the single trailing version token. An attacker-controlled path that repeats the version marker is therefore rewritten into a different path than the version strategy produced, and resolving versioned resources for such paths drives the algorithmic DoS the advisory describes. The 6.2.19 fix 8d51f47357e4 enforces single-version removal: removeVersion() removes only the last occurrence and VersionResourceResolver additionally rejects ignored input paths.

VersionResourceResolver.resolveResourceInternal at spring-webmvc/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/servlet/resource/VersionResourceResolver.java:151-156 strips the extracted version from the request path and resolves the resulting simplePath through the resolver chain without calling ResourceHandlerUtils.shouldIgnoreInputPath(simplePath); a crafted versioned request path can therefore reach a path that the resource handler would otherwise reject (a path whose removal of the version prefix leaves an invalid or traversal-looking remainder), and the resolved resource is read outside the intended static location (CWE-22). The 6.2.19 fix 8d51f47357e4 adds the shouldIgnoreInputPath check in both the Servlet and Reactive VersionResourceResolver.

DefaultRequestToViewNameTranslator.getViewName at spring-webmvc/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/servlet/view/DefaultRequestToViewNameTranslator.java:175-178 builds the view name as prefix + transformPath(lookupPath) + suffix with no check of the resulting name. For a "/**" mapping that does not set an explicit view name, a request path that transforms into a view name starting with the special "redirect:" or "forward:" prefix is handled by the view resolver as a redirect, so an attacker can craft a link that makes the application answer 302 to an arbitrary external host (CWE-601). The 6.2.19 fix 3aaec987651c rejects the redirect:/forward: prefixes in getViewName, with the same guard in the WebFlux ViewResolutionResultHandler (7add5243b9db).

ExpressionState.operate at spring-expression/src/main/java/org/springframework/expression/spel/ExpressionState.java:189-200 dispatches every operator evaluation to the configured OperatorOverloader and returns the result without counting how many operations the expression performs, so a specially crafted user-supplied expression that nests or repeats operations drives an algorithmically expensive evaluation with no upper bound (CWE-407). The 6.2.19 fix 76a36dfd707c adds an operations counter to ExpressionState (operationsCount, trackOperation()) fed by a new DEFAULT_MAX_OPERATIONS = 10_000 in SpelParserConfiguration and the spring.expression.maxOperations setting, aborting evaluation past the limit. At 4.1.1 neither the counter nor the configuration knob exists.

MimeTypeUtils.parseMimeType at spring-core/src/main/java/org/springframework/core/util/MimeTypeUtils.java:205-241 splits the header with StringUtils.tokenizeToStringArray(mimeType, ";") and then splits each parameter on the first "=" with plain indexOf/substring, with no awareness of quoted strings or quoted-pairs. A quoted parameter value that contains ";" or "=" is therefore parsed as additional parameters, so Spring's view of a multipart Content-Type differs from the view of the HTTP stack that delimited the body (CWE-444 multipart request smuggling). The 6.2.19 fix 8a93a889620c (gh-36730) makes the parser quoted-pair aware, only treating a double quote as a delimiter when the preceding character is not a backslash.

MappingJackson2MessageConverter.getJavaTypeForMessage at spring-jms/src/main/java/org/springframework/jms/support/converter/MappingJackson2MessageConverter.java:362-377 reads the type id from the JMS message string property named by typeIdPropertyName, and when the id is not in the configured idClassMappings it resolves the value with ClassUtils.forName(typeId, this.beanClassLoader) and hands the resulting class to the ObjectMapper for deserialization. In an untrusted JMS environment the producer of the message controls that property, so an attacker selects an arbitrary gadget class on the consumer classpath to be instantiated/deserialized (CWE-502). The 6.2.19 fix 9bec52b1ec74 adds setTrustedPackages()/isTrustedPackage() to MappingJackson2MessageConverter so only allowlisted packages may be resolved from the type id.

The advisory describes a bypass of the CVE-2015-5211 RFD protection through a ";jsessionid=" path parameter: the fixed 4.3.29/5.x code must strip the session id before the RFD content-disposition check runs. At 4.1.1 neither half exists: UrlPathHelper.removeSemicolonContent (spring-web/src/main/java/org/springframework/web/util/UrlPathHelper.java:454-478) drops all ";" content in the default removeSemicolonContent branch and always removes ";jsessionid=" through removeJsessionid in the disabled branch, and the RFD protection (addContentDispositionHeader in RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor) was only added by the CVE-2015-5211 fix, after this snapshot. The 2020 fix eb11c6fa2330 reinstates exactly the jsessionid removal that 4.1.1 already performs, so the bypass mechanism does not exist here; the underlying RFD issue is the separately tracked CVE-2015-5211 row.
notes: bypass requires the CVE-2015-5211 RFD check, absent at 4.1.1; UrlPathHelper already strips ";jsessionid="

basis: The advisory describes unbounded growth of a SpEL pattern cache. That cache is the parser-level ConcurrentMap/ConcurrentLruCache introduced by the CVE-2023-20861 fix in 5.2.23; at 4.1.1 OperatorMatches.getValueInternal calls Pattern.compile((String) right) inline (spring-expression/src/main/java/org/springframework/expression/spel/ast/OperatorMatches.java:67) and no pattern, expression or AST cache exists in the spring-expression module, so there is no cache whose growth can exhaust memory. The 6.2.19 fix e8f08b415849/ec89834fa8f6 bounds the cache (MAX_PATTERN_CACHE_SIZE = 256) that a later release introduced, which is a regression fix for 5.2.23+ code, not a pre-image present at 4.1.1.
notes: pattern cache was introduced in 5.2.23; 4.1.1 has no cache to grow

basis: Http11Processor.prepareRequestProtocol at java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:609-612 sets http09 = true and keepAlive = false for any request line whose protocol token is empty, without constraining the method. Under HTTP/0.9 simple-request parsing the request is dispatched with the HTTP/0.9 rules, so an attacker can send a non-GET method that security constraints evaluate differently from the equivalent HTTP/1.1 request. The 9.0.113 fix 2e2fa23f2635 adds, immediately after keepAlive = false, `if (!Method.GET.equals(request.getMethod())) { response.setStatus(400); setErrorState(ErrorState.CLOSE_CLEAN, null); }` because HTTP/0.9 only allows GET. At 9.0.98 that guard is absent.

OpenSSLEngine.processOCSPRequest in the FFM/panama engine at java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/openssl/panama/OpenSSLEngine.java:1352-1362 parses an OCSP response whose status is OCSP_RESPONSE_STATUS_SUCCESSFUL, extracts the single response for the certificate and returns OCSP_single_get0_status directly. It never adds or checks a nonce, never calls OCSP_basic_verify on the basic response signature and never applies OCSP_check_validity to thisUpdate/nextUpdate, so a forged or stale OCSP response is accepted as GOOD and certificate revocation is bypassed. The 9.0.x fix e76e9eaa246f (vendor lists 9.0.115 as the first fixed release) adds OCSP_request_add1_nonce/OCSP_check_nonce, OCSP_basic_verify, and two OCSP_check_validity windows (OCSP_MAX_SKEW = 15 minutes) before returning the status. At 9.0.98 none of those calls exists.

LockOutRealm.isLocked at java/org/apache/catalina/realm/LockOutRealm.java:207-210 looks the supplied user name up verbatim in failedUsers, and registerAuthFailure (:241-248) stores it the same way, so the failure counter is keyed on the exact spelling of the attempted name. An attacker can therefore keep guessing passwords for a locked account by alternating case variants ("Alice", "ALICE", "alice", ...): each spelling gets its own LockRecord, the failure count never reaches failureCount and the lock-out never triggers. The 9.0.118 fix 6dd75beb55bd adds a caseSensitive attribute (default false) and lowercases the key with Locale.ROOT in isLocked, registerAuthSuccess and registerAuthFailure. At 9.0.98 neither the lowercasing nor the attribute exists.

WebdavServlet.doPropfind at java/org/apache/catalina/servlets/WebdavServlet.java:835-839 feeds the request body straight into documentBuilder.parse(new InputSource(req.getInputStream())) whenever the client supplies a positive Content-Length or a chunked Transfer-Encoding, with no upper bound on the body size; doLock performs the same read at :1382-1386. The DOM parser buffers the whole body, so an unauthenticated client can stream an arbitrarily large LOCK or PROPFIND body and exhaust the server heap. The 9.0.118 fix 17dacd9aa486 adds maxRequestBodySize (default 4096), a Content-Length short-cut and a BoundedByteArrayOutputStream around both reads. At 9.0.98 the body is parsed with no bound.

Http11Processor.prepareRequest at java/org/apache/coyote/http11/Http11Processor.java:788-789 validates the Host header with parseHost(hostValueMB) but never compares the request host name with the SNI host name presented in the TLS handshake. When one connector serves several virtual hosts with client certificate verification, a client can complete the handshake (and the client-certificate check) against one SNI host and then send a request whose Host header names a different virtual host, reusing the certificate that was verified for the first host. The 9.0.113 fix 152c14885d45 adds AbstractEndpoint.checkSni/strictSni (default true) and calls protocol.checkSni(socketWrapper.getSniHostName(), request.serverName()) immediately after parseHost; a4aa74232e82 (NIO2) and 9276b5e783c8 (APR) add the per-endpoint support the check needs. At 9.0.98 there is no checkSni call. The case-insensitive variant that gets past this check is a separate advisory, CVE-2026-32990, fixed in 9.0.116 by 95f77782.

OpenSSLEngine.processOCSPRequest in the FFM/panama engine at java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/openssl/panama/OpenSSLEngine.java:1352-1380 handles only OCSP_RESPONSE_STATUS_SUCCESSFUL. For a TRY_LATER (or any other non-successful) response the method falls through the success branch and returns V_OCSP_CERTSTATUS_UNKNOWN() at :1380 without calling X509_STORE_CTX_set_error. The verify caller at :1188-1197 turns UNKNOWN into a failure only when X509_STORE_CTX_get_error() is <= 0, so if another OCSP URL attempt or verification step has already set an error on the same X509_STORE_CTX, the TRY_LATER result leaves ok = 1 and the client certificate is accepted although OCSP soft fail is not configured. The 9.0.116 fix d1406df5ae03 adds the missing else branch X509_STORE_CTX_set_error(x509ctx, X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_GET_CRL()), matching Tomcat Native. At 9.0.98 the non-successful path sets no error.

OpenSSLEngine.processOCSPRequest in the FFM/panama engine at java/org/apache/tomcat/util/net/openssl/panama/OpenSSLEngine.java:1306-1341 returns V_OCSP_CERTSTATUS_UNKNOWN() from every OCSP request failure path: OCSP_REQUEST_new, OCSP_cert_to_id, OCSP_request_add0_id, i2d_OCSP_REQUEST, a non-200 HTTP response, and the catch block. None of those returns calls X509_STORE_CTX_set_error, and the finally block at :1368-1371 only sets X509_V_ERR_APPLICATION_VERIFICATION when ocspResponse is NULL. The verify caller at :1188-1197 keeps ok = 1 when the context error is positive, so a failed OCSP exchange can be treated as a soft failure and the client certificate is accepted. The 9.0.117 fix ff589ab26e82 adds X509_STORE_CTX_set_error(x509ctx, X509_V_ERR_UNABLE_TO_GET_CRL()) to each of those returns so FFM hard-fails when OCSP cannot be completed. At 9.0.98 the failure returns carry no error.

JNDIRealm.bindAsUser at java/org/apache/catalina/realm/JNDIRealm.java:1839-1848 adds the supplied credentials to the DirContext with userCredentialsAdd(context, dn, credentials) and then triggers the bind with context.getAttributes("", null). When the realm environment sets Context.SECURITY_AUTHENTICATION to GSSAPI, the provider binds with the connection's already established GSSAPI identity instead of the supplied password, so HttpServletRequest.login(username, password) succeeds for any password. The 9.0.102 fix c32bbd37ea9e preserves the context environment, removes SECURITY_AUTHENTICATION while the user credentials are checked and restores it in the finally block. At 9.0.98 the GSSAPI mechanism is still in the environment during bindAsUser.

ChatAnnotation.sendMessage at webapps/examples/WEB-INF/classes/websocket/chat/ChatAnnotation.java:96-101 appends every message to the per-connection ArrayDeque messageBacklog whenever a send is already in progress, with no limit on the queue size. A slow or stalled WebSocket client stops draining its backlog, and the example keeps buffering every broadcast for that client until the server heap is exhausted. The 9.0.121 fix f6dda658e4ed adds BACKLOG_LIMIT = 10, a skippedMessageCount and the logic that clears the backlog and skips further messages once the limit is reached. At 9.0.98 messageBacklog.add(msg) is unconditional.

The advisory describes "+" being converted to a space while the rewrite valve handles a rewritten path: the 9.0.120 fix a520aecb325e replaces URLDecoder.decode(urlStringRewriteEncoded, uriCharset.name()) with UDecoder.URLDecode, because java.net.URLDecoder maps "+" to " ". At 9.0.98 the valve never decodes the rewritten path: RewriteValve.invoke takes the already-decoded request path in urlDecoded, appends URLEncoder.DEFAULT.encode(urlStringDecoded, uriCharset) to the requestURI chunk (java/org/apache/catalina/valves/rewrite/RewriteValve.java:492), normalizes the decoded string at :495 and appends that same decoded string to the decodedURI chunk at :502. There is no URLDecoder call anywhere in the 9.0.98 file (the only UDecoder use is the sendRedirect branch at :409). The decode-after-normalize flow that the advisory targets was introduced by the 9.0.103 rewrite refactor ee3ab548e923, so the "+" conversion and the security-control bypass it enables cannot occur at 9.0.98.
notes: the affected URLDecoder.decode call exists only since the 9.0.103 rewrite refactor; 9.0.98 works in decoded space and never decodes the rewritten path.

basis: The 9.0.120 fix 617d7275782b changes documentation only: webapps/docs/config/cluster-interceptor.xml and webapps/docs/changelog.xml now state that EncryptInterceptor replay protection is effective only for non-malleable algorithms and recommend AES/GCM/NoPadding. No product code changes, so the snapshot has no code location to anchor for this advisory. The underlying weakness is the EncryptInterceptor padding-oracle/default-algorithm issue tracked as CVE-2026-29146, which is already a Ground Truth row for this snapshot.
notes: docs-only fix; the code weakness is CVE-2026-29146 (already GT).

basis: Out-of-bounds read/write in RFC 3211 KEK unwrap in CMS password based decryption. The vendor advisory 20250930.txt states that OpenSSL 3.5 is vulnerable and "OpenSSL 3.5 users should upgrade to OpenSSL 3.5.4", so the fix ships in 3.5.4 and every later 3.5 release. The frozen snapshot is openssl-3.5.8 (f4dc4d58b48d), which is past 3.5.4. The OSV record corroborates this: its version list covers 3.5.0 through 3.5.3 only, and its GIT ranges are the per-branch fix commits (5965ea5dd6 for 3.5). NVD carries no CPE configuration for this CVE, which is why the version resolver left it unknown.
notes: vendor fixed release 3.5.4; snapshot 3.5.8 is later.

basis: Minerva timing attack, described as "OpenSSL 3.0.0 through 3.3.2 on the PowerPC architecture", exploitable by timing EVP_DigestSign and recovering the ECDSA nonce. The range ends at 3.3.2, so the frozen openssl-3.5.8 snapshot is outside it; 3.4 and 3.5 were released after the fix and the OpenSSL vulnerabilities index has no advisory for this CVE. The OSV record only carries the GIT fix commits (89cd17a0, fb7fab9f) and no version list, which is why the resolver left it unknown.
notes: CVE range 3.0.0-3.3.2 (PowerPC); snapshot 3.5.8 is outside.

basis: PHP openssl_private_decrypt with OPENSSL_PKCS1_PADDING is exposed to the Marvin attack. The advisory states the exposure exists "unless it is used with an OpenSSL version that includes the changes from this pull request: openssl/openssl#13817 (rsa_pkcs1_implicit_rejection). These changes are part of OpenSSL 3.2". The frozen openssl-3.5.8 provider includes them: RSA_PKEY_CTX has implicit_rejection (crypto/rsa/rsa_pmeth.c:55) initialised to 1 at :77, pkey_rsa_decrypt only falls back to RSA_PKCS1_NO_IMPLICIT_REJECT_PADDING when the option is switched off (:384), and ossl_rsa_padding_check_PKCS1_type_2 (crypto/rsa/rsa_pk1.c:376-388) deliberately returns a deterministic random message instead of an error. NVD routes this CVE to the PHP product only, which is why the resolver could not decide it for openssl/openssl; the OpenSSL-side mitigation the advisory requires is present at the tag.
notes: implicit rejection (openssl#13817, part of 3.2) is enabled by default at 3.5.8; the CVE itself is assigned to PHP.

basis: SLOTH: acceptance of MD5 signatures in TLS 1.2 Server Key Exchange. The advisory assigns the defect to Mozilla Network Security Services ("NSS before 3.20.2, as used in Mozilla Firefox before 43.0.2 and Firefox ESR 38.x before 38.5.2") and NVD's only CPE is cpe:2.3:a:mozilla:network_security_services. No OpenSSL component is named. As a secondary check, the frozen tree's only MD5 signature entry is legacy_rsa_sigalg (ssl/t1_lib.c:2134, "rsa_pkcs1_md5_sha1", the legacy TLS<1.2 RSA fallback), and md5_sha1 is assigned security bits 67 (:2608-2609), below the 80 bits required by the default security level, so tls12_sigalg_allowed (:3305, secbits check at :3370-3374) rejects it.
notes: advisory and CPE name Mozilla NSS only; no openssl/openssl component.

basis: D(HE)at: the Diffie-Hellman key agreement protocol as specified permits long exponents, which makes server-side exponentiation more expensive than necessary; the CVE is assigned to diffie-hellman_key_exchange_project and its only CPE is cpe:2.3:a:diffie-hellman_key_exchange_project:diffie-hellman_key_exchange. It describes a protocol-level property, not a defect in a specific OpenSSL source component, and the advisory does not name openssl/openssl. The candidate reached the openssl queue through the keyword sweep.
notes: protocol-level DH exponent issue; CPE names only the DH project.

basis: Missing authorization in the Octolize "Cart Weight for WooCommerce" WordPress plugin (affected "from n/a through <= 1.9.11", patchstack WOOWOO record). The advisory concerns a WordPress plugin and names no OpenSSL component; the candidate reached the openssl queue through the keyword sweep. OSV has no record for this CVE, which is why the resolver left it unknown.
notes: WordPress plugin advisory; no openssl/openssl component.

basis: Emlog (PHP blog/CMS) v2.6.1 and earlier exposes /index.php?rest-api=upload without validating file type, extension or content, giving an authenticated API-key holder arbitrary file upload (GHSA-p837-mrw9-5x5j). The advisory and its CPE concern the emlog product only; no OpenSSL component is named, and the candidate reached the openssl queue through the keyword sweep.
notes: emlog CMS advisory; no openssl/openssl component.

basis: The exceptions renderer builds its request-body panel from Exception::requestBody() (src/Illuminate/Foundation/Exceptions/Renderer/Exception.php:155-164), which takes Request::all() — query string and parsed body parameters supplied by the client — JSON-encodes it with JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES and then removes every backslash with str_replace('\\', '', $json), so quote escapes produced by json_encode disappear. The template echoes that string with an unescaped Blade echo at src/Illuminate/Foundation/resources/exceptions/renderer/components/context.blade.php:54 ({!! $exception->requestBody() ?: 'No body data' !!}). When APP_DEBUG=true (Handler::renderExceptionContent at src/Illuminate/Foundation/Exceptions/Handler.php:841 selects this renderer), a request parameter such as x"><script>alert(document.domain)</script> is reflected into the debug error page and executes with the application origin (CWE-79). The 11.36.0 fix 45287fb2a91c changes the echo to {{ }} so the JSON is HTML-escaped.

Exception::applicationRouteParametersContext() (src/Illuminate/Foundation/Exceptions/Renderer/Exception.php:189-197) JSON-encodes the route parameters of the failed request — including URL segments bound to route placeholders such as /user/{name}, which the client controls — and the exceptions renderer echoes the returned JSON with an unescaped Blade echo at src/Illuminate/Foundation/resources/exceptions/renderer/components/context.blade.php:108 ({!! $routeParametersContext !!}). The same 11.36.0 fix 45287fb2a91c changes both this echo and the request-body echo to {{ }}. With APP_DEBUG=true (src/Illuminate/Foundation/Exceptions/Handler.php:841) a route parameter carrying HTML markup is rendered as HTML in the debug error page and executes with the application origin (CWE-79).

XSS in the debug page information through a Tippy.js tooltip configured with allowHTML: true. The OSV range says introduced 0, fixed 12.69.0, which nominally contains v11.30.0; the source does not. The fix b495ca2ec4e1 (PR #61381) does two things: it renames the tooltip attribute in formatted-source.blade.php from data-tippy-content to data-tippy-html-content, and it splits the single tippy() call that had allowHTML: true into two, with allowHTML: false for data-tippy-content. Neither part exists in the frozen v11.30.0 tree: there is no formatted-source.blade.php component, no allowHTML option in the renderer source, and the shipped bundle src/Illuminate/Foundation/resources/exceptions/renderer/dist/scripts.js contains only allowHTML:!1 (false). The only tippy targets at v11.30.0 are context.blade.php:20 and :74, whose data-tippy-content values are Blade-escaped {{ }} header and route names. With allowHTML disabled tippy renders content as text, so no markup from the page can execute. The vulnerable tooltip is a later renderer feature; v11.30.0 is not affected.
notes: range introduced 0 is nominal; the allowHTML:true tooltip and formatted-source component do not exist at v11.30.0.

basis: Unauthorized data destruction through relationship inclusion on a read endpoint. The OSV record carries two ranges: introduced 12.45.0, fixed 12.68.0, and introduced 13.0.0, fixed 13.27.0; the resolver only considered the 13.x branch and left the 11.x snapshot possible. The fix commits 50a7970efe9f and b89f2944995d both modify src/Illuminate/Http/Resources/JsonApi/Concerns/ResolvesJsonApiElements.php, the JSON:API resource feature that shipped in 12.45.0. The frozen v11.30.0 tree has no src/Illuminate/Http/Resources/JsonApi directory at all, so the defective inclusion/destruction path does not exist there. v11.30.0 predates the introduced version and is not affected.
notes: 12.x range starts at 12.45.0; the JsonApi resource directory does not exist at v11.30.0.

basis: GHSA-4r2f-6fm9-2qgh is a GitHub-withdrawn duplicate advisory: its own text says it duplicates GHSA-2xxx-fhc8-9qvq and is kept only to preserve external references. The canonical advisory is already a Ground Truth row on this same v2.2.0 snapshot (vulnerability GHSA-2xxx-fhc8-9qvq, alias CVE-2017-20166, anchor lib/ecto/repo/queryable.ex:351-352, fix db55b0cba652, range = 2.2.0 fixed in 2.2.1). The withdrawn advisory adds no distinct root cause, so the candidate resolves as a duplicate.
notes: Withdrawn duplicate of GHSA-2xxx-fhc8-9qvq / CVE-2017-20166, already GT at queryable.ex:351-352.

basis: Channel-name SQL injection in Postgrex.Notifications.listen/3. The GitHub advisory filed in the elixir-ecto/ecto repository names package `postgrex` (range > 0.16.0, fixed 0.22.2) and the NVD record's only CPE is cpe:2.3:a:elixir-ecto:postgrex. The frozen ecto v2.2.0 tree contains no Postgrex.Notifications module (no "Notifications" match under lib/ or test/) and its optional postgrex requirement is "~> 0.13.0" (mix.exs:47), below the first affected postgrex release. No ecto source component is affected; the candidate entered the ecto queue because the advisory was published under the ecto repository.
notes: advisory package is postgrex; no Postgrex.Notifications in the ecto tree; optional dep is postgrex ~> 0.13.0.

basis: SQL injection through an unescaped dollar-quote ($$) in the reconnect DO block. The advisory filed in elixir-ecto/ecto names package `postgrex` (range >= 0.16.0, fixed 0.22.3); NVD describes it as "SQL Injection vulnerability in elixir-ecto postgrex". The frozen ecto v2.2.0 tree has no reconnect/notification code and its optional postgrex requirement is "~> 0.13.0" (mix.exs:47). No ecto source component is affected.
notes: advisory package is postgrex; no reconnect DO block in ecto.

basis: SQL injection through the :comment option of Postgrex.stream/4. The advisory filed in elixir-ecto/ecto names package `postgrex` (range >= 0.19.3 and < 0.22.4) and NVD's only CPE is cpe:2.3:a:elixir-ecto:postgrex. The frozen ecto v2.2.0 adapter only forwards to Postgrex.stream/4 (lib/ecto/adapters/postgres/connection.ex:112-113) and never constructs a :comment option — the only comment handling in the adapter is DDL COMMENT ON with single_quote escaping (:687-692). Its optional postgrex requirement is "~> 0.13.0" (mix.exs:47), below the affected >= 0.19.3 range. The defect is in postgrex, not ecto.
notes: advisory package is postgrex; ecto only forwards to Postgrex.stream and never sets :comment.

basis: Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers at lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex:189-219 receives the operator configured cumulative :length budget but only the body readers deduct from it: the already-parsed part headers are never charged (there is no headers_size/2), and the :skip branch at :217-218 returns {conn, limit, acc} without reading or charging the skipped part body at all. A request of many file parts with empty or skipped bodies therefore costs essentially zero against :length while each part still opens a temporary file and retains a Plug.Upload entry, so an unauthenticated attacker holds one request under the 8 MB default while forcing unbounded temp files/inodes and memory growth (CWE-770). The 1.19.x fix 0ee8afcc/56edca2c ("Count files and skipped multiparts towards length", advisory names 981597d3 for the 1.20 line) adds `limit = limit - headers_size(headers)` at the head of parse_multipart_headers and a parse_multipart_skip reader for the :skip branch.

GHSA-wpmj-jh88-rpgm (cookie attribute injection through unvalidated ";" in Plug.Conn.Cookies.encode/2) is already a Ground Truth row on this same v1.19.2 snapshot at lib/plug/conn/cookies.ex:72-80 (fix 149d9ed68fee). This needs_version_check candidate is the same advisory reached through the GHSA rather than the EEF record, so it adds no distinct root cause.
notes: Same advisory and root cause as the GT row at lib/plug/conn/cookies.ex:72-80.

basis: GHSA-95qv-c9g9-rm63 is the GitHub copy of the multipart :length advisory whose EEF candidate (disc2_56ec30554f5d9652b9e1a4a1) is promoted in this same pass at lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex:189-219 with fix commits 0ee8afcc/56edca2c. This needs_version_check candidate names the same advisory and adds no distinct root cause.
notes: Same advisory as the row promoted here from the EEF candidate.

basis: Plug header injection through an unvalidated cookie value: the advisory and NVD configuration restrict the vulnerable ranges to plug > 1.0.6 to <= 1.1.9 and the 1.2/1.3 lines fixed in 1.2.5 and 1.3.5, so v1.19.2 is outside every range. Static corroboration: the 2017 fix 8857f8ab adds validate_header_value!(cookie) to verify_cookie!, and the frozen v1.19.2 code at lib/plug/conn.ex:1946-1948 already validates every Set-Cookie value with validate_header_key_value!("set-cookie", cookie).
notes: all vulnerable ranges end at 1.1.9/1.2.5/1.3.5; frozen 1.19.2 validates Set-Cookie values at conn.ex:1946-1948.

basis: django.utils.translation.check_for_language at django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:462-479 is decorated with @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1000) and its only pre-filter is language_code_re.search (pattern at :52: "^[a-z]{1,8}(?:-[a-z0-9]{1,8})*(?:@[a-z0-9]{1,20})?$"), which accepts a well-formed chain of arbitrarily many "-segment" groups. django.views.i18n.set_language (views/i18n.py:47-48) passes the raw request.POST[LANGUAGE_QUERY_PARAMETER] value straight in, so when that view is routed an unauthenticated client can submit many distinct codes of up to DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE bytes (2.5 MB default); each is retained as an lru_cache key and the process holds up to 1000 of them, growing memory far beyond the size of any single request (CWE-789). No LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH guard exists anywhere in the 4.2.13 tree (grep is empty). The fix c72a5dbb (5.2.x) / 27137e65 (main) removes the decorator from check_for_language, rejects lang_code longer than LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH (500) before lookup, and moves the cache to translation_catalog_exists so oversized codes are never retained as keys. NVD CPE is versionEndExcluding 5.2.17 with no versionStartIncluding, so 4.2.13 is inside the published range; the advisory text notes that unsupported series such as 4.2.x were not evaluated.

CVE-2024-41990 (urlize/urlizetrunc DoS) is a regression of the 4.2.14 fix for CVE-2024-38875: the 4.2.15 patch d0a82e26 edits the CountsDict-based trim_punctuation introduced in 4.2.14, and its new regression inputs ("&.;"*100000, ".;"*100000) exercise the `amp = middle.rfind("&")` branch added by that rewrite. The frozen 4.2.13 trim_punctuation (django/utils/html.py:333-367) is the earlier implementation: it calls html.unescape(middle) and rstrips once per while-pass over the whole word and contains no amp/rfind, no CountsDict and no trailing_punctuation_chars_no_semicolon, so the code the 4.2.15 fix modifies does not exist at this tag. 4.2.13 has its own urlize DoS (very large bracket inputs, CVE-2024-38875, fixed in 4.2.14), which is a distinct advisory. The OSV/NVD range "4.2 before 4.2.15" is coarse and does not mean the patched construct is present at this snapshot.
notes: Fix context (CountsDict, counts[closing], amp/rfind, trailing_punctuation_chars_no_semicolon) is absent at 4.2.13; the 41990 defect was introduced by the 4.2.14 rewrite.

basis: CVE-2024-45230 (urlize/urlizetrunc DoS via trailing semicolons) targets the amp/semicolon branch that the 4.2.14 urlize rewrite introduced: the 4.2.16 fix d147a8eb rewrites that branch using trail_start and trailing_punctuation_chars, and its regression input "&" + ";:"*100000 exercises it. At the frozen 4.2.13 tag trim_punctuation (django/utils/html.py:333-367) is the earlier implementation with no amp variable, no semicolon/entity special-case and no CountsDict; the whole post-4.2.14 code path the fix edits is absent. The published "4.2 before 4.2.16" range is coarse version-range boilerplate; code-level review shows this CVE cannot be anchored in the 4.2.13 source.
notes: Fix pre-image (amp/rfind + semicolon branch) does not exist at 4.2.13; the defect arrived with the 4.2.14 urlize rewrite.

basis: CVE-2026-53878 is a missing-newline check in DomainNameValidator: the fix d5d60ed0 changes the class regex tail from r"$" to r"\Z". The frozen 4.2.13 tree has no DomainNameValidator at all: a grep over the whole tag checkout finds zero occurrences, and django/core/validators.py only defines RegexValidator, URLValidator, EmailValidator and the validate_* helpers (no hostname_re/tld_re class). The component the advisory names therefore cannot accept a newline here. NVD also restricts the CVE to 5.2 < 5.2.16 and 6.0 < 6.0.7. The OSV record's blanket {introduced: 0} range is not code evidence, and the advisory text itself says earlier unsupported series were not evaluated.
notes: no DomainNameValidator symbol in the 4.2.13 tree; NVD range starts at 5.2.

basis: Process::escapeArgument at src/Symfony/Component/Process/Process.php:1630-1647 has a Windows-only branch that returns the argument unquoted when it does not match /[\/()%!^"<>&|\s]/ (:1641). The class omits "=", ";", "*", "?", "'", "$", "[" and "]", which MSYS2 treats as special when PHP itself runs under an MSYS2 environment (Git Bash) and spawns a native Windows executable: the MSYS2 argument/path conversion mangles the unquoted value, so the child receives a corrupted or truncated argument instead of the one Symfony intended (CWE-88). Applications (or Composer scripts) that pass an attacker-influenced path containing "=" to file-management commands such as rmdir/del can therefore act on a broader directory. The fix ec154f6/3520393 replaces the class with /[()%!^"<>&|\s[\]=;*?\'$]/, forcing the quoting branch for these characters; it is released on 5.4 in 5.4.51.

ParameterizedHeader::setParameters at src/Symfony/Component/Mime/Header/ParameterizedHeader.php:57-60 stores the caller-supplied parameter array without validating the names, and createParameter (:107) interpolates $name into the serialized header (`$name."=".$value`) after checking only the value against TOKEN_REGEX (:117). RFC 2045/5322 require parameter names to be tokens; a caller that derives a name from untrusted input can therefore put CR/LF or other non-token bytes into Content-Type/Content-Disposition and inject additional headers into the rendered mail (CWE-93). The fix 8cc149f/1503ceb adds a per-name preg_match(TOKEN_REGEX) in setParameters that throws RfcComplianceException. Note on versions: the GHSA record states fixed 5.4.52, but v5.4.52's ParameterizedHeader.php is byte-identical to v5.4.45 and the name check first appears in the 5.4.55 backport 1503ceb (2026-10-28, matching FriendsOfPHP symfony/mime CVE-2026-45070.yaml, affected <5.4.55); v5.4.45 is inside either range.

GHSA-7q22-x757-cmgc is a withdrawn advisory ("Withdrawn Advisory: Symfony http-security has authentication bypass") and NVD records that the supplier concluded this is a false report, describing Symfony v7.0.7 and carrying no CPE configuration at all. Static check at v5.4.45: FormLoginAuthenticator::authenticate (src/Symfony/Component/Security/Http/Authenticator/FormLoginAuthenticator.php:82-110) builds a Passport from getCredentials (:135-172); an empty username is passed to UserProvider::loadUserByIdentifier(), which throws UsernameNotFoundException, and an empty password reaches PasswordCredentials/BadCredentialsException. There is no early return, anonymous token or missing-credential path that would authenticate the request.
notes: advisory withdrawn and supplier-declared false report; NVD has no CPE; frozen 5.4.45 authenticator has no empty-credential bypass.

basis: The CVE is about the Auth0-PHP SDK: applications using Auth0-PHP 8.0.0-8.17.0 (and bundles built on it, including Auth0/symfony 5.0.0 to 5.5.x) accept ID tokens as access tokens because audience validation is improper. NVD's only CPEs are cpe:2.3:a:auth0:auth0-php, auth0:laravel-auth0, auth0:symfony (5.0.0 to <5.6.0) and auth0:wp-auth0. The frozen repository is the symfony/symfony monorepo (composer.json name "symfony/symfony"), which contains no auth0 dependency or code (grep -i auth0 over composer.json and src/ is empty). The "symfony" package in the advisory is Auth0's Symfony integration bundle, not the framework.
notes: CVE names Auth0-PHP / Auth0/symfony bundle; frozen monorepo has no auth0 code or dependency.

basis: FormDataReader.ProcessFormKeys at src/Components/Endpoints/src/FormMapping/FormDataReader.cs:124-165 splits each form key into bracket segments. It computes `endIndex = key.Value.Span[startIndex..].IndexOf(']') + startIndex` (:140) and then tests `endIndex == -1` (:141), but adding startIndex first turns the -1 sentinel into startIndex-1, so the guard can only fire when the "[" is at index 0. For an ordinary key such as "customer[0" (no closing bracket anywhere after the "[" at index 8) endIndex becomes 7, the code slices an empty key segment, then resumes at `endIndex + 1 + nextOpenBracket` where the "[" search starts at endIndex+1 == startIndex and finds the same "[" again (:158-160): startIndex never advances and the while loop runs forever, pinning the request thread with no further allocation (CWE-835). The reader is driven by form binding for Razor Components and by minimal-API [FromForm] binding (the same fix also touches RequestDelegateFactory.cs and HttpContextFormValueMapper.cs), so any endpoint that accepts form data is reachable by an unauthenticated POST whose field name contains an unmatched "[" (e.g. `customer[0`). The 8.0.27 fix ab7d766648 (public backport #66674, merge b48ed8d3) deletes ProcessFormKeys and rewrites GetKeys() to check `key.Span[prefix.Length] != '['` and to skip a key with no closing "]" via `continue`, so no loop remains.

The advisory describes a stack overflow in the SignalR/Blazor MessagePack hub protocol caused by deeply nested arrays. The v8.0.28 fix dc6799d732 ("Merged PR 61221: Update MessagePack", 2026-05-19) does not change any deserializer logic in this repository: it bumps eng/Versions.props MessagePackVersion from 2.5.187 to 2.5.301, applies src/submodules/msgpack-fix-full.diff and upstream-patch.diff to the MessagePack-CSharp submodule, and adds only a regression test in src/SignalR/common/SignalR.Common/test/Internal/Protocol/MessagePackHubProtocolTestBase.cs. The deserializer that recurses on nested arrays lives in the separate project aspnet/MessagePack-CSharp (a .gitmodules entry at the frozen SHA; the submodule has no content in the frozen tree), so the root cause is outside this repository and cannot be anchored here.
notes: fix is a MessagePack dependency/submodule update (2.5.187 -> 2.5.301), no in-tree deserializer change; root cause in aspnet/MessagePack-CSharp.

basis: NVD describes CVE-2026-92707 as a MessagePack for C# defect: PrimitiveObjectFormatter allocates an object[] from each declared array length before the object-graph depth limit rejects the input, fixed in MessagePack 2.5.303 and 3.1.9; an ASP.NET Core SignalR hub with an object parameter is only named as one exposure path. The v8.0.32 fix in this repository is 21f2be26fd ("Update MessagePack to 2.5.303 (#69370)", 2026-09-21), i.e. a dependency version bump, and eng/Versions.props at v8.0.32 reads <MessagePackVersion>2.5.303</MessagePackVersion>. No file in this repository contains the formatter or its depth handling; the defect belongs to MessagePack-CSharp, so this repository cannot carry a source anchor for it.
notes: CVE/NVD texts describe MessagePack-CSharp PrimitiveObjectFormatter; aspnetcore fix is only the MessagePack 2.5.303 bump.

basis: In the pure-Python backend, MessageDecoder at python/google/protobuf/internal/decoder.py:661-708 generates the message-field decoders DecodeRepeatedField (:671) and DecodeField (:693); both call `value._InternalParse(buffer, pos, new_pos)` (:682 and :703) with no depth argument, and InternalParse (python_message.py:1139) itself calls every field decoder as `field_decoder(buffer, new_pos, end, self, field_dict)` with no depth. Nothing in the parser counts nesting levels, so a message containing recursively nested sub-messages recurses once per level until CPython raises RecursionError; the equivalent group paths (_DecodeUnknownFieldSet/_DecodeUnknownField at decoder.py:945/962, reached through InternalParse :1182) and chains of SGROUP tags recurse the same way (CWE-674). Any application that parses untrusted protobuf data with PROTOCOL_BUFFERS_PYTHON_IMPLEMENTATION=python (or the pure-Python wheel/Bazel default) can be crashed remotely. The main fix 17838b adds a DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT=100 plus SetRecursionLimit and increments/checks current_depth around every recursive parse; the 25.x backport d31100c9 threads the same current_depth parameter through InternalParse and the decoder closures and ships as protobuf-python 4.25.8.

json_format._ConvertAnyMessage at python/google/protobuf/json_format.py:626-656 parses an Any. ConvertMessage (:463) is the only place that increments self.recursion_depth and raises when it exceeds self.max_recursion_depth (:474-477), but when the Any payload type is a well-known type the code calls the WKT method directly through `methodcaller(_WKTJSONMETHODS[full_name][1], value['value'], sub_message, path)(self)` (:646-649) instead of self.ConvertMessage, so that nesting level is never counted. An attacker-supplied JSON document with deeply nested Any messages can therefore pass the intended depth guard and exhaust the Python stack (CWE-674). ParseDict is the exposed entry point (google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict, max_recursion_depth=100 by default), so any service that converts untrusted JSON into protobuf messages can be crashed remotely. The fix replaces the methodcaller branch with `self.ConvertMessage(value['value'], sub_message, '{0}.value'.format(path))` (d2b00162 on main, 5ebddcb1 on 5.x) and documents the exclusive depth semantics.

This candidate is the discovery-pipeline copy of the same CVE-2025-4565 / GHSA-8qvm-5x2c-j2w7 pure-Python recursion DoS that is promoted in this same pass from adv3_ad4a88b1721f87cc at python/google/protobuf/internal/decoder.py:661-708; its source URLs are the same advisory, the same fix commit 17838b and the same PyPI package, and it adds no distinct root cause. It also lists the Java sibling GHSA-735f-pc8j-v9w8, but that is CVE-2024-7254, which is already a Ground Truth row on this snapshot.
notes: same advisory/CVE as the row promoted here from adv3_ad4a88b1721f87cc; the Java GHSA-735f alias is already GT.

basis: The advisory (CWE-626, vector CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N) lists io.netty:netty-codec-socks "<= 4.1.136.Final" as vulnerable and 4.1.137.Final as patched; the frozen snapshot is the 4.1.137.Final release commit. Static check at the frozen SHA: Socks4ClientEncoder writes userId and dstAddr through sanitize("userId"/"dstAddr") (:50-57) and sanitize (:61-70) walks every char and throws EncoderException when AsciiString.c2b(c) == 0, so an embedded NUL can no longer create a second SOCKS4 string terminator; Socks5ClientEncoder now writes the auth-method count, username length, password length and a DOMAIN destination length through writeFieldLength/checkFieldLength (:114/:120-129), which rejects lengths > 255 or < 0 instead of letting ByteBuf.writeByte truncate them to one byte and desynchronise the frame. Both hunks are part of 9e05192391 ("Merge changes from forks (#17213) (#17217)"), which the v4.1.136...v4.1.137 compare places in this release; tag netty-4.1.136.Final has neither (Socks4ClientEncoder there calls ByteBufUtil.writeAscii directly on msg.userId()/msg.dstAddr()). Note on scope: the advisory also claims SOCKS5 domain and username/password "null byte and CRLF injection", but those fields are length-prefixed per RFC 1928 (ATYP=0x03: LEN + domain) and RFC 1929 (ULEN + UNAME, PLEN + PASSWD), so NUL and CRLF are ordinary data there and the 4.1.137 patch deliberately leaves them uninspected; netty-4.1.139.Final and netty-4.2.17.Final still contain no such check, which confirms that only the SOCKS4 terminator and the SOCKS5 length bounds were treated as the defect.
notes: frozen tag is the advisory-patched 4.1.137.Final; SOCKS4 NUL sanitizer and SOCKS5 field-length guards from 9e05192391 are present; version 4.1.136 lacks both. SOCKS5 NUL/CRLF claims concern length-prefixed RFC fields and are not patched in any later release either.

basis: The advisory (CWE-297, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) describes the OpenSSL client path where hostname verification depends on JDK-internal trust-manager wrapping: OpenSslX509TrustManagerWrapper only builds its Unsafe-based wrapper when PlatformDependent.getUnsafeUnavailabilityCause() is null, and otherwise installs the pass-through DEFAULT (OpenSslX509TrustManagerWrapper.java:50-55, :57-145) — so on Java 25+, where Unsafe is unavailable, a plain X509TrustManager stays unwrapped. It lists io.netty:netty-handler "<= 4.1.136.Final" vulnerable and 4.1.137.Final patched. At the frozen 4.1.137.Final release commit the OpenSSL client context fails closed: after chooseTrustManager (:172-173), if endpointIdentificationAlgorithm is set and non-empty and !useExtendedTrustManager(manager), it throws UnsupportedOperationException("Endpoint identification algorithm '...' is configured but the trust manager does not support extended trust manager verification. Please provide an X509ExtendedTrustManager or use the SslProvider.JDK.") (ReferenceCountedOpenSslClientContext.java:181-187). useExtendedTrustManager is PlatformDependent.javaVersion() >= 7 && manager instanceof X509ExtendedTrustManager (ReferenceCountedOpenSslContext.java:791-793), so the unwrapped-manager case that the advisory describes now aborts context construction instead of continuing without hostname verification. The guard is part of 9e05192391 and is absent from netty-4.1.136.Final, matching the advisory. Scope note (static fact, not a new finding): the guard is evaluated at client-context creation; a later engine setSSLParameters call reaches configureEndpointVerification (ReferenceCountedOpenSslEngine.java:2250-2266), which only sets SSL_CVERIFY_REQUIRED and does not re-check the trust-manager type.
notes: frozen tag is the advisory-patched 4.1.137.Final; the fail-closed endpoint-identification guard (9e05192391) is present at ReferenceCountedOpenSslClientContext:181-187 and absent in 4.1.136.

basis: PHPMailer::setLanguage at src/PHPMailer.php:2078-2143 assembles `$lang_file = $lang_path . 'phpmailer.lang-' . $langcode . '.php';` (:2128) from the caller-supplied $lang_path and then executes it with `$foundlang = include $lang_file;` (:2137). The sole guard is `if (!static::isPermittedPath($lang_file) || !file_exists($lang_file))` (:2132), where isPermittedPath (:1745-1748) is just `return !preg_match('#^[a-z]+://#i', $path);`. A Windows UNC path such as `\\attacker\share\` contains no URI scheme and passes the check, so file_exists() issues an SMB request to the attacker host and the remote `phpmailer.lang-xx.php` is then included as PHP: RCE on Windows whenever the application passes untrusted data as $lang_path (the advisory precondition), plus NTLM credential disclosure to that share during file_exists(). $langcode itself is constrained by `/^[a-z]{2}(?:_[a-zA-Z]{2})?$/` (:2124), so only the directory component is attacker-defined. The 6.5.0 fix acd264bf ("Merge branch 'CVE-2021-34551'", 2021-06-16) adds the docblock warning "Do not set this from user input!" and replaces the include with `$lines = file($lang_file);` plus a per-line `preg_match('/^\$PHPMAILER_LANG\[\'([a-z\d_]+)\'\]\s*=\s*(["\'])(.+)*?\2;/')` that copies only string assignments for keys already present in the built-in table, so language files are parsed as text and never executed. The frozen 6.1.5 tree still carries the include and the URL-scheme-only check.

The candidate carries the aliases BIT-phpmailer-2021-34551, CVE-2021-34551 and GHSA-7q44-r25x-wm4q and comes from the FriendsOfPHP security-advisories yaml feed. That identifies the same defect promoted from adv3_47770e25681da792: the setLanguage() $lang_path include in src/PHPMailer.php, the same "< 6.5.0" composed range with 6.5.0 patched, and the same Windows UNC execution path (the FriendsOfPHP yaml was the source of the GHSA record). One vulnerability account, one source anchor; this row is an alias cluster of CVE-2021-34551.
notes: FriendsOfPHP yaml alias of CVE-2021-34551; no separate root cause, so duplicate rather than a second promotion.

basis: XMLUtil::GetCharacterRef at tinyxml2.cpp:475-568 parses numeric character references with no upper bound on the number of digits: `unsigned long ucs` and `unsigned mult` (:481, :484) accumulate `ucs += mult * digit; mult *= 16;` (:521-525) in the hex branch and `ucs += digitScaled; mult *= 10;` (:551-559) in the decimal branch. The only guards are the debug assertions `TIXMLASSERT( mult <= UINT_MAX / digit )` (:520), `TIXMLASSERT( ucs <= ULONG_MAX - digitScaled )` (:522) and `TIXMLASSERT( mult <= UINT_MAX / 16 )` (:524), mirrored at (:550, :552, :558) for decimal. TIXMLASSERT expands to `assert` only when TINYXML2_DEBUG is defined (tinyxml2.h:79-93; meson.build:40-42 adds -DTINYXML2_DEBUG for debug builds, CMakeLists.txt:31 for the Debug configuration) and to a no-op otherwise, so in an assertion-enabled build the check aborts the process through __assert_fail as soon as `mult` passes UINT_MAX/16 = 268435455: the hex branch reaches 16^7 = 268435456 after eight digits (e.g. `&#xffffffff;`) and decimal reaches 10^9 after ten digits. The path is reachable from any attribute value or text node through StrPair::GetStr (:322-344), which calls GetCharacterRef for every `&#` entity when entity processing is on (the default), so a document alone can terminate a host that parses untrusted XML -- a DoS in CWE-617 terms, and in non-assertion builds merely a wrapped accumulation that ConvertUTF32ToUTF8 rejects as length 0 (:440-443) or mis-decodes. The 10.1.0 fix 494735de ("fix the potential overflow in char refs", 2024-12-05, merged as 4cbb2515 "Merge pull request #1009") switches the arithmetic to `uint32_t`, defines `MAX_CODE_POINT = 0x10FFFF` and returns 0 as soon as `ucs > MAX_CODE_POINT`, deleting the overflow assertions and adding those inputs (`&#xffffffff;`, `&#5000000000;`, long zero-padded forms) to xmltest.cpp. Frozen 10.0.0 still contains the assertions and no MAX_CODE_POINT; the maintainer confirmed "Should be fixed" on issue #996 on 2026-05-24.

The candidate carries CVE-2024-50614 for the same snapshot and the same advisory range (OSV: introduced 0, last_affected 321ea883 = tag 10.0.0). That is the defect promoted from disc2_c259dbfa630800a8b2a454ac: XMLUtil::GetCharacterRef assertion overflow in tinyxml2.cpp, fixed by 494735de in 10.1.0. No second root cause, so this row is an alias cluster.
notes: second candidate for CVE-2024-50614 at the same snapshot; duplicate of the promoted row.

basis: Connection reuse is decided by ConnectionExists (lib/url.c:1055-1491). It first looks up the conncache bundle, whose key is built by hashkey (lib/conncache.c:125-148) as `scope_id/port/hostname` (or `port/hostname`), so it carries no scheme and no URL path; the per-connection filter then compares TLS flags (:1190-1196), proxy settings (:1198-1241), connect-to bits (:1208-1216), local bind (:1269-1286), credentials (:1288-1298) and further transport properties, but never the SMB share. The share is per-URL: smb_setup_connection (:428-440) calls smb_parse_url_path (:1161-1190), which copies the first path component into `smbc->share` (:1176), and the tree connect thereafter names that share (smb_send_tree_connect, :686-698, invoked from smb_request_state :961). SMB marks the connection as reusable (`connkeep(conn, "SMB default")`, :461), so two requests to smb://host/shareA/... and smb://host/shareB/... with the same credentials are matched by ConnectionExists. When the match is taken, reuse_conn (lib/url.c:3286-3355) copies the new credentials/host into the existing connection and then frees the temporary connection (:3354), which discards the smbc parsed for the new URL; the transfer keeps `existing->proto.smbc.share`, so the new request tree-connects to the previous share. The result is a read of a file from the wrong share or a write into the wrong share on the same server with the same credentials (CWE-488). The fix 74a169575d ("protocol: disable connection reuse for SMB(S)", 2026-04-07) removes PROTOPT_CONN_REUSE from the SMB and SMBS rows of the scheme table in lib/protocol.c, i.e. it disables reuse outright instead of matching the share; that table and flag do not exist at 8.3.0 (both handlers there already carry PROTOPT_NONE, lib/smb.c:275 and :303), so the fix has no pre-image in the frozen tree and the anchor is a direct source review of the reuse path.

myssh_is_known (lib/vssh/libssh.c:334-561) asks libssh for the known_hosts entry (ssh_session_get_known_hosts_entry, :401) and maps the result to a CURLKHMATCH value in the switch at :442-458. At 8.3.0 `case SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER:` has only a `/* fallthrough */ comment (:446-447) and shares the body of SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_NOT_FOUND / UNKNOWN / ERROR, which sets `keymatch = CURLKHMATCH_MISSING;` (:453); only the `default:` arm assigns CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH (:455-457). SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER is what libssh returns when the host is known but its key type differs from the recorded one, so a host whose key was replaced with another key type is reported to the CURLOPT_SSH_KEYFUNCTION callback as an unknown host rather than as a mismatch (:513-517). A trust-on-first-use callback that accepts CURLKHMATCH_MISSING (typically returning CURLKHSTAT_FINE or FINE_ADD_TO_FILE, :520-531) then accepts the untrusted server, defeating SSH host verification for SCP/SFTP transfers over the libssh backend (CWE-297). Without a callback the MISSING verdict is still rejected (:537-541), so the defect needs the callback, matching the advisory. The 8.21.0 fix 0b8dbbc63 ("libssh: map SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_OTHER to CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH", 2026-05-25) adds `keymatch = CURLKHMATCH_MISMATCH; break;` to that case, so the callback sees the mismatch and the documented callback logic rejects it. The fix marker is absent from the frozen file, where the only MISMATCH assignment is the default arm.

reverse_proxy records the upstream it selected in the request's variable map: proxyLoopIteration calls `caddyhttp.SetVar(r.Context(), dialInfoVarKey, dialInfo)` (modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/reverseproxy.go:663-666), with `dialInfoVarKey = "reverse_proxy.dial_info"` (hosts.go:332-334). The transport's dial closure then recovers the target through `GetDialInfo(ctx)` (hosts.go:299-302), which reads the same map with `caddyhttp.GetVar(ctx, dialInfoVarKey)`, and overwrites network/address with it before `dialer.DialContext` (httptransport.go:275-293). The variable map is shared request state, and a new connection is dialled lazily when the transport needs one, so in a handler chain that runs `forward_auth` and then `reverse_proxy` the auth handler's SetVar can land between the proxy's RoundTrip and its dial: the proxy transport then dials the auth upstream, and the resulting pooled connection is used for proxy requests, which arrive at the wrong backend (observed as spurious 404s) and can make a `forward_auth` check pass against an endpoint that returns 200. The 2.11.5 fix 1830809afe8c ("reverseproxy: save dial info in a context key instead of a variable key to avoid race conditions when forward_auth is used", #7859) deletes the SetVar call and instead attaches the DialInfo to an immutable private context key right before the roundtrip (`ctx := context.WithValue(req.Context(), dialInfoCtxKey, di)`, reverseproxy.go:1032-1042), and GetDialInfo reads `ctx.Value(dialInfoCtxKey)`; the mutable-var pre-image present at v2.11.4 is exactly what the fix removes.

baseUnset (lodash.js:4371-4414) validates path segments in a loop that skips every non-string key: `var key = path[index]; if (typeof key !== 'string') { continue; }` (:4385-4390). castPath returns an array path unchanged (:4556-4561 `if (isArray(value)) return value;`), so a segment can itself be an array and is skipped by that guard; the terminal deletion then resolves the parent through parent()->baseGet (:6678-6680, :3070-3080), which stringifies each segment with toKey (:6856-6862, `var result = (value + '');`), and deletes `obj[toKey(last(path))]` (:4412-4413). A call such as `_.unset({}, [['constructor'], ['prototype'], 'toString'])` therefore passes the guard untouched, walks to Object.prototype via `constructor`/`prototype`, and deletes a built-in prototype member; the same array wrapping bypasses the `constructor`/`prototype` pair check at :4398-4409 and the primitive-root exception it allows. The pre-existing CVE-2025-13465 guard (GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg, shipped in 4.17.23) is string-only, which is exactly the gap; the array-wrapped form reaches Object.prototype, Number.prototype and String.prototype and deletes properties (no overwrite of behaviour). The 4.18.1 fix fe8d32ed ("fix: block prototype pollution in baseUnset via constructor/prototype traversal") normalizes every segment with `var key = toKey(path[index]);` and rejects constructor/prototype as non-terminal traversal keys unconditionally, dropping the string-only skip and the primitive-root exception.

GHSA-pj86-cfqh-vqx6 / CVE-2024-51999 was withdrawn on 2025-12-02: the advisory text now reads "This advisory has been withdrawn because it describes a correctness bug, not a vulnerability with real security impact." The described behaviour does exist at the frozen 4.19.2: lib/utils.js:288-292 (parseExtendedQueryString) calls `qs.parse(str, { allowPrototypes: true })`, so a key such as `hasOwnProperty` becomes an own property of the request-scoped `req.query` object, and the 4.x security patch 2f64f68c37c6 (`allowPrototypes` -> `plainObjects`) was reverted on master by 697547cde621 the same day the advisory was withdrawn. That shadowing affects only the requester's own request object and was never demonstrated to cross a trust boundary; the maintainers withdrew it as a correctness issue, so no vulnerability exists for this snapshot.
notes: withdrawn 2025-12-02 as a correctness bug; frozen 4.19.2 allowPrototypes:true only shadows keys on the requester's own req.query; patch reverted upstream (697547cd).

basis: GHSA-9822-6m93-xqf4 lists the affected actionpack/rails rows as `>= 7.0.0, < 7.0.8.1` and `>= 7.1.0, < 7.1.3.1`; those are the two series that existed at disclosure (2024-02-27), and the frozen RAILS_VERSION is 8.0.4, outside both. The discovery flag came from a truncated `>= 7.0.0` range read, not from a published row. Static check: the fix 857f2e4a6a6c ("fix XSS vulnerability when using translation", 2024-01-05) is an ancestor of tag v8.0.4 (compare v8.0.4...857f2e4a: ahead_by 0, behind_by 3070) and the frozen actionpack/lib/abstract_controller/translation.rb:26-30 escapes string defaults with `ERB::Util.html_escape(value)` when the key is an html-safe translation key, so the pre-fix shape (default passed through unescaped to ActiveSupport::HtmlSafeTranslation) is gone.
notes: published rows end at 7.0.8.1 / 7.1.3.1; frozen 8.0.4 outside; fix hunk present in actionpack translate.

basis: The unbounded `strategy.matrix` expansion that CVE-2026-96580 / GHSA-p3rv-cr5f-9gjh describes is performed by the workflow parser, which is not in this repository at v1.25.5: go.mod:94 requires github.com/nektos/act v0.2.63 and go.mod:301 replaces it with gitea.com/gitea/act v0.261.7-0.20251003180512-ac6e4b751763, there is no vendor/ directory, and no MaxJobNumPerRun symbol exists in the tree. Every expansion goes through `jobparser.Parse` in the pinned module (e.g. services/actions/notifier_helper.go:362, services/actions/schedule_tasks.go:143, services/actions/workflow.go:157); the cap that the advisory fixes ships only when 28.0.0 moves the parser in-tree. The same dependency-only situation as next.js http-proxy (the fix adds a patched npm package and touched no Next-authored source) and the Jenkins support-log-formatter row, so the candidate resolves as out_of_scope: no repository source location can carry the defect, and the row cannot be promoted with a source anchor.
notes: defective expansion code is in the pinned gitea.com/gitea/act module (go.mod:301), no vendor dir, no MaxJobNumPerRun in tree; in-tree call site notifier_helper.go:362 only forwards to it.

basis: Source review of the frozen 9.0.98 valve (java/org/apache/catalina/valves/rewrite/RewriteValve.java) shows the defect carrier does not exist in this tree. At 9.0.98 RewriteValve.invoke takes `urlDecoded` from request.getDecodedRequestURIMB():306, rewrites in decoded space, and when a rule matched builds the encoded requestURI with `URLEncoder.DEFAULT.encode(urlStringDecoded, uriCharset)` (:492), then normalizes the decoded string with `urlStringDecoded = RequestUtil.normalize(urlStringDecoded)` (:495) and appends it to decodedURI (:502). The file contains no java.net.URLDecoder call and no decode step after normalization, so an encoded traversal introduced by a rewrite substitution cannot survive into decodedURI. The normalize-before-decode arrangement the advisory describes first appears in 9.0.103, together with the bug-60013 rewrite ee3ab548e923 ("Better handling of URLs with literal ';' and '?'", 2025-03-13): 9.0.103 imports java.net.URLDecoder (:24), runs RequestUtil.normalize on the encoded rewrite result (:548) and only then URLDecoder.decode(...) into decodedURI (:555); 9.0.108 has the same shape at :558/:565, and the fix b5042622b8b7 reverses the order in 9.0.109 (`String urlStringRewriteDecoded = URLDecoder.decode(...)` :559, `urlStringRewriteDecoded = RequestUtil.normalize(...)` :560). The frozen 9.0.98 predates that regression: 9.0.98 and 9.0.102 both show the single normalize call at :495 and no URLDecoder, and the vendor's own text attributes the defect to "the fix for bug 60013". The published range "Affects: 9.0.0.M11 to 9.0.108" is a conservative RewriteValve-era range; the static counter-evidence is the decode-then-normalize flow, and the same reasoning already closed CVE-2026-59083. No in-range anchor exists at the frozen SHA, so no promotion.
notes: closed: 9.0.98 normalizes the decoded rewrite output (:495) and has no URLDecoder; the vulnerable encoded-space flow starts at 9.0.103 and is fixed in 9.0.109. Vendor range is over-broad relative to its own regression statement.

basis: At the frozen v5.0.11 the deny matcher is built as `picomatch(config.server.fs.deny, { matchBase: true })` (packages/vite/src/node/server/index.ts:620) over the default patterns `['.env', '.env.*', '*.{crt,pem}']` (index.ts:933); picomatch ^2.3.1 is pinned in packages/vite/package.json:127 and its matchBase implementation is `regex.test(path.basename(input))` (picomatch 2.3.1 lib/picomatch.js:161-163). A request target `/.env\` is parsed by new URL() with the backslash normalized to "/", fsPathFromUrl/normalizePath keeps the trailing slash, and path.basename(".../.env/") is still ".env", so the deny matcher returns true at static.ts:216 and ensureServingAccess refuses the request (403) before sirv reads anything. Verified with picomatch 2.3.1 directly: {matchBase:true} + ".env" matches "/root/.env/" while the 5.2.6-style regex "**/.env" with matchBase:false does not. That is why the vendor row starts at 5.2.6: 5.2.5 still uses `{ matchBase: true, nocase: true }`, and 5.2.6 replaces the construction with `config.server.fs.deny.map(p => p.includes("/") ? p : `**/${p}`)` plus `{ matchBase: false, nocase: true, dot: true }` (index.ts:688-698), which loses the trailing-slash match. The OSV record collapses the vendor rows into introduced 2.9.18 / fixed 5.4.21, and that union is what flagged this snapshot; the per-row vendor ranges exclude 5.0.0-5.2.5 for the matcher reason above, and v5.0.11 lies in that gap. No vendor statement contradicts the mechanism, so the row closes as confirmed_not_affected.
notes: closed: 5.0.11 uses picomatch matchBase:true, which matches path.basename("/root/.env/") = ".env"; the bypass needs the 5.2.6+ `**/` + matchBase:false matcher, so the vendor row starting at 5.2.6 is a code difference, not a support-policy gap.

basis: Server Action POSTs whose body is multipart/form-data reach handleAction, which passes the request FormData to `decodeAction(formData, serverModuleMap)` (packages/next/src/server/app-render/action-handler.ts:574) from the vendored `react-server-dom-webpack-builtin` build. At the frozen v14.2.24 that bundle is 18.3.0-canary-178c267a4e-20241218 (packages/next/src/compiled/react-server-dom-webpack/package.json:50-51). Its `decodeAction` (react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.development.js:3620-3656) iterates every form field and, for every key that starts with `$ACTION_REF_`, calls `decodeBoundActionMetaData(body, serverManifest, formFieldPrefix)` (:3603-3618) with no record of which prefixes have already been decoded: the 19.0.4 hardening adds exactly that (`const seenActions = new Set<string>()` with an early return), and the frozen build has neither the set nor the `MAX_BOUND_ARGS` cap in `bindArgs` (:3577-3579). Each call builds a fresh response over the whole request body, closes it and forces initialization, and `parseModelString` case 'K' (:3412-3429) walks `response._formData` in full to rebuild each FormData reference, so one decode costs O(number of form fields) and N repeated `$ACTION_REF_` keys cost O(N^2) JSON parses and form scans while the request is parsed. The attacker controls both the field count and the repeated key, so a single request can occupy the server with excessive CPU (CWE-770, "allocation of resources without limits or throttling"), matching the advisory's "excessive CPU usage, out-of-memory exceptions, or server crashes" impact. The production bundle carries the same logic (`$ACTION_REF_` handling at react-server-dom-webpack-server.node.production.js:3223, no seenActions/MAX_BOUND_ARGS/arraySizeLimit anywhere in the file). The 14.2 line has no patch: the Next advisory (GHSA-h25m-26qc-wcjf, published 2026-01-26) lists 15.0.8 and later as fixed and its vulnerable range `>=13.0.0 <15.0.8` contains v14.2.24. The fix that ships in 15.0.8 is 99b450109dfd "Sync DoS mitigations for React Flight", which re-pins react and react-dom to 19.0.0-rc-4cd8f914-20260126; upstream the hardening is React 19.0.4 commit de58cca00cf0, released as 19.0.4/19.1.5/19.2.4.

The HTTP/1.1 request parser records `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding` independently and never treats their combination as an error. In `Request::decode` (actix-http/src/h1/decoder.rs:231-315) the header block is handed to `set_headers` at :276; `set_headers` (:75-213) stores `content_length` for every Content-Length (:106-127) and sets `chunked` for `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (:135-150), then resolves the payload length by testing `chunked` first (`if chunked { PayloadDecoder::chunked() }` at :198-202) and only afterwards `content_length` (:205-209). Nothing compares the two flags, so a request that carries both is accepted and decoded as chunked, exactly the ambiguity RFC 9112 section 6.3 requires a recipient to reject. The frozen tree documents this as intended behaviour in its own test: `hrs_cl_and_te_http10` (:1118-1134) comments "in HTTP/1.0 transfer encoding is simply ignored so it's fine to have both" and expects the request to parse. With a front-end intermediary that frames on Content-Length while forwarding the conflicting Transfer-Encoding, the backend consumes only up to the terminating chunk, and the bytes the intermediary still attributes to the first request are parsed as a second request on the reused connection: classic CL.TE smuggling (CWE-444), reachable by any unauthenticated network client. The fix 3c056bd361 (released in http-v3.12.1) inserts the missing cross-check into `Request::decode` immediately after the `set_headers` call: it rejects Transfer-Encoding on HTTP/1.0, rejects a Transfer-Encoding that is not chunked (including `identity`), and rejects any request that carries Content-Length while Transfer-Encoding is present; it also flips the `hrs_cl_and_te_http10` expectation and adds `hrs_cl_and_chunked_te_http11`, `hrs_identity_te_http11` and a codec-level test.
